The native executable must advertise ancestral_pedigree support before preparation. The ancestral reduction admits ordinary and supplied-metafounder pedigrees. Metafounder models additionally require the native ancestral_metafounders capability; every correlated base remains in the factor, with all original coefficients reconstructed. Existing thread controls apply to the native phases, but dependency-ordered pedigree sweeps can contain serial work.
For supplied-covariance pedigree-blended ssSNPBLUP prediction, an optional preconditioner control avoids exact extraction of the marginal pedigree precision diagonal:
execution:
  preconditioner_diagonal:
    method: stochastic
    probes: 256
    seed: 4401
    batch_width: 32
Merge this mapping into the existing execution block. Omission, or preconditioner_diagonal: {method: exact}, retains exact extraction. The stochastic method uses seeded Rademacher probes and clips estimates to the positive bound 1/A_ii before applying the polygenic precision scale. It changes the fixed PCG preconditioner only: genomic/pedigree operators, covariances, solver tolerances and original-equation residual acceptance remain unchanged. Reported probes, batches, seed, clipped entries and workspace distinguish this work from exact-diagonal solves. The default probe count is an initial control, not an accuracy or speed guarantee. This control currently excludes REML, uncertainty and independent-ridge models. A rebuilt native driver with the corresponding capability is required; older binaries are rejected. The estimator follows Bekas, Kokiopoulou and Saad, An estimator for the diagonal of a matrix. Focused Windows/PARDISO validation on the six-animal four-trait adjusted-blend fixture compared exact setup with 64 and 256 probes. All 24 genetic predictions agreed within 3.6e-11 absolute difference, and the original residual threshold was identical. Exact setup used 31 PCG iterations and these stochastic runs used 32. A one-probe run exceeded the original residual threshold and was rejected; no tolerance was relaxed. Batch-width reproducibility and native portable-factor diagonal checks were also tested. Linux/HPC speed and the million-animal probe/iteration trade-off remain unqualified. The single-step toy example explicitly uses a tighter 1e-12 PCG tolerance to pass both transformed and original-equation checks. Omitted applicable thread counts are 1; inapplicable options and unsupported route combinations are errors. REML convergence is separate from linear convergence. There is no fixed application RAM ceiling or timeout. Optional future budgets must distinguish factor/workspace allowances from process RSS.
output.directory must be fresh. Default tables are fixed_effects, random_effects and diagnostics; an explicit tables list may select them. Named output.predictions requests specify contributing effects. levels: all reports existing level values for intercept-only effects. Curve requests name a table input through data, with an explicit unique ID and the grouping/basis bindings required by the requested effects. Traits default to all. Prediction inputs do not need response columns. Requests report only the named effects, without adding fixed effects or clipping time. New effect levels and unsupported reporting requests fail before fitting. For one selected effect, optional channels: [direct] restricts the sum to named channels in that effect. Channel names must be unique and present; the default trait set is then inferred from those channels. Explicit trait requests must be represented by the selected channels. For example:
output:
  directory: results/direct-maternal
  predictions:
    direct_values: {effects: [genetic], channels: [direct], levels: individuals}
    maternal_values: {effects: [genetic], channels: [maternal], levels: individuals}
    record_contributions: {effects: [genetic], data: observations}
Level predictions evaluate the selected coefficients at the same named level; they do not substitute that individual’s parent. Data predictions instead use each selected channel’s grouping column, so the final request reports direct[individual] + maternal[mother]. Omitting channels sums all applicable channels. A selected maternal-only prediction table needs the mother binding, but does not need an unused direct-individual column. Basis channels require data predictions; selecting only intercept channels permits level predictions. Separate channel selection currently requires exactly one effect per request; multi-effect data predictions can still sum the full requested effects. Selected ordinary packed genetic values can additionally request uncertainty:
output:
  directory: results/my-fit
  predictions:
    genetic_values: {effects: [genetic], levels: individuals}
  uncertainty:
    method: exact
    effect: genetic
    individuals: ["004", "001"]
    traits: [trait1, trait2]
    maximum_targets: 4
This writes genetic_uncertainty.csv, ordered by the requested individuals and traits. Columns are individual, trait, prediction, prior_variance, pev, prediction_error_standard_error, reliability, method, prior_mcse, pev_mcse, reliability_mcse and qualified. Exact extraction has zero MCSE. PEV includes uncertainty from jointly estimated fixed and other random effects; the standard error is sqrt(PEV). Reliability is 1 - PEV / (Hii * Ktt) for the supplied effective genomic/pedigree covariance and trait variance. It is conditional on the supplied covariance parameters, not uncertainty in estimated variance components or a claim of empirical calibration.
method: exact extracts selected diagonal entries within the numerical solve tolerances. It performs one PCG inverse query per individual/trait pair, reusing the fitted conditional operator, preconditioner and pedigree factor. Both transformed and original augmented residual gates must pass for every target. No dense inverse or stochastic fallback is used. maximum_targets is a required positive solve-work cap, not a RAM ceiling; the request fails before preparation if its number of individual/trait pairs exceeds that cap. All IDs must be unique quoted strings present in the pedigree. Trait order is preserved and defaults to the genetic effect’s declared channels.
Prior variances reuse native exact genomic diagonal preparation and bounded H unit-column extraction. Non-genotyped targets require additional inner PCG work for their prior Hii; these solves and iterations are reported separately. This stage can be expensive for many targets even when the prediction fit is fast. Native uncertainty stage time, target-solve iterations and both maximum residual-to-threshold ratios appear in diagnostics. Estimates are not clipped; failed solves or invalid PEV/reliability bounds fail the requested evaluation.
The initial YAML scope is ordinary-pedigree packed ss_snp PCG with an intercept-only genetic effect with one channel per genetic trait, either pedigree-factor route and either preconditioner, including supplied ridge or pedigree-blended genomic covariance. Metafounders, genetic groups, genetic regression trajectories, compiled-MME uncertainty and arbitrary contrasts are rejected. The native executable must advertise packed_uncertainty_exact before result creation. See the complete example (models/multitrait-single-step-uncertainty.yml).
For a large target set, the alternative is an explicit stochastic request:
output:
  directory: results/genotyped-uncertainty
  uncertainty:
    method: stochastic
    effect: genetic
    individuals: genotyped
    traits: [trait1, trait2]
    probes: 32
    deflation_rank: 16
    seed: 4401
    maximum_solves: 48
    maximum_reliability_mcse: 0.02
    prior: {method: exact, maximum_individuals: 0}
The native estimator uses a fixed NystrÃ¶m sketch followed by independent Rademacher residual probes. deflation_rank + probes posterior PCG queries must fit maximum_solves; each query reuses fitted factors and passes both equation checks. Rank zero selects plain diagonal probing. At least two residual probes are required, rank is at most the target dimension and 2048, and all seeds are explicit unsigned 64-bit integers. There is no automatic probe increase or exact fallback. These are work budgets, not memory ceilings.
individuals accepts explicit quoted IDs, genotyped (mapped FAM order), or all (pedigree order). Trait order is retained. For genotype-only requests, Hii is exact and requires no unit-column query. The exact prior option’s maximum_individuals caps additional non-genotyped prior diagonals. To probe non-genotyped prior Hii instead, specify:
    prior:
      method: stochastic
      probes: 32
      deflation_rank: 8
      seed: 4402
      maximum_relative_mcse: 0.01
Prior sketch/probe counts bound H applications separately from the posterior maximum_solves; H applications perform inner pedigree PCG work, whose solves and iterations are reported. Genotyped diagonals remain exact. Prior and posterior seeds must differ and cannot differ by the sketch-stream constant 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15. This prevents reuse of either random stream.
PEV MCSE is estimated from residual probes conditional on the sketch. Reliability MCSE uses a first-order delta approximation combining independent PEV and prior MCSE. Neither is a confidence-interval or calibration guarantee; PCG error, covariance-parameter estimation and model misspecification are outside MCSE. Nonpositive/nonfinite prior estimates fail uncertainty. Finite PEV outside [0,prior] remains an unqualified candidate, without clipping; negative PEV has a blank prediction-error standard error.
A row is qualified only when PEV/reliability satisfy their bounds, reliability MCSE meets maximum_reliability_mcse and prior relative MCSE meets its target. run.json retains prediction accepted separately from uncertainty_accepted and uncertainty_status (passed, unqualified or failed). Numerical stochastic failure preserves validated predictions but publishes no uncertainty CSV. Precision/bounds failure retains the candidate CSV and per-row flags. The driver must advertise packed_uncertainty_stochastic. This mode has the same ordinary-pedigree/intercept-only scope as exact extraction. See the complete example (models/multitrait-single-step-stochastic-uncertainty.yml).
Stochastic requests can set estimator: information instead of the default estimator: pev. This probes the explained covariance I = reported_prior - reported_posterior, reusing the same PCG queries, sketch/probe budget and residual checks. It reconstructs PEV = prior - diag(I) and reliability = diag(I)/prior. This can reduce stochastic error for weakly informed targets; the benefit depends on the covariance structure. For genotyped-only targets the additional prior actions apply G and the trait covariance directly, with no pedigree solves or dense G storage. Mixed targets use H actions and incur separately reported inner pedigree solves. These prior actions are additional to maximum_solves, which caps posterior queries. The driver must advertise packed_uncertainty_information.
The CSV includes estimator and information_mcse (zero in PEV/exact mode). For information probing, pev_mcse = hypot(prior_mcse, information_mcse) and reliability_mcse = hypot(information_mcse/prior, reliability*prior_mcse/prior). The latter accounts for the shared estimated prior in reconstructed PEV and its denominator. Prior-diagonal probes use an independent seed. Scope, qualification thresholds and the no-clipping policy remain the same. See the complete information example (models/multitrait-single-step-information-uncertainty.yml).
For stochastic estimator: pev, optional probing: trait masks residual probes to each requested trait in turn; unstructured remains the default. The NystrÃ¶m sketch is unchanged. probes counts all masked posterior queries, so it must be divisible by the number of requested traits and supply at least two complete groups. At four traits, deflation_rank: 4, probes: 28 and maximum_solves: 32 use four sketch queries plus seven independent groups of four masked queries. MCSE uses seven samples per target, not 28. Ordinary probing with the same controls uses 28 samples per target. Removing cross-trait noise can compensate for this smaller sample count, depending on the model. Diagnostics label the structure and report independent groups and color count. The native executable must advertise packed_uncertainty_trait_probing. This choice is not available for exact extraction or information probing.
The describe operation prints the expanded effects and channels, covariance order, fixed terms, level/record counts and route decisions before factorization. For the curve example it shows 6 genetic channels, 6 individual environmental channels and 2 site-visit channels, with a 2-by-2 residual matrix. Generating that metadata must not materialize a population-sized incidence matrix. Primary scientific coefficients and marker/pedigree-auxiliary solver coordinates are counted separately in native diagnostics after fitting.
Diagnostics retain the resolved model/defaults, identities, named results, phase timings, process RSS, and prediction/original-equation residual checks. run.json is always retained as the execution audit. Selected tables produce fixed_effects.csv (trait,term,estimate), random_effects.csv (effect,level,channel,trait,estimate) and diagnostics.json. Each named prediction writes <name>.csv, with level,trait,prediction for level requests or record_id,trait,prediction for a prediction grid. Grid IDs are retained verbatim. Native phase RSS covers the native process; it does not include Python preparation. End-to-end Python preparation memory is not yet profiled.

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
Ordinary pedigree and joint random-regression models lower through greml’s public compiled-MME facade; single-step models reuse its packed conditional PCG driver. No new numerical solver or R selector is introduced. The focused checks in tools/validation/test_hpc_model_yaml.py cover independent dense equations, missing traits, reordered pedigree IDs, covariance labels, curve predictions, checksums and CLI execution. These checks do not establish performance at industrial scale or full-package qualification.
The frontend spools CSV/TSV input tables, normalized observations, long-input grouping, residual assignments and record prediction grids to a disposable SQLite snapshot. By default this uses the operating system temporary directory (TMPDIR on Linux); optional execution.preparation.directory selects an existing directory, with relative paths resolved beside the YAML file:
execution:
  # Other required execution settings remain here.
  preparation:
    directory: /scratch/myproject
Each CLI invocation owns a fresh temporary child directory and removes it on normal completion or handled failure; an externally killed process may leave that child behind. The parent directory and source files are preserved. Disk use grows with input rows, and preparation makes multiple sequential passes over the snapshot. No application RAM or disk ceiling is imposed. Pedigree and effect-level IDs/indexes, PLINK sample/marker metadata, supplied dense relationships and covariance matrices remain in memory. Rank checking uses a fixed-term Gram matrix, quadratic in fixed coefficients per trait. Prepared record prediction targets live in checksum-protected prediction_*.jsonl files rather than an embedded population-sized JSON array; reporting reads these files one row at a time. The frontend writes sparse record references, without materializing a population-sized incidence matrix. The native text adapter has a maximum of 256 responses per record, 65,536 incidence entries per record and 64 genetic channels on the packed marker route; these are adapter shape restrictions, not RAM ceilings. Packed ssSNPBLUP requires one H effect, declared first, with identity relationships for the other effects. Ordinary compiled models and supplied-genomic ssGBLUP can reuse one pedigree input across multiple random effects. Supplied-genomic ssGBLUP currently allows one H effect; genomic and pedigree references must be explicit and valid. The current compiled-MME facade requires at least one fixed coefficient across the model; an entirely empty fixed design is rejected before preparation. The packed marker route supports an empty fixed design. Covariance matrices must be positive definite. New prediction levels, unsupported genomic combinations, unsupported REML structures and uncertainty outside the ordinary packed genetic scope above are rejected rather than inferred. YAML duplicate keys, anchors, aliases, custom tags and unknown keys are rejected. The draft schema has runtime validation; a separate formal machine-readable schema has not been published.

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
Observation precision is separate from genetic incidence weighting. For independent residual occasions, use one precision column for every trait or a single column shared by traits:
model:
  residual:
    type: independent
    covariance: residual
    precision_weights: {trait1: weight1, trait2: weight2}
    measurement_error: {covariance: sampling, scale: sampling_scale}
All referenced columns are bound in the observation input. Weights must be finite and strictly positive for observed responses; missing responses use the existing missingness declaration rather than zero weights. Omitted weights are one. sampling_scale is an optional nonnegative column; its default is one. The named sampling matrix is a supplied natural covariance in the residual coordinate order, and may be positive semidefinite. It must be distinct from estimated covariance blocks. The observed covariance is D^(-1/2) R(theta) D^(-1/2) + scale * sampling, with diagonal D containing relative precision weights. The known term is added after residual weighting. Responses and genetic incidence are not rescaled.
The same optional modifiers apply to grouped and supplied trait-by-visit residual blocks. Known covariance must be constant within a declared block; missing coordinates select the joint covariance’s observed submatrix before inversion. Blocks do not imply covariance between otherwise independent units. Solving supports compiled and ordinary packed prediction; estimation of the weighted residual covariance uses compiled REML. Known measurement error stays fixed and is excluded from the default estimated blocks. Packed REML rejects these modifiers until its corresponding update machinery is available. See the complete example (models/multitrait-observation-precision.yml).

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
For one response, declare trial-specific row-by-column AR1 residuals with an independent nugget. The covariance entries are structured parameter blocks:
covariances:
  trial_A:
    type: spatial_ar1
    variance: 1.2
    nugget: 0.3
    row_correlation: 0.45
    column_correlation: 0.30
model:
  residual:
    type: spatial_ar1
    group: trial
    row: plot_row
    column: plot_column
    covariances: {A: trial_A}
Bind trial, plot_row and plot_column in the observation input. Coordinates must be integers; their actual gaps determine correlation. Each trial is an independent spatial block by default. An optional block column identifies independent fields within each trial that share the trial’s covariance parameters. Duplicate coordinates within a block are rejected. The covariance between observed plots is variance * row_correlation^row_distance * column_correlation^column_distance, plus nugget on the diagonal. Absent plots are marginalized, not imputed. The trial map must match observed trials exactly.
Both variances are positive; correlations lie strictly between minus one and one. Compiled solving and REML use the same native covariance and analytic derivatives. REML coordinates are variance, nugget, row_correlation and column_correlation; omitted estimated blocks remain fixed. Parameters and starts are reported in parameters.csv. This initial family is univariate and uses exact dense covariance algebra within each observed spatial block, with quadratic block storage. It does not provide industrial spatial scalability or the packed formulation, and it does not expose zero-nugget boundary fitting. Observation-precision modifiers are not combined with this family yet. See the spatial example (models/spatial-field-trial.yml).

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
Features in this table do not imply that every cross-combination is supported. Invalid combinations are rejected before fitting. See the complete example catalog for runnable files rather than copying isolated fragments.









Route
Prediction
Covariance estimation
Likelihood




Compiled pedigree/identity/dense relationships
Direct or PCG; regression, correlated/weighted incidence, groups/metafounders, FA and serial/general residual blocks
Sparse-direct unstructured/FA/serial REML with named fixed coordinates; operator relationships excluded
Exact absolute restricted likelihood and line search


Compiled exact/APY ssGBLUP
PCG; supplied effective G/blocks or streamed raw PLINK APY; pedigree individuals retained
Not exposed for operator H relationships
Not an estimation route


Packed ssSNPBLUP
PCG; ancestral/full Qnn, reuse/shifted preconditioning, separate/weighted incidence, supplied FA/serial covariance, groups/metafounders
Ordinary pedigree, one genetic channel per trait, unstructured genetic/independent residual matrices; whole-block fixing; fixed additional identity-effect covariances
Optional exact or SLQ start-to-final change; zero global determinant work when omitted



Wide/long CSV/TSV observations lower to the same joint residual occasions. Sparse external natural covariance uses retained sparse factors; factor fill and exact diagonal work remain model-dependent. Raw-genotype APY uses explicit core IDs and tiled/file-backed products; industrial throughput is unqualified. Ancestral metafounder reduction retains every correlated base. Packed fixed/combined groups prepare O(individuals × groups) inheritance columns; ordinary random groups remain implicit. Packed Gamma pseudo-EM is conditional on an explicit absolute marker base, separate from joint covariance REML.
Selected exact/stochastic PEV is conditional on supplied covariances and has its own work/precision qualification, separate from prediction acceptance. General PEC/trajectory uncertainty, probabilistic pedigrees, general level-specific or structured marker covariance, scalar interval constraints, shared parameter tying and zero-variance boundary fitting are not exposed. Industrial REML precision/runtime, industrial APY preparation, new large-data combinations and complete package qualification remain separate work.

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
Compiled models use transport format 8 with the matching native driver. The declarations below use the same input/model/analysis/execution sections. Existing R interfaces and PEV qualification limits are unchanged. Complete examples include small CSV/PLINK inputs; small reference checks do not establish industrial performance.


Random-intercept REML example (models/reml-random-intercept.yml):
covariances:
  genetic:
    - [2.0]
  residual:
    - [2.0]
analysis:
  task: reml
  estimate: [genetic, residual]
  optimizer:
    maximum_iterations: 100
    maximum_line_search_reductions: 24
    maximum_step: 1.0
    score_tolerance: 1.0e-7
execution:
  solver: sparse_direct
  sparse_backend: cholmod
  threads: {factor: 1}
The natural covariance matrices are starting values. estimate names the free whole covariance blocks; omitted blocks are held exactly at their supplied values. Omitting estimate estimates every referenced block. At least one must be free. Log-Cholesky coordinates enforce positive definite covariance, and line search accepts nondecreasing restricted likelihood. maximum_step bounds the transformed-coordinate step. Convergence requires stationarity of the free transformed scores, not small changes alone. A fixed block’s score need not be zero. Named optimizer coordinates may also be fixed, as detailed below. Unstructured covariance entries are not independently fixed by that control: it fixes the named Cholesky element. Zero-variance boundary fits, cross-component equality tying and user-defined scalar interval bounds are not exposed.
REML supports ordinary/explicit-base compiled models, distinct covariance names for each component and sparse-direct solving, using PARDISO or CHOLMOD. FA loadings/specifics and scalar or multivariate AR1/exponential parameters are estimated through native derivatives. Operator relationship REML is not exposed by this compiled adapter. Packed EM-REML is a separate route below. Exact derivative work can be substantial; this is a moderate-problem REML route, not an industrial marker REML claim.
variance_components.csv labels starting and fitted covariance entries and fixed/free status. reml_history.csv retains likelihood/score/step diagnostics. convergence.json reports convergence and covariance/BLUP availability. Its structured likelihood block (also written as likelihood.json) reports absolute likelihood for compiled REML and optional start-to-final likelihood change for packed REML, with separate status/precision diagnostics. Nonconverged fits return failure and retain their diagnostics; they do not publish qualified predictions. Linear residual checks still apply at the accepted final covariance.



The fast packed route uses the same covariance starts and estimate names, with independent covariance-fit and likelihood work controls:
analysis:
  task: reml
  estimate: [genetic, residual]
  optimizer: {maximum_iterations: 200, score_tolerance: 1.0e-6, step_fraction: 1.0}
  traces:
    method: stochastic
    probes: 64
    seed: 4401
    maximum_solves: 10000
    maximum_score_mcse: 0.001
  likelihood:
    method: slq
    maximum_operator_products: 6144
step_fraction is the EM interpolation fraction in (0,1]; the compiled optimizer’s maximum_step is inapplicable. Whole blocks can be fixed; packed coordinate constraints are not yet supported. Exact trace references use traces: {method: exact, maximum_solves: 10000}. These budgets are examples, not production precision recommendations. The ordinary-pedigree/unstructured scope, score/MCSE gates, independent final bank and solve accounting are specified in packed REML.
Omit likelihood to do no global determinant work. method: exact requires maximum_dimension for bounded small matrix references. SLQ requires an operator-product cap and accepts probes, seed, lanczos_steps, check_steps, maximum_mcse and maximum_depth_change. It evaluates both start/final states at both depths, using paired samples. Likelihood outputs describe a change relative to the supplied start; they are not absolute likelihoods comparable across different models or starts. Sampling MCSE and depth sensitivity are separate; the latter is not an error bound. This optional diagnostic does not control the fit or reject qualified predictions if its precision targets fail. The complete exact (models/multitrait-packed-reml.yml) and SLQ (models/multitrait-packed-reml-slq.yml) examples include all files and controls.



Fixed groups (models/multitrait-fixed-genetic-groups.yml) use the group declaration family, with no random prior:
model:
  random:
    genetic: {group: individual, relationship: A, covariance: genetic}
    ancestral_means:
      type: genetic_groups
      mode: fixed
      group: individual
      pedigree: A
      assignments: group_assignments
      groups: [G1, G2]
      reference: G1
This adds inherited, unpenalized group contrasts to the fixed design for each selected trait. The reference group’s mean is zero. Full fixed-design rank is checked natively; a reference declaration does not guarantee identifiability in every dataset. Estimates appear in fixed_effects.csv; named predictions can sum genetic and ancestral_means as usual.
Explicit phantom group-parent codes (models/multitrait-phantom-groups.yml) can replace the separate assignment table:
inputs:
  pedigree:
    type: pedigree
    file: data/pedigree_phantom.csv
    columns: {individual: sample_id, parent1: parent_1, parent2: parent_2}
    phantom_groups: {PG1: G1, PG2: G2}
Each code designates a missing-parent group slot and is absorbed into the native inherited proportion design. It does not create an individual, a shared biological parent, or a latent phantom coefficient. Every unknown parent slot needs an explicit group, either through codes or an assignment table. If both describe a slot they must agree. Unlisted biological parent IDs still cause an error. A group-mean model must explicitly consume these codes.
Combined bases (models/multitrait-combined-base.yml) keep supplied metafounder covariance and fixed or independent random inherited group means separate: a has the metafounder pedigree covariance, while F is computed from the original ordinary pedigree and missing-parent assignments. Latent metafounders have no observed group-mean incidence. Group and genetic random coefficients are independent. No covariance/base conversion is inferred. The compiled adapter materializes ordinary pedigree group proportions once; the existing packed random-group route keeps its implicit inheritance sweeps. Fixed groups and combined bases currently use compiled pedigree or supplied ssGBLUP/APY models; their packed adapters are rejected explicitly.
Gamma estimation (models/multitrait-estimated-gamma.yml) uses the existing native pseudo-EM estimator during packed preparation:
relationships:
  A:
    type: pedigree
    input: pedigree
    metafounders:
      covariance: Gamma_start
      assignments: base_assignments
      estimation: {method: pseudo_em, maximum_iterations: 2000}
  H:
    type: single_step
    pedigree: A
    genotypes: genotypes
    genomic:
      adjustment: none
      scale: 1.0
      polygenic_weight: 0.0
      independent_ridge: 0.05
      centering: absolute_half
      normalization: markers_over_two
This explicitly selects allele-frequency one-half centering (dosage center one) and normalization M/2. Pseudo-EM uses the raw absolute-base marker covariance; the declared independent ridge/blend belongs to the subsequent evaluation model. The supplied Gamma is a start. Failed or nonconverged estimation blocks prediction. Prepared Gamma is fingerprinted and used to rebuild the prediction pedigree. metafounders.csv and run.json.gamma_estimation report the estimate, iterations and fixed-point residual. Pseudo-EM is not exact REML, does not certify biological calibration, and prediction is conditional on the estimate.



Complete example (models/multitrait-weighted-incidence.yml):
model:
  random:
    genetic:
      group: individual
      relationship: A
      covariance: genetic
      incidence:
        - {individual: individual, weight: 0.6}
        - {individual: contributor, weight: contribution}
individual names a mapped logical ID column. weight is a finite literal or a mapped numeric column. This yields 0.6*a[individual] + contribution*a[contributor]. Weights are not normalized; negative contrasts are allowed. Duplicate contributors are coalesced, zero contributions omitted, and a zero-weight contributor may have a missing ID. Explicit channel-level incidence overrides the effect-level mapping; group and incidence cannot both override the same channel. A channel-level group keeps the existing single-individual override. All nonzero contributor IDs must belong to the relationship domain. Compiled and packed genetic products use the existing sparse record design; packed preparation uses all records. Observation predictions use the same mixture, while level predictions remain per individual. Group-mean mixture mappings and weighted PEV requests are not exposed.



Complete example (models/multitrait-sparse-relationship.yml):
inputs:
  relationship_levels:
    type: table
    file: data/relationship_levels.csv
    columns: {individual: sample_id}
  relationship_covariance:
    type: sparse_covariance
    file: data/relationship_sparse.csv
    levels: relationship_levels
relationships:
  E: {type: sparse_covariance, input: relationship_covariance}
The CSV header is row,column,value; IDs use the declared levels-table order. Supply unique lower-triangle entries sorted by column index then row index, including every positive diagonal. Missing off-diagonal entries mean zero. The input is covariance, not precision. Symmetry follows the triangle contract; native sparse factorization certifies positive definiteness. The frontend streams entries to disk and native PCG retains a sparse covariance factor as its inverse-action operator. It does not form a dense covariance inverse. This supports extra compiled-model effects, not a new raw-genomic H route. Use threads.relationship and an explicit sparse backend.
Storage depends on factor fill, not only input nonzeros. Exact precision diagonals use selected inversion with CHOLMOD; the current PARDISO adapter uses bounded batches of unit solves. That fallback avoids quadratic storage but can be expensive for large relationships. Industrial setup time and arbitrary out-of-core relationship plugins remain unqualified.



Complete example (models/multitrait-nonseparable-residual.yml):
model:
  residual:
    type: supplied_blocks
    group: individual
    position: time
    covariance: residual
    coordinates:
      - {trait: trait1, position: 20}
      - {trait: trait2, position: 20}
      - {trait: trait1, position: 21}
      - {trait: trait2, position: 21}
The supplied SPD matrix spans these coordinates in exactly this order. It can have visit-specific trait covariance and any admissible serial cross-covariance. Each group receives one independent copy. Missing trait/visit observations use the observed marginal submatrix, with no imputation or conditioning on missing responses. Duplicate observed coordinates within a group are errors. Wide and long inputs are equivalent. Named covariance row/column labels, if used, are trait@position, with numeric positions formatted without unnecessary zeros. This compiled adapter is intended for moderate within-group coordinate grids; large dense grids and their parameterization storage can be costly. It does not add a parametric nonstationary serial kernel, packed residual-block route, or serial-parameter REML.



Local Windows validation on 2026-10-16 passed 19 focused Python reference and affected-route regression tests, the native compiled-MME optimizer check and all eight added complete YAML examples. Balanced univariate and multivariate REML recover analytic covariance estimates; whole fixed matrices remain unchanged. Other references assemble the observation design, covariance and mixed-model equations independently, including combined exact/APY H models, weighted packed products, missing nonseparable residual coordinates and both sparse backends. Nonconvergence, indefinite covariance and stale source inputs are rejected. Existing packed, direct/maternal, FA, serial and raw APY cases remain included. These checks do not constitute a new industrial benchmark, Linux qualification, broad package qualification or resumed PEV precision work.
The existing R wrapper was rebuilt against the extended native optimizer control structure, and canonical package runtime verification passed. A separate test-correlated-formula.R check has 29 passing and two failing expectations: it assumes a one-iteration nonconverged REML fit has successful status and score output. The committed native optimizer already reports iteration exhaustion as failure, and the unchanged R wrapper returns no score output for that failure. Those existing expectations and the R interface were left unchanged; the local R test suite is not claimed fully green.
The reviewed fixed-block REML path checks average-information curvature only on free transformed coordinates, including when the unrestricted covariance components would be confounded. The unrestricted model still rejects an unusable information matrix. The portable 50K validation recipe exports 14 complete YAMLs from the preserved fixture and checks seven equivalent model pairs, a bounded analytic REML reference and immutable input provenance. Full-fixture prediction and moderate-sized REML qualification remain separate.
The final review additionally passed all 12 extended model tests with only PARDISO selected, the two portable fixture-workflow tests (including deliberate output-tamper rejection), and the native optimizer regression check. Both starts on the actual fixture’s bounded REML submodel agree with its independent residual-variance reference, 1.9994769667549. The full 50K paired campaign is provided for GenomeDK execution; it has not been run locally as part of this bundle refresh. Existing PEV qualification limits remain in force.

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
Format 8 adds runnable FA REML (models/factor-analytic-reml.yml), multivariate serial REML (models/multivariate-serial-reml.yml), packed fixed groups (models/multitrait-packed-fixed-groups.yml), packed combined bases (models/multitrait-packed-combined-base.yml) and independent-pilot PEV (models/multitrait-single-step-pilot-uncertainty.yml) examples. These additions leave the R interfaces unchanged. Reprepare compiled inputs with the matching frontend and driver; frozen earlier bundles are unchanged.


analysis.estimate selects complete parameter blocks. For a serial residual, the block includes its covariance and its correlation/rate. For FA it contains the identified free loadings and positive specific variances. Omitted blocks stay fixed at their supplied natural starts. A selected block can additionally hold named optimizer coordinates at their starts:
analysis:
  task: reml
  estimate: [genetic, residual]
  constraints:
    genetic:
      fixed: ['loading[trait2,shared]', 'specific[trait1]']
    residual:
      fixed: [correlation]
  optimizer:
    maximum_iterations: 100
    maximum_step: 1.0
    score_tolerance: 1.0e-6
FA names use the declared channel and factor labels. Fixing a positive loading or specific variance fixes its log coordinate, hence the same natural value. An unstructured multivariate block names lower Cholesky entries in column order, such as cholesky[trait2,trait1]; diagonal entries are optimized on the log scale. This holds a Cholesky element, not a covariance matrix entry. Other covariance entries can change. A scalar covariance uses variance[trait1]. A scalar serial residual uses variance and correlation/rate; a multivariate serial block uses Cholesky names followed by correlation/rate. describe lists the exact names in analysis.parameter_coordinates. Unknown, duplicate, entirely fixed or inapplicable declarations are rejected. Arbitrary scalar interval bounds, cross-block equality tying and zero-specific/zero-variance boundary fitting are not exposed.
The optimizer applies the Jacobian, AI submatrix and stationarity test to the free coordinates. Fixed whole natural blocks are restored exactly. A fixed direction with a nonzero score does not prevent a valid free-submodel fit. parameters.csv separates natural coordinate names/values from optimizer coordinate names/fixed status. variance_components.csv reports matrix entries and their whole-block status. For FA REML, covariance_models.json distinguishes the starting model from fitted parameters and implied covariance.



For a scalar model, reference a named 1Ã—1 covariance in variance:
covariances:
  residual:
    - [1.0]
model:
  residual: {type: ar1, group: individual, position: time, variance: residual, correlation: 0.4}
For multivariate data, use covariance: residual with a natural trait covariance matrix. AR1 uses integer positions and a correlation strictly within (-1,1); exponential uses numeric positions and a strictly positive rate. Native REML rebuilds the exact observed trait-by-time covariance and its analytic derivatives at each trial. Missing traits/visits are marginalized by the observed submatrix. It does not freeze the prediction whitening transform while estimating parameters. Trait covariance and serial parameters can be estimated jointly or selectively fixed through the same block controls.
This is deterministic sparse-direct REML for moderate compiled problems. It stores dense covariance/derivative blocks within each series, and the usual global sparse derivative arrays. The supplied-covariance packed prediction route retains its existing Markov preparation. Industrial packed REML and long-series REML scalability have not been qualified. Failed fits retain diagnostics and publish no qualified predictions; no convergence or likelihood gate is relaxed automatically.
For ordinary pedigrees with unstructured genetic covariance and independent residual blocks, the separate packed EM-REML route uses analysis.traces to select exact or stochastic PCG moment traces. It shares the pedigree factor across covariance updates and reports scores/MCSE rather than a restricted likelihood. Whole-block fixing is supported; FA, serial parameters, groups and metafounders are outside this initial packed REML scope.



The fixed-group syntax and ordinary inheritance definition above also work with formulation: ss_snp, either pedigree factorization and either supported packed preconditioner. Combined models keep the metafounder covariance pedigree and the original ordinary group-inheritance pedigree separate. The small references compare all coefficients, group contributions and total predictions with dense equations under both pedigree factorization routes.
For these additions, preparation computes F once in parent-first order and writes a fingerprinted NumPy array, with 8 Ã— ordinary-individuals Ã— groups bytes per group effect, plus metadata/array overhead. describe.group_proportion_bytes reports this storage. Fixed reference contrasts or random inherited means are lowered into record columns; random group coefficients retain the supplied independent group prior. Packed genotype products and the exact genetic model are unchanged. The original ordinary random-group route retains implicit pedigree sweeps. Models with many group levels can make the explicit preparation array expensive; no application RAM ceiling is imposed. Packed inherited random means currently require the common, unweighted individual incidence used in these references; their combination with weighted or separate channel mappings is rejected pending validation.



PEV precision work has resumed. Existing fixed-budget estimators remain available. For unstructured stochastic PEV with exact prior diagonals, optionally add:
output:
  uncertainty:
    method: stochastic
    effect: genetic
    individuals: genotyped
    probes: 28
    pilot_probes: 8
    deflation_rank: 4
    seed: 4401
    maximum_solves: 128
    maximum_reliability_mcse: 0.02
    prior: {method: exact, maximum_individuals: 0}
The independent, nondeflated pilot estimates raw posterior sampling variance. For each target its pilot reliability MCSE predicts the required final count using inverse sample-count variance scaling. The maximum across requested targets is rounded up, with probes as the minimum and maximum_solves - pilot_probes - deflation_rank as the maximum. The pilot can be conservative because the final estimator may use deflation.
Pilot samples are discarded. Final probes use a separate stream and a fixed count conditional on the pilot, avoiding reuse and repeated-stopping selection of the final diagonal/MCSE. Diagnostics separately count pilot queries, allocated and completed final probes, sketch queries and all posterior solves. Both equation residual gates still apply to every solve. The precision target can remain unmet; such finite candidates remain unqualified and are never clipped. MCSE is Monte Carlo sampling error, not a confidence-coverage or model-calibration certificate. More probes can improve precision at extra runtime. This does not establish a better estimator at the same total solve budget or industrial performance.
Focused Windows qualification passed 25 affected model/reference tests, four native compiled-MME gates and the five complete new examples. Additional CHOLMOD checks cover FA/scalar constraints and serial likelihoods. Final direct dense comparisons also check complete natural scores and AI matrices for FA and both serial families. The nonlinear serial covariance curvature term is included, and both strict 1e-8 and default-control serial references converge on PARDISO and CHOLMOD. Iteration-limited nonconvergence remains a rejected fit. The canonical package-only rebuild and R runtime smoke checks passed; this is not a full R CMD check or GenomeDK qualification. Receipts are under build/validation/model-parameter-* and build/validation/parameter-model-examples-20261016/. In the small independent pilot comparison, mean reliability MCSE changed from 0.25277 with four final probes to 0.05464 with 64 final probes plus four discarded pilot queries. The final values exactly match a separate fixed-64-probe run. The requested precision target was still unmet and remained unqualified; this demonstrates work allocation and error reduction, not production precision or coverage.

title: Standalone YAML model specification
text:
The optional top-level evaluation mapping references a named individual-level output.predictions request, a long truth CSV and its column mappings:
evaluation:
  predictions: genetic_values
  truth:
    file: true_breeding_values.csv
    columns: {individual: animal, trait: trait, value: true_breeding_value}
  subset: heldout
  individual: individual
  genotypes: genotypes
predictions, truth, subset and individual are required. genotypes is an optional PLINK input reference for stratified reporting. individual names a mapped model-data column. subset is heldout, phenotyped or all; cohort membership uses individuals with any observed response after wide/long input lowering. Evaluation does not mask records or change the model. Record/grid prediction requests are not evaluation targets. Unknown keys, missing or nonfinite truth values, duplicate labels and unknown target levels/traits are rejected. validate checks settings and targets; describe includes resolved paths and cohort counts. Only run performs scoring after numerical acceptance.
Outputs, metric definitions, qualification and the frontend version boundary are described in the standalone guide.


Use output.uncertainty.contrasts to request sums, differences or trajectories from named predictions. A term names prediction, trait, weight, and a quoted level for level predictions or record for data predictions. The prediction already defines effect channels, incidence mappings and bases. See the complete example (models/prediction-contrasts.yml).
method: exact requires maximum_solves and computes one inverse action per contrast. covariance: full also reports cross-contrast prediction-error covariances; the default is diagonal. Coefficient right-hand sides stream one at a time. Direct models reuse the accepted factor; packed models reuse the pedigree transforms and PCG preconditioner.
method: stochastic supports diagonal PEV with explicit probes, deflation_rank, seed, maximum_solves and maximum_mcse in PEV units. The budget counts sketch plus residual-probe inverse actions. Reports retain raw estimates, MCSE and target qualification; negative estimates are not clipped. These controls reuse the existing independent-sketch estimator and do not change the qualification of the existing genetic reliability estimators.
Outputs are prediction_uncertainty.csv and, when requested, prediction_covariance.csv. Uncertainty is conditional on supplied covariance parameters; it excludes variance-parameter estimation error. The initial YAML contrast route uses analysis.task: solve and excludes inherited group effects. Fit covariances first and refit them for conditional uncertainty. Native compiled and packed APIs support arbitrary sparse coefficient contrasts.

title: Separate LMT directives and data
text:
The development standalone frontend provides two independent commands for a four-trait, wide-table ssSNPBLUP comparison with supplied covariance matrices. These commands prepare files; they do not execute LMT.
gsuite convert-data model16-ancestral.yml --to lmt --output lmt-data
gsuite translate model16-ancestral.yml --to lmt --output para.xml \
  --data-manifest lmt-data/manifest.json --lmt-conv -25
The convergence value above is an explicit LMT setting for illustration. It is not a translation of gsuite’s relative or absolute residual tolerance. Select and verify LMT convergence using its documented criterion and compare final residuals before comparing performance.


The current simulation uses scale: 0.95, polygenic_weight: 0.0 and independent_ridge: 0.05: its genomic matrix is 0.95 G + 0.05 I. The public LMT ssSNPBLUP example documents aweight, a blend with the pedigree relationship matrix. That does not express this identity ridge. An exact LMT mapping for the independent scale and ridge has not been verified.
For this model, data conversion is available, but directive translation writes an accepted: false report beside the requested XML path, returns exit status 2, and writes no XML. Do not change the blend merely to make translation pass: that would change the statistical model being compared.
The initial directive profile supports the documented positive pedigree blend with scale one, no independent ridge, optional pedigree-moment adjustment, sample-mean centering and sum-of-2p(1-p) normalization. Even for that profile, acceptance means a supported translation only. A user-run GHPC test passed for a tiny four-trait adjusted 5% pedigree blend; that is not qualification of every input model or executable. The report always records numerical_equivalence_verified: false.



For the four-trait comparison inspired by the WCGALP example, use a separate model copy with this genomic block:
genomic:
  adjustment: pedigree_moments
  scale: 1.0
  polygenic_weight: 0.05
  independent_ridge: 0.0
The translator emits aweight: 0.05 and switch: adjustg2a. For a sample-mean centered genomic matrix, the grand mean is zero. Matching mean diagonal and grand mean therefore gives intercept mean(A_gg) and slope (mean(diag(A_gg)) - mean(A_gg)) / mean(diag(G)). Using the off-diagonal mean instead gives the same affine transformation. Both approaches are checked on a tiny example with unequal pedigree relationships and unsorted genotype IDs. The native gsuite check agrees with the independent reference at relative tolerance 1e-11. A user-run GHPC comparison on 31 October 2026 confirmed LMT coefficients of slope 0.25 and intercept 0.75 and agreement of all 24 animal genetic predictions. The largest reported absolute difference was 9.218406594e-11. This is a small-fixture result, not a large-data guarantee.
On a GHPC allocation with the updated source bundle, run the independent comparison against the installed LMT executable:
python3 validation/compare_lmt_adjustment.py \
  --output "$PWD/lmt-adjustment-check" \
  --gsuite "$PWD/install/bin/gsuite" \
  --lmt /path/to/lmt --lmt-key /opt/lmt.key
This creates fresh six-animal, three-genotyped, four-marker, four-trait inputs, runs gsuite and LMT, and compares LMT’s logged beta and alpha with an independent dense calculation. comparison.json distinguishes native gsuite verification from live LMT verification. The updated test checks the adjustment, resulting blended genomic covariance and all 24 animal genetic predictions. prediction-comparison.json records the prediction tolerances and differences. It does not establish matching convergence criteria. LMT is not bundled. Run in a fresh output directory to prevent reuse of LMT’s adjustg2a.bin cache. If LMT fails or does not expose the coefficients, the test fails and retains the inputs and logs.
The Windows development host has no usable Linux LMT runtime; live LMT evidence above was supplied by the user from GHPC. Existing frozen bundles do not acquire these translator changes automatically. The current exporter writes <models> and datafile:, as required by the tested executable.
LMT’s adjusted ssSNPBLUP solution CSV includes animal predictions, marker coefficients and one augmented coefficient under the same variance/factor label. For the tiny fixture, the prediction checker validates six animal rows, four marker rows and one augmented row per trait, then compares only the animal predictions. This fixture-specific checker must not be applied directly to the million-animal solution file.



Real-valued data, frequencies and XML numbers use scientific notation with 17 fractional mantissa digits. This preserves binary64 round trips in the exported text while bounding the decimal mantissa length for reader compatibility. IDs and genotype encodings remain unchanged. Conversion manifests record numeric_encoding: scientific_17_fraction_digits; translation rejects older manifests without this encoding. Reconvert old snapshots into a fresh directory before binding their manifest; an earlier successful conversion does not certify its numeric text for this reader compatibility requirement. Original snapshots are never modified automatically.
For the existing GHPC million-animal dataset, after installing the new bundle inside a 16-CPU allocation, prepare a separate model without editing the identity-ridge model:
export GSUITE="$PWD/install/bin/gsuite"
export DATA="$HOME/gsuite/datasets/n1000000-ng150000-m40000-q4-s4401-new"
python3 - "$DATA" <<'PY'
import pathlib, sys, yaml
d = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
m = yaml.safe_load((d/'model16-ancestral.yml').read_text())
m['name'] = 'single_step_1m_t16_blend05_adjusted'
m['relationships']['H']['genomic'].update(
    adjustment='pedigree_moments', scale=1.0,
    polygenic_weight=0.05, independent_ridge=0.0)
with (d/'model16-blend05-adjusted.yml').open('x') as f:
    yaml.safe_dump(m, f, sort_keys=False)
PY

"$GSUITE" validate "$DATA/model16-blend05-adjusted.yml"
export LMT_DATA="$DATA/lmt-data-v36"
"$GSUITE" convert-data "$DATA/model16-blend05-adjusted.yml" \
  --to lmt --output "$LMT_DATA"
If this dataset has already been converted successfully with the scientific numeric encoding above, set LMT_DATA to that existing directory and skip convert-data. Covariance, genomic blend, adjustment and solver settings do not change the data contract. This reuses a snapshot: verify that the original inputs have not changed since conversion.
Run sequentially on the same allocation and record separate output trees:
export COMPARE="$DATA/comparison-blend05-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir "$COMPARE"
"$GSUITE" run "$DATA/model16-blend05-adjusted.yml" \
  --output "$COMPARE/gsuite"

"$GSUITE" translate "$DATA/model16-blend05-adjusted.yml" \
  --to lmt --data-manifest "$LMT_DATA/manifest.json" \
  --output "$COMPARE/lmt/para.xml" --lmt-conv -25 --lmt-convtype cr

(
  cd "$COMPARE/lmt" || exit 1
  cp -p /opt/lmt.key lmt.key
  ulimit -s unlimited
  export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16 MKL_NUM_THREADS=16
  export OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE MKL_DYNAMIC=FALSE
  export OMP_STACKSIZE=2000M OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=true
  export OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS=2147483647
  export KMP_AFFINITY=granularity=core,scatter
  "$CONDA_PREFIX/bin/time" -v -o time.txt \
    /path/to/lmt -f para.xml > console.log 2>&1
)
Keep each LMT run directory fresh to avoid priming from results.bin or reusing adjustg2a.bin. GNU time is the existing Conda time package. Data conversion is outside both fit timings. gsuite’s end-to-end timing is in execution.json; LMT’s end-to-end timing is in time.txt. Inspect both native logs for successful convergence. LMT’s explicit cr=-25 setting is the small test’s setting; it is not asserted equivalent to gsuite’s relative 1e-11 and absolute 1e-13 stopping controls. Report the criteria alongside timings, and compare final predictions before drawing performance conclusions.
convert-data reads and validates the YAML inputs, then writes a fresh output directory containing:

Numeric data.csv with four responses, an intercept and effect group columns.
Complete numeric pedigree.csv, individual-major genotypes.txt, its pedigree-ID cross.csv, and frequencies.blkcsv containing mean dosages.
Reversible id-map.csv, record-map.csv and marker-map.csv mappings, a diagnostic missing.csv, and manifest.json with source/output hashes.

Source files remain unchanged. Partial response missingness uses an explicit LMT missing-value threshold; observed zero remains observed. Records with all responses missing follow gsuite’s omission policy. Missing genotypes and fixed markers are rejected rather than imputed or removed. Genotypes retain source sample and marker order and count the first BIM allele.
BED decoding uses bounded sample batches (--sample-batch, default 128). The 150,000 by 40,000 panel produces approximately 6 GB of genotype text, in addition to observations, pedigree and mappings. Conversion is a separate cost from fitting and can be reused when only covariance or solver settings change. An interrupted or failed conversion retains an unaccepted manifest and partial files. Neither command overwrites an existing destination.



translate reads the YAML and optionally the small conversion manifest. It does not read or rewrite phenotype, pedigree or genotype data, and can run before those data exist. Without a manifest, references default to lmt-data/ beside the XML file. With a manifest, it checks the input/binding contract and records its hash; it does not rehash the large converted files or check whether source contents have changed since conversion. The manifest identifies the converted snapshot, not a live data view.
The initial profile requires four traits, an intercept, one single-step genetic effect, ordinary identity random effects, and full positive-definite covariance matrices in declared trait order. It excludes weighted/structured residuals, random regressions, genetic groups, metafounders and genotype ID maps. gsuite thread/backend settings and requested output tables are not translated into an LMT execution policy. The receipt records source execution settings and the explicit LMT convergence setting. LMT runtime settings must be controlled separately for a benchmark.
The format references are the official LMT guide’s parameter elements, input files, examples and algorithms.



The reverse adapter admits the explicit four-trait snpblup1 profile generated by this frontend: four intercept equations, genetic, site, family and individual environment effects, supplied positive definite covariance matrices, positive pedigree blending and optional adjustg2a. Unsupported equations, switches and data options are rejected. This is not a general LMT parameter-file importer.
gsuite convert-data para.xml --from lmt --to gsuite --output imported-data \
  --source-data-manifest lmt-data/manifest.json
gsuite translate para.xml --from lmt --to gsuite \
  --data-manifest imported-data/manifest.json --output imported.yml
gsuite validate imported.yml
For files not produced by gsuite, provide --marker-map marker-map.csv instead of --source-data-manifest. The map must contain lmt_column, source_marker, chromosome, position, dosage_allele and other_allele, in marker order. Text dosages cannot identify marker names or alleles by themselves. Conversion reconstructs SNP-major BED, BIM and FAM, checks supplied frequencies against sample mean dosages, and rejects missing/non-012 genotypes and fixed markers. Custom centering frequencies are outside this profile.
The imported model retains LMT numeric animal IDs and trait labels y1 through y4; it does not infer original source names. Directive translation reads control files and manifest metadata, without rewriting or scanning data. Without a manifest it emits a draft with data_ready: false. Source convergence controls are recorded, but their stopping criterion is not declared equivalent to gsuite’s.
Small deterministic reverse-conversion tests compare all animal genetic values with independent marginal BLUP equations at two pedigree blend weights, with partially missing responses. Genotype round trips and unsupported-input rejection are tested separately. These tests do not invoke LMT or certify arbitrary LMT models. Full cross-software prediction and residual qualification remains a separate, executable-specific step.
