Ncores defaults to one. Explicit MCMC-only arguments fail for vbayes. Multiple optimization starts are not chains and are outside this target.
Nchains counts logical chains; ncores requests workers. Multiple chains may run serially. Prepared resources are immutable and shared. State, RNG, residuals, workspaces, accumulators and traces are chain-private. A multivariate chain samples the entire joint model; traits are not independent tasks. Worker threads do not call R APIs or allocate R objects.
Preserve native RNG behavior during interface-only changes. Initially map the starting uint32 seed to consecutive distinct chain seeds, reject overflow and record requested/resolved seeds. A hashed task-seed scheme would need a separate versioned decision. Logical chain identity, never worker assignment, owns its seed. On qualified backends/builds, changing supported worker scheduling must preserve each logical chain’s scientific output. Cross-library/platform random stream identity is not promised.
For post-burn u=1,…,nit, retain u modulo nthin equal to zero and save the exact indices. Complete all requested transitions, including a remainder. A backend unable to honor the schedule must reject it rather than round or shorten nit. Remove burn-in once. The initial factor adapter may require divisibility until the exact full-schedule boundary is qualified.
Expose only qualified parallel execution. Validate ncores>1 support and report requested workers and actual execution; do not silently claim parallel execution after falling back. Existing serial factor routes do not gain parallelism from a signature change. The specialized summary MCMC adapters are likewise serial. Point-normal has no native thinning API and explicitly requires nthin=1.

title: gbayes R interface design
text:
Diagnostics and resource accounting
Diagnostic capture, posterior thinning, compact chain records and retained trace arrays are separate policies. Capture occurs at completed transitions, consumes no RNG and cannot change updates, rerun chains or feed back into inference. Report the actual available diagnostic schedule. Do not imply that unthinned native traces exist where they do not.
MCMC diagnostics include applicable rank-normalized split/folded R-hat, ESS and MCSE, with explicit constant/fixed/unavailable/unrequested statuses. One chain provides no between-chain R-hat evidence. Factor diagnostics emphasize invariant effects, covariance and predictions rather than uninterpretable pooled loading means. Sampling completion, adequate mixing, numerical correctness and calibration are distinct claims.
Variational diagnostics record objective definition, iteration count, stopping reason, parameter changes and EB updates. An augmented missing-outcome bound is labelled separately from observed-data likelihood. Hitting nit is not a convergence certificate.
Preflight counts shared packed/LD/kernel resources, all chain workspaces, output, diagnostic traces and transient R/native copies. An estimated allocation ceiling is not measured process RSS. Pass through solve, factorization, update, decode/ packed-product and preparation counters where available. Unknown counters stay unavailable. Separate preparation, fitting and formatting time where measurable.
All-marker draw/diagnostic storage is opt-in and bounded. Diagnostic defaults and retention requests need a capability-checked mapping to current backends; this design does not authorize a new generic trace subsystem.

title: gbayes R interface design
text:
Qualification and implementation gates
Resolve the following against current native contracts before enabling the corresponding target. They do not reopen the six-function naming decision.







Gate
Required outcome




Per-route defaults
Exact initialization, hyperprior scale, likelihood dimension and learning behavior; explicit/default equivalence


BayesRC initialization and residual policy
Resolved for scalar individual/block-eigen routes above; preserve independent coefficient priors and separate block-scale mapping


Multivariate BayesRC
Individual and sparse-summary fixed-residual routes expose separate pattern/positive-magnitude annotations; cross-product remains gated


Specialized summaries
Resolved above for both existing MCMC and both fixed-prior variational engines; preserve distinct scales, windows and availability


Additional cross-product methods
Extend the qualified exact C/R adapter only after method-specific scale, response-scatter and prediction checks


Internal additive kernel
Selected-genotype dense references, normalization, multi-file ordering and factor input invariants


Execution and diagnostics
Actual capture/retention availability, RNG preservation and supported worker behavior



Existing factor limits remain n<=256, T<=128, q<=16, and bayesFR p<=4096. Packed factor support is resident; relationship storage is quadratic in samples. Multiple kernels, arbitrary fixed covariates, generic overlap, broad calibration and genome-wide factor performance are not qualified. Recorded full-model MegaBayesC mixing failures remain unresolved and paused. New names and common summaries do not repair them. Additional annotation-dependent sharing/covariance models beyond the documented joint pattern/magnitude/variance model and extra variance components are outside scope.

title: gbayes R interface design
text:
Bounded implementation sequence and acceptance
Beyond the authorized individual slice, implementation requires a separate user instruction. Use existing public native APIs and independent references in this sequence.







Work
Focused acceptance




Resolved specifications and six adapters
Exact names, dimensions and supported combinations; explicit/default mapping; no compatibility branch


Common result and access
Correct meanings, labels, size-one axes and NULL reasons; final versus posterior; serialization and prediction gates


Resources and internal kernel
Sample/marker selection, alleles, training imputation and kernel entries/normalization versus independent dense references


Chain and diagnostic integration
Per-chain replay, exact retained indices, observational capture, qualified serial/parallel equivalence and bounded allocation rejection


Route promotion
Small installed-package fixtures and existing native references; fresh pinned parity when a numerical/prior change warrants it



Keep tests deterministic and focused. Preserve tolerances, independent dense references, pinned-software provenance and installed-consumer checks. API identity cannot replace an independent numerical oracle. Broad simulations, performance campaigns, sampler development, releases, commits and pushes are not authorized by this design task.

title: gbayes R interface design
text:
Related contracts and implementation references
Use the current Bayesian workflow, package boundaries, genotype preparation contract, development limits and Bayesian qualification guide for their subjects. This page alone owns the target six-interface design.
Current R implementation references are packages/gbayes/R/qgg-interface.R, gbayes.R, gbayes-multivariate.R, adaptive-factor.R, adaptive-bed.R, covariance-mixture.R, factor-facade.R, block-eigen.R and blr.R. Glist preparation is in packages/gbase/R/gprep.R.
Native owner contracts include gbayes docs/multivariate.md, docs/mega-factor.md, docs/mega-bayesc.md and the mr.mash route contracts; gmat docs/design/relationship_kernels.md owns the reusable kernel primitive. Sblr reference principles are its current public wrappers, raw-v2/access code, and docs/dev/blr_phase8a_public_r_alignment_checkpoint.md, blr_phase7_pattern_scale_mt_checkpoint.md, blr_output_schema.md and blr_convergence_contract.md. Check current dispatch before using older capability tables. Sibling sources are provenance references, not build, test, runtime or website-render dependencies.

Exact in-sample residual learning
Batch source 0.1.16 reuses native fit_informed_bayesc with GaussianLearning and fit_multivariate_residual; no new sampler is introduced. It is implemented in source, awaiting the batch build and focused runtime tests.
Informed scalar bayes/sbayes BayesC MCMC accepts updateE=TRUE, explicit initial ve, optional nue (default 4, >2) and prior\(veScale. Marker means, probabilities
and slab variances stay fixed. Individual preparation supplies centered
response scatter and defaults to dimension n-1; control\)likelihoodDimension can declare the compatible selected likelihood dimension. Summary preparation requires control$normalization with response_ss, likelihood_dimension and in_sample_ld=TRUE; residualPolicy, if supplied, must be “in_sample”. VB stays fixed-residual and ordinary uninformed defaults are unchanged.
Independent msbayes C/R MCMC accepts updateE=TRUE with sampling fields residual_variance (initial values), response_sum_squares, likelihood_dimension and in_sample_ld=TRUE. Numeric vectors are named in provider order, independently of trait order. nue is one scalar or a provider-named vector; explicit veScale is a provider-named vector. Existing updateB/updatePi learning and proper priors remain available. Complete per-provider LD, common N equal to its reference count and compatible response scatter are required. N can differ between providers; declared study_sample_size must match it. There is no overlap model. Shared-LD response-crossproduct covariance learning remains separate.
For sigma^2=nu*a/chi-square(nu), the default scale a=(nu-2)/nu times initial variance makes that initialization the prior mean. The exact native SSE is y’y-2b’X’y+b’X’Xb, with conditional degrees of freedom nu+d. The same outcome units, covariate projection and selected samples must define all statistics. An explicit in_sample_ld assertion and equal counts record assumptions; they cannot independently establish provenance or sample independence.
Provider posterior means live in parameters\(provider_residual_variance;
retained parameter columns are provider_residual_variance[provider], and final
chain-by-provider scales live in final\)providerResidualVariance. Native trace summaries supply intervals and diagnostics; without trace retention these remain unavailable while means and terminal values remain. Initial variances stay explicitly initial in sampling metadata. Common formatting accepts real terminal effects separately from continuation states. These extensions expose no capture, annotations, continuation or saved gmap interpretation; effects, PIP meanings and save/reload are preserved. Full-panel reference LD and truncated/eigen residual updates cannot substitute for the exact likelihood. See ?exact_residual_learning and tools/examples/gbayes/exact-residual.R.


Population continuous shrinkage
Development version 0.1.16 extends msbayes with method=“continuous_shrinkage”, algorithm=“mcmc” and prior$hierarchy=“prs_csx”, “jointprs_reference” or “panther_reference”. All updates reuse native fit_population_shrinkage or fit_panther_reference. These adapters pass focused developer references; experimental reference/mixing limits remain. The existing scalar sbayes route is unchanged.
Supply 2-32 named population summary tables. Their names are effect columns; trait is one unnamed common phenotype (default “trait”), not a study-to-trait mapping. Declare independent sampling. A shared Glist or named catalog with sampling$reference supplies population LD. Each reference and summary must already cover the same ordered marker intersection, alleles and coordinates, with verified define_ld_blocks() partitions. There is no automatic intersection, missing-marker union or sharing-group construction. GWAS rows/alleles use the existing checked summary alignment. Common N is required within each population; N and LD/blocks may differ between populations. Samples must be independent; reference reuse does not imply discovery sample overlap. Native block checks reject retained edges crossing blocks.
Effects use standardized phenotype/genotype units. GlobalScale defaults to 1; updateB defaults FALSE and controls its learning. Local and normalized residual scales always update. These are reference transitions with normalized outcomes, not the exact in-sample SSE extension described above. updateE=FALSE and C/R pi/vb/ve hyperparameters are rejected. Serial chains share prepared CSR resources. Managed memory admission includes moments and mandatory selected native traces, with remaining-budget reservations for dense blocks. The default maximum block size is 2048, native limit 8192; no process-wide RSS guarantee is claimed.
PRS-CSx/JointPRS localShape and auxiliaryShape default to 1/.5, with explicit referenceLocalCap=TRUE. Post-GIG min(psi,1) is clipping, not exact truncated sampling. JointPRS requires population-named correlationCaps; pair support is [0,min(cap[t]*cap[u],.99)] with the native +/- .02 correlation proposal. Correlation means, acceptance fractions and selected traces remain visible. Its marginal residual-scale/pairwise-rho sequence remains an experimental reference transition; existing weak-fixture mixing and tail-ESS limitations are retained. Prior population correlation is not a local genetic correlation or evidence of shared causal markers.
Panther requires an exact marker-by-population binary sharingGroups matrix, pantherRoute (source/target) and outputPopulation. Source mode permits category one only in the output population, with category zero represented in every population. Target mode ignores supplied categories and caps psi at 1/phi. These are supplied annotations, not fitted sharing probabilities. The current native result estimates all population effects, including auxiliary populations; the adapter retains them and records the output role without relabelling axes. No LOGODetect search or score combination is added.
Common bayesfit preserves empirical means/second moments, pooled variances, terminal effects, a marker-named shared localScales vector, population-labelled residual scales, optional populationCorrelation/groupScales and selected native trace intervals/diagnostics. Fixed global scale is marked not estimated. Selected first-marker traces do not imply all-marker draws. Turning retention off keeps transitions/moments/final effects unchanged. No spike PIPs, posterior capture, annotations beyond Panther categories, continuation, individual prediction or saved gmap conversion are exposed. See ?population_shrinkage and tools/examples/gbayes/population-shrinkage.R.


Scalar summary IBSS
Development version 0.1.16 adds sbayes(method=“multi_effect”, algorithm=“ibss”) for one bounded region and one quantitative trait. Native fit_multi_effect owns sequential updates, component variance learning and expected-SSE residual learning. The R adapter accepts checked score=X’y/information=diag(X’X), or calls exported gmap::gmap_stat on ordinary b/seb/n with control$phenotypeVariance. Preparation uses intercept-only conventional OLS, not S-scale conversion or 1/SE^2. gmap is optional for raw preparation/reference tests; prepared inputs fit without it.
The whole fitted panel must match complete one-chromosome sparse LD in exact marker/allele/coordinate order. No row harmonization, implicit filtering or regional regeneration is performed. The same public gsolve eigensystem and gbayes factor/response helpers used by gmap bind diag(sqrt(information))Rdiag(sqrt(information)). All verified eigenvalues must be positive: no rank truncation, jitter or silent score projection is exposed. The default panel bound is 2048 markers, with managed dense/factor/component memory admission rather than a process RSS claim.
nit caps sweeps (default 500), control\(effects defaults 10, vb starts at .02 and
ve at 1. updateB defaults TRUE and reuses native learned single-effect variance,
including inactive zero-variance components. updateB=FALSE fixes vb. Named
prior\)markerWeights are fixed relative assignment masses; zero excludes a marker. updatePi=TRUE and C/R pi/h2/shape hyperpriors are rejected. There are no sampled chains, burn-in, thinning or seeds, and only one worker is supported.
updateE defaults FALSE. TRUE requires explicit control$normalization with response_ss, likelihood_dimension and in_sample_ld=TRUE, declared common N equal to reference N, compatible prepared scatter, and fitted rank <= dimension <= N. Counts and assertions do not establish provenance. Native full-factor checks and expected SSE retain component prediction uncertainty/assignment covariance. SSE/d is a variational/EB update, not inverse-chi-square MCMC sampling. External LD is allowed only with fixed residual variance on its supplied Gaussian likelihood.
Common bayesfit returns OLS effects, variational variances, active-component union PIPs, component assignments/scales/moments, active and inner-convergence flags, objective/residual traces and final score residual. Inactive components have zero effects/PIPs even if their uninformative assignment row retains prior mass. Positive fixed components force assignments; PIPs are not guaranteed to vanish under weak evidence. Components condition on the others’ means and do not prove independent causal signals. The objective is a relative variational bound, not model evidence. Maximum sweeps and inner nonconvergence remain provisional.
fit_contract records OLS units and assignment meanings; RDS contains no native handles. Prediction, capture, continuation and saved scalar gmap conversion are unavailable. Existing joint IBSS mapping and direct gmap multi_effect remain unchanged. Focused developer references pass in 0.1.16. See ?scalar_summary_ibss and tools/examples/gbayes/scalar-summary-ibss.R.


Weighted individual and summary elastic-net penalties
Development version 0.1.16 extends all four genomic elastic_net/coordinate_descent interfaces with control\(l1Weights and control\)l2Weights. Each supplied vector is finite, nonnegative and uniquely named for every fitted marker; names align it. One omitted vector defaults to ones. Neither vector is normalized. Without either, the existing unweighted scalar/joint path is unchanged.
For training empirical-SD dosages Z, centered unscaled y and existing scalar penalty covariance K (default 1), the objective is squared loss/(2n) plus lambdaalphasum(w1abs(beta))/sqrt(K) and lambda(1-alpha)sum(w2beta^2)/(2K). Penalties remain centered at zero. Constant w1=w2=c is lambda multiplied by c; zero removes that penalty rather than excluding a marker. Both zero leave a coefficient unpenalized. Alpha=1 is already supported and ignores L2 weights; alpha=0 remains rejected.
For mbayes the existing fixed SPD penalty covariance K must be labelled in selected trait order. The objective for centered unscaled response matrix Y is
||Y - Z B||_F^2/(2*n)
 + lambda*alpha*sum_jt w1[j]*abs(B[j,t])/sqrt(K[t,t])
 + lambda*(1-alpha)/2*sum_j w2[j]*B[j,]' inverse(K) B[j,].
Both marker vectors are shared across traits. A zero L2 weight removes that marker’s full precision block, including cross-trait terms. K is a penalty covariance, not residual covariance or likelihood weighting. Marker-by-trait weight matrices are not admitted.
The adapter prepares selected training BED statistics through the public native preparer, converts empirical penalties to HWE sum-scale coefficients and calls existing fit_l1_quadratic. No numerical optimizer or dense design/Gram is copied. The joint bridge calls additive native fit_individual_weighted_covariance_elastic_net, reusing its existing packed multivariate preparation and covariance operator. The native marker scale multiplies the whole precision block; old public native signatures/result layouts remain intact. Rebuild/install native gbayes before the R package at the batch checkpoint to supply the new symbol. Returned effects/coding are empirical-SD coordinates, with missing imputation, centers and SD estimated only on training samples. Existing prediction and RDS handoff are preserved. No PIPs, posterior variances or MCMC draws are invented.
Resolved normalized penalty coefficients are saved in input\(penalty, and canonical
weights in input\)control. Joint l1 is a marker-by-trait matrix; joint l2 records markerWeights, multiplier, covariance and the quadratic form without repeated per-marker precision matrices. Diagnostics preserve native sum-scale objective/KKT, add normalized empirical-coordinate KKT, and qualify lambdaMax. Zero L1 weight with nonzero null score in any trait yields Inf/no_finite_null_threshold; all zero scores can yield a zero threshold. A numerically unrepresentable positive-weight threshold has its own exceeds_numeric_range status. Native convergence/failure semantics remain; these diagnostics do not certify coefficient uniqueness when curvature is singular. No selection, weight fitting or additional generic covariates are added. Independent full-precision active-set references, unit/ constant/diagonal reductions, zero weights, trait permutations and saved prediction tests pass in the focused 0.1.16 developer checkpoint. See ?weighted_elastic_net and tools/examples/gbayes/weighted-elastic-net.R.
The same source batch extends scalar sbayes elastic_net/coordinate_descent using the existing checked b/SE/n conversion r=b/sqrt(n*seb2+b2), complete marker/coordinate/allele alignment and one common GWAS N. With supplied sparse reference LD R, its normalized objective is
beta' R beta / 2 - r' beta
 + lambda*alpha*sum(w1*abs(beta))/sqrt(K)
 + lambda*(1-alpha)*sum(w2*beta^2)/(2*K).
Scalar penalty covariance K defaults to one. Both weights default to ones and retain the same named, nonnegative, nonnormalized marker contract. The bridge composes public disk_ld_cross_products, prepare_summary_gaussian/common_n and fit_l1_quadratic with C=NR, score=Nr and N times these penalties. There is no new native API/solver, dense Gram expansion or genotype recoding. maxLdEntries and managed memoryLimit preflight the existing disk-backed LD operator/workspace.
Effects use standardized summary phenotype/dosage coordinates, not individual empirical-SD coordinates. This is a reference-LD pseudo-likelihood, not exact in-sample statistics. Convexity requires supplied PSD LD; thresholding/windowing can violate that assumption. The adapter does not certify/repair/project LD. ldPsdCertified=FALSE and ldRepair=“none” remain explicit; coordinate/KKT convergence does not establish PSD, mismatch suitability or uniqueness. A singular summary objective with incompatible score may be unbounded when penalties vanish. Native objective/convergence failure checks remain active.
Summary maximumKktSum/objectiveWithoutResponseConstant are sum-scale; maximumKktSummary/normalizedObjectiveWithoutResponseConstant divide by GWAS N. The response constant is not identified. lambdaMax is max(abs(r)sqrt(K)/(alphaw1)), retaining zero-weight and numeric-overflow statuses. No training coding/intercept, direct prediction, posterior uncertainty, capture, continuation, tuning or saved mapping is added. Focused active-set, closed-form identity-LD, Gaussian reduction, unit/constant/default, allele/order and common-contract tests are authored; source parsing alone does not validate them at runtime.
Joint msbayes now has source support for the same penalty, with required trait-labelled SPD control$covariance K and explicit sampling. It reuses normal shared-Glist or study-named Glist/trait-map preparation. The bounded route has 2–32 traits, one provider per trait, and one common complete ordered marker panel. Independent providers can have distinct LD and different common N; shared_ld requires one reference and equal N across traits. Variable marker N, missing/local panels and repeated providers per trait remain outside this route.
The independent normalized loss is sum_t (.5b_t’R_tb_t-r_t’b_t)/v_t, with fixed sampling\(residual_variance v. The shared-LD loss is
.5*tr(inverse(Omega)*B'R*B)-tr(inverse(Omega)*r'B), with fixed sampling\)covariance Omega. Each provider’s Gaussian statistics are divided by its own N. This is a sum of normalized task losses, not an N-weighted pooled likelihood. Both add the same full-block K penalty as mbayes. Marker weights are shared across traits. Penalty K and sampling Omega/v are distinct and are never substituted for each other. The null threshold uses the likelihood score r_t/v_t or r*inverse(Omega).
Additive native fit_summary_weighted_covariance_elastic_net binds existing MultivariateStatistics, a scaled reference operator, the existing Coupled operator with optional shared likelihood precision, and fit_l1_quadratic. Shared residuals reuse the generic native marker residual; no solver is copied into Rcpp. Existing native signatures/result layouts are unchanged. Rebuild native gbayes before R when refreshing this additive native symbol. Objective/KKT are already normalized and return directly as normalizedObjectiveWithoutResponseConstant/maximumKktSummary. The common saved contract now includes joint penalty provider maps/sampling. PSD LD remains a supplied assumption; no repair/certification, posterior uncertainty, training coding, direct prediction or mapping is added. Native/R dense active-set, distinct-LD/N, covariance-separation and scalar/unit reductions pass in the focused 0.1.16 developer checkpoint.


Prepared-design Gaussian and elastic net
Development version 0.1.16 adds bayes(data,X=Z,…) for scalar marker_gaussian/ pcg and elastic_net/coordinate_descent. Z must be finite, labelled by sample and feature, already centered and nonconstant by column. Data rows align by sample ID; the single response is centered without rescaling. Glist is omitted. No raw feature transform, missing-value preparation or feature standardization is inferred. Prediction takes already prepared target features and uses saved identity coding and the response mean. Coefficients are outcome units per supplied feature unit, rather than HWE/empirical-SD genotype units.
Use blr(XX,Xy,yy,n,…) for exact supplied scalar companions. Existing full joint Gram PSD, score-column-space, rank, likelihood-dimension and coding checks are reused. Optional yy may be zero for a zero response. Centered inputs default to n-1 likelihood dimension; residualized coding requires an explicit dimension. Cross-products are never normalized as marginal summaries. No generic joint, sparse, streamed or additional nuisance-design adapter is added here.
Gaussian priors reuse complete named markerVariance and optional markerMean with fixed ve; zero variance fixes a coefficient at its supplied mean. Native marker Gaussian fitting includes the full mean/fixed-coordinate score offsets. The bridge reuses marker_gaussian_mean and native fit_gaussian_marker_prior; the existing PCG fitter owns solving/residual checks. No variances/PIPs are fabricated by this mean-only route.
Prepared elastic net retains lambda>0, alpha in (0,1], scalar penalty covariance K and complete nonnegative named L1/L2 weights without normalization. It now also admits a fixed named prior$markerMean as penalty center m. Its objective is
(beta' XX beta / 2 - Xy' beta)/n
 + lambda*alpha*sum(w1*abs(beta-m))/sqrt(K)
 + lambda*(1-alpha)*sum(w2*(beta-m)^2)/(2*K).
The native L1/quadratic entry takes m and n times the penalties. No feature recoding occurs. lambdaMax targets effects equal to m, based on Xy-XX*m; it does not necessarily target zero effects. Native sum-coordinate objective/KKT and normalized prepared-coordinate diagnostics are both retained. Only the optional diagnostic mean product is separately counted; total optimizer-product counts are not invented. Alpha=0 remains gated; Gaussian priors use the PCG route.
Dense preparation is bounded by maxFeatures (2048) and managed memoryLimit (256 MiB), checked before crossprod/eigendecomposition; the feature cap is not a memory guarantee. R owns base crossprod and existing Gram validation; Rcpp constructs the public dense operator and calls existing native fitters. No native owner API or solver is added. Common fit_contract/extraction/RDS and prepared feature prediction retain explicit units. MCMC/learning/capture/restart/tuning controls remain rejected. Independent Gaussian, shifted active-set, exact-X/XX, fixed-coordinate, rescaling and prediction tests are authored, not run. See ?prepared_design and tools/examples/gbayes/prepared-design.R after the checkpoint.


Streamed and batched mixture prediction
Pending 0.1.16 adds scalar bayes normal_mixture/vbayes and streamed X support for laplace_gaussian/vbayes, reusing native fit_variational_prediction. X is a labelled finite matrix or a list(ids,features,readColumns,sourceId). The reader takes one-based inclusive column endpoints and returns every declared sample and requested feature in exact labelled order. Reads are synchronous/serial, ncores=1 and the source is immutable by contract. No new file format is added. sourceId records provenance but does not establish immutability.
Data rows align by sample ID and contain one finite quantitative response. The adapter adds an intercept; optional control$fixed supplies labelled finite covariates. Native full-rank QR projects both response and feature chunks and recovers fixed coefficients at the end. No feature centering/SD transform or imputation is inferred; effects use supplied source units. Prediction uses matching target feature matrices, plus fixed covariates for phenotype output. Only the feature component is returned by the common type=“genetic” option.
Normal-mixture vb contains absolute variances (one positive Gaussian, or leading zero plus positive normals); pi is a positive simplex and ve is fixed. Native weighted-mean normalization is compensated with totalVariance=psum(pivb), so the requested component variances are preserved. Laplace–Gaussian uses the existing per-feature vb/probability/fraction contract, supplied as totalVariance p*vb. This total is an internal scale conversion, not an estimated heritability. Prior means, variance/weight learning and h2/gamma calibration are not exposed.
Optional control$models is a named list of up to 128 vb/ve/pi/prior overrides within the same family/response/fixed design. Shared decoding/projection/Grams does not couple their posteriors. A supplied batch returns bayesfit_batch with named fits, each an ordinary scalar bayesfit. Without it, return one bayesfit. No CV, validation-driven stopping, selection, candidate averaging or trait-axis reinterpretation is performed. General selection/refit orchestration stays in gscore; current candidate batching is only a fitting primitive.
The source wrapper derives gsolve::RidgeDesignSource and copies bounded columns; all numerical moments, fixed projection, products, ELBO and residual audits are owned by the existing native engine. Controls expose chunkSize, localIterations, fullSweepInterval, skipSettledChunks, tolerance, gramCacheLimit and memoryLimit. The decoded backend/full marker schedule and strict audits are fixed. Native experimental adaptive schedules, validation callbacks, active masks, warm starts and persistent cache handles remain separate. Temporary chunk Grams are bounded; no global feature Gram or decoded whole panel is constructed by the adapter.
The public memory planner runs before source reads after reserving bridge, callback chunk, fixed-design/output and objective-history space. Source/caller storage and arbitrary closure/runtime allocations remain outside this managed bound. Means/variances for all features/candidates necessarily remain in memory. Shared counts are recorded once on the batch and copied into each fit’s batchExecution field; those copies must not be summed as independent work.
Return native variational means/variances, fixed coefficients, negative-ELBO history, residual sum of squares and execution/cache diagnostics. No component responsibilities/PIPs are exposed by the native moment result. Gaussian-limit means can match the projected Gaussian solve, but mean-field variances are conditional rather than full posterior marginal variances. The relative negative ELBO omits the fixed likelihood constant and is not absolute evidence. Convergence is a complete-refresh per-sample objective criterion, not a proof of global optimality; maximum sweeps is explicitly provisional. Errors publish no partial fit. There are no chains, capture, restart or mapping adapters.
Saved fits contain no reader closures/native handles, including calls made via do.call. Source metadata, resolved priors, fixed coefficients and units survive fit_contract and RDS. Focused analytic/quadrature, projected-Gaussian, batch/serial/cache, prediction and failure tests are authored, not executed. See ?streamed_prediction and tools/examples/gbayes/streamed-prediction.R.

title: gbayes R interface design
section: Scalar Gaussian co-data with frozen design coding
text:
Scalar Gaussian co-data with frozen design coding
Development version 0.1.16 adds bayes(method="marker_gaussian", algorithm="gaussian", X=..., ve=..., prior=list(coData=...)). R validates labels, complete scalar outcomes, group coverage and explicit options; gbayes::fit_gaussian_co_data owns all moment equations, hyper-ridge learning and final Gaussian fitting. No new native algorithm or sibling source change is needed. The direct Gaussian algorithm has its own contract; existing marker_gaussian/pcg behavior is unchanged.
X may be a finite labelled numeric matrix or dgCMatrix. The model is y = Z beta + noise, Z[,j] = (X[,j]-center[j])/scale[j]. Saved control$coding supplies named centers/scales (defaults zero/one). Outcomes are reordered by ID and otherwise unchanged. There is no inferred intercept, centering, nuisance projection or imputation. Effects have outcome units per transformed feature unit, not automatically HWE or standardized-phenotype units.
prior$coData contains a single named, fully covering, possibly overlapping groups list, group-set id, positive globalVariance (default 1), required positive hyperLambda, globalMode (fixed or known_noise_ml), positive varianceBounds, normalize, rhs (ecpc_2_positive_part or gaussian_unbiased) and profile (ecpc_2_full or target_one). One native update learns clipped group multipliers and averages them across each feature’s memberships. Optional normalization sets mean feature variance to the global variance. An unnormalized all-zero profile records ordinary-ridge fallback; normalizing an all-zero profile fails. Known-noise ML estimates the initial shared variance within supplied bounds, not residual variance. A nonconverged search fails without returning an accepted bayesfit. This is the native exact Gaussian profile, not complete ecpc software reproduction or a global ML certificate.
diagnostics(fit)$coData records learned feature variances, raw/clipped/used multipliers, moment equations, hyper-ridge profile, normalization/fallback, ML evaluations/boundary and factor/solve/materialization counts. Its samplingVariance is the sampling variance of the fitted mean at a frozen learned prior. It is not placed in posterior effectVariance. PIPs, posterior variances, hyperparameter uncertainty, chains, continuation and mapping remain unavailable. Native prediction uses saved transforms and complete fitted feature order; genetic/phenotype predictions agree because no intercept is fitted. Serializable results retain no original X or live native design.
Controls admit the dense dual n-by-n workspace and group-by-group equations before CSC copying/fitting: memoryLimit (64 MiB), maxRows (2048), maxGroups (256), and ML maximumEvaluations/maximumIterations/precisionBits. ncores must be one; nit does not control this direct fit. Numeric admission includes conservative bridge allowances; it is not an RSS cap or large-cohort throughput qualification. Supplied-fold CV, joint/summary adapters and general gscore selection remain separate; optional initial noise learning is described below. Focused developer reference checks pass in gbayes 0.1.16. Focused developer tests pass; this does not establish large-cohort qualification.

Multiple annotation group sets
The same scalar marker_gaussian/gaussian route now accepts prior$coData$sets=list(A=groupsA, B=groupsB) instead of groups/id, using native fit_gaussian_co_data_multi. Each named set must independently cover all fitted features. Overlap counts are normalized within its own set; group names can repeat across sets. These are annotations on one Gaussian response, not additional traits, cohorts or independent candidate models.
hyperLambda is an unnamed positive scalar shared across sets or a complete positive set-named vector. Group normalize and normalizeSets are distinct booleans. weightRule selects ecpc_2_switch (default), nonnegative or unconstrained_then_clip. The native switch tries normal equations and clips negatives, using NNLS after numerical failure or near-collinear feature profiles. Single-set weights stay one; all-unit profiles use equal weights. A one-group set uses the native fixed-unit group rule and skips hypershrinkage. The original groups adapter retains its generic profile, including its one-group behavior. Global variance selection is shared once; noise and per-set hyperpenalties remain fixed. The combined variance is t times the sum of weighted within-set feature profiles. Set normalization is post-fit scaling, not a constrained sum-to-one fit.
control$maxSets defaults to 16; maxGroups bounds total groups. Optional control$setWeights records native similarity/rank/NNLS tolerance and work limits (see package help). Whole-call native memory admission covers all stage bounds, plus conservative bridge/output allowances. Group, cross and final Gaussian counts are retained separately from set-weight normal/NNLS work. The diagnostic groupFits are named by set; setWeights retains raw/used weights, route, profile cosines, reduced equations, normal rank and NNLS KKT/work fields. Cross moments retain flattened set/group labels and native zero-based offsets. NNLS KKT fields describe raw weights before normalization, and unused route fields have no certificate meaning. Weights can be nonunique for dependent profiles and are prior-variance multipliers, not posterior/sharing probabilities.
A zero per-set fallback returns an explicit unidentified_source_profile failure with set identity when multiple sets are combined. Failed set solvers and ML searches return no accepted fit. Frozen coding, prediction, save/reload, units and unavailable posterior uncertainty are unchanged. Automatic group tuning is now source-ready below; patient CV and joint/summary co-data remain separate; initial noise learning is now source-ready below. Focused developer reference checks pass in gbayes 0.1.16. Focused references pass in the 0.1.16 developer checkpoint.


Saved feature-group split tuning
In development version 0.1.16, hyperLambda=0 requests native automatic group-penalty tuning through the same scalar marker_gaussian/gaussian adapter. Positive values keep fixed penalties; omission is still an error. Zero does not fit an unpenalized group equation. Noise is frozen during group fitting. Existing fixed/ known-noise modes are unchanged; optional initial joint ML is described below.
For groups, supply coData$splits as a nonempty named list of saved pairs: list(first=list(inside=list(left="u",right="v"), outside=list(left="v",right="w"))). Each half names every group and contains feature IDs from that group. The two halves must partition its full membership exactly; empty halves use character(0). Names are preserved and groups aligned by name. No splits are generated randomly. For sets, the outer splits list names exactly the automatically tuned sets, with those same per-set pair lists. Positive/zero set-named penalties can be mixed. Native one-group sets keep their unit profile and skip tuning even for zero penalties; fixed and skipped sets must not receive unused splits.
Native fitting retains full group denominators and within-set target overlap weights when computing split row equations. It builds inside-split ridge paths, sets lower=min(terminal path penalties)/100 and upper=max(first path penalties), then searches log(lambda) using the mean outside-equation RSS and raw, unclipped split-profile gamma. The split profile is ecpc_2_split; the final full fit still uses the declared full profile. The first path point has source deviance zero and the infinite-penalty convention, not a finite fit at that displayed value. This preserves the native exact-equation procedure and qualification limits.
control$tuning exposes native path count/minimum steps, minimum ratio, deviance and improvement stopping, double or archived Fortran-exponent spacing, and hyper-search evaluations/iterations/precision. These are distinct from global ML controls and set-weight solver controls; unused tuning controls are rejected. control$maxSplits defaults to 32 across all sets. Native planners and bridge allowances include retained split equations, paths and serialized output copies.
Saved input retains splits and resolved controls. Diagnostics expose tuning status, bounds, selected lambda, named paths/split equations, actual evaluations, boundary and factor/solve counts, at the top level for groups or under each named groupFits entry for sets. Exhaustion returns no accepted fit, identifying the set for a multi-set failure. Degenerate equations fail explicitly without inventing replacement splits. Prediction/save/reload do not retune, and effect units, coding, no-intercept semantics and unavailable posterior uncertainty stay unchanged. Bounded search is not a global-optimum certificate for arbitrary curves.
These are feature-group equation splits, not patient CV. All equations still use the supplied training outcomes. Keep held-out patients out of fitting; general patient-fold selection/refitting remains in gscore. Patient CV and joint/summary co-data remain separate; initial noise learning is now source-ready below. Focused developer reference checks pass in gbayes 0.1.16. Focused independent references pass in the 0.1.16 developer checkpoint.


Residual variance learning in scalar co-data
Pending 0.1.16 source adds the existing native joint_noise_ml profile to single-/multiple-set co-data. Use coData$globalMode="joint_noise_ml" and explicit varianceRatioBounds=c(.01,100), omitting ve. Supplied ve, globalVariance and varianceBounds are rejected in this mode rather than ignored. Existing fixed and known-noise modes still require positive ve. The method/algorithm remain marker_gaussian/gaussian; top-level updateE is not an alternative selector.
Native fitting first estimates y ~ N(0, s I + t Z Z’) on the saved transformed design. It searches log(r=s/t) within the closed supplied bounds, profiling s=y’(I+ZZ’/r)^(-1)y/n and t=s/r and checking endpoints. The objective is the full normalized Gaussian marginal negative log likelihood. This is zero-mean ML, not REML or an intercept/nuisance fit. Ratio bounds follow supplied feature units; they do not bound the two variances separately. The existing top-level global search controls govern this stage; tuning and setWeights controls retain their separate roles.
The learned residual/global pair is fixed before group moments, split tuning, set weighting and the final fit. All annotation sets receive the same pair, with no per-set or subsequent residual refit. The final annotated prior is not necessarily the initial global variance. Actual residual/global values, estimated flags, ratio and search objective/status/boundary are saved; per-set flags are FALSE. input\(varianceLearning and the common descriptor record the one-time stage
and actual likelihood variance, with resolved learning\)updateE=TRUE. Gaussian counts include native profile evaluations, identification and its intermediate ordinary-Gaussian fit; no extra profile is run to create diagnostics.
Native identification rejects zero outcomes, zero designs and transformed Gram matrices proportional to identity at its 64-epsilon shape threshold. Nearly unidentified profiles can remain broad. The assembly does not expose that primitive shape statistic, and R does not recompute it. Quota exhaustion returns no accepted fit. Native numeric admission and dense-dual limitations remain. This bounded profile is not an unrestricted global certificate or full original ecpc optimizer reproduction.
Residual variance uses outcome-squared units; effects/global coefficient prior retain supplied transformed-feature units. No centering, intercept, probability or posterior-uncertainty interpretation changes. Saved prediction never uses target outcomes or re-estimates variances. Sampling variance remains a frozen- parameter estimator diagnostic. Patient CV and joint/summary co-data are still separate. Focused developer reference checks pass in gbayes 0.1.16. Focused references pass in the 0.1.16 developer checkpoint.


Supplied-fold co-data initialization with gscore selection
Development gbayes 0.1.16 adds public co_data_cv_statistics; gscore 0.1.2 adds co_data_cv. Selection and refit orchestration stay in gscore. All fold, variance-profile and final annotation fitting stay in gbayes, using the existing native Gaussian ridge CV primitive and scalar co-data fitters. No solver, sampler, task-neutral computation or second selector framework is introduced. The new explicit R workflow dependency is optional gscore -> gbayes; gbayes does not depend on root gsuite or call gscore for fitting.
The selected target is the ordinary-ridge initial ratio, not CV of the final annotated empirical-Bayes model. Supply complete scalar outer-training data, labelled real/CSC X, sample-named integer patient folds exhausting 1:F, and positive unique candidate penalties. Optional patient clusters cannot cross folds; they govern splitting, not loss weights or residual covariance. Frozen external coding must be declared with cvControl$preprocessing=“externally_frozen”. Neither package learns fold-specific transforms or accepts outer test outcomes. Caller preprocessing provenance cannot be verified automatically.
The native normal_equation_ratio profile uses each candidate directly. The separate glmnet_4_1_1_gaussian profile uses n_train*lambda/RMS(y_train), with zero intercept/feature standardization and native rejection of nonzero constant training columns. Fold losses are SSE and row-weighted MSE including unequal fold sizes; optional OOF predictions are tuning outputs, not outer performance. A held-out prediction uses only its fold-training outcomes. No automatic paths, random folds, one-standard-error rule, candidate averaging or full-model nested CV is added.
The existing native primitive also profiles a provisional winning candidate. gscore independently selects minimum reported MSE (largest penalty on exact ties), verifies that index/penalty before reuse, then calls public gbayes::bayes at the frozen selected pair. A disagreement fails before annotation refitting; native provisional choice and its ordinary-Gaussian final work are not hidden. Known noise s gives t=s/ratio; optional estimateNoise profiles s at that selected ratio on full training data, then t=s/ratio. This fixed-ratio scale estimate can admit an identity Gram, unlike free joint_noise_ml variance identification.
The final single-/multiple-set co-data fit receives exactly the same frozen coding and pair. Fixed or saved feature-group split penalties compose with it; patient folds and feature-group equation splits remain distinct. Omit prior initializer modes/variances/bounds and fitControl\(coding to avoid ignored inputs.
Result\)fit is the ordinary common bayesfit; its flags describe the conditional fixed-pair fit. Earlier CV/noise profiling remains in gscore selection metadata, including fold/cluster identities, candidates/losses, penalty profile, work and owner version. fit\(provenance\)selection preserves that metadata if saving the fit alone. Common effect units, uncertainty limits and frozen prediction remain.
CV and final-fit numeric bounds are stage-specific, not a combined RSS ceiling. Native dense-dual planning includes optional retained predictions and work caps; incomplete CV or an invalid final co-data fit yields no workflow result. Focused developer reference checks pass in gbayes 0.1.16. Independent references pass in the focused gbayes 0.1.16 / gscore 0.1.2 developer checkpoint. Full-model CV and fold-learned coding remain planned.

The small script supplies correlated genotypes to gsim(W = ...); gsim generates the effects and phenotypes. This artificial LD construction is not a demographic simulation. It provides differing LD scores without reference data downloads. Marginal regressions are calculated separately in the two disjoint GWAS samples. Their t statistics are supplied as z statistics, using the large-sample approximation. All marker identities and allele directions are aligned by construction; no harmonization is needed for this generated example.
The reference is prepared once as a separate LDlist, saved and reloaded. All three regional methods reuse its cached eigensystems. LD files remain unchanged during fitting. Every within-region correlation is retained; regions are treated as independent chromosomes for LD preparation.

title: gcorr method comparison: simulated results
text:
What counts as truth?
The effect draw does not have to reproduce its generating correlation exactly. For this draw, the population h2 values are 0.299 and 0.395, and the genetic correlation is 0.540, rather than the generating value of 0.60.
Truth is calculated from the realized gsim effects and the known population covariance of the genotype generator, not from the estimated reference LD. After converting standardized effects to raw-dosage effects, for region \(r\):
\[
G_r = B_r^\mathsf{T}\Sigma_r B_r,
\qquad (\Sigma_r)_{jk}=2(0.3)(0.7)\rho_r^{|j-k|}.
\]
The regions are independent, so \(G=\sum_r G_r\). Total phenotypic variances combine its diagonal with gsim’s residual variances. Regional covariance is scaled by the square root of the two total phenotypic variances; it is not a within-region genetic correlation. The script also checks that the effect conversion reproduces gsim’s individual genetic values.

Recorded results
The published figure and result table preserve the reviewed single-run and 20-replicate outcomes. They are not regenerated during website rendering. Current executable validation uses the gcorr package tests and binary-package workflow.
The website displays a reviewed figure and result table. Rendering it does not run the simulation. See the saved-LD workflow and method capabilities for the broader interface and limitations.
This demonstrates a working analysis chain and provides a small repeated comparison under one deliberately simple design. The observed coverage counts do not establish general calibration, realistic genetic architecture or equivalence to every option in the original software packages.

title: Direct genotype-to-score and SumHer workflow
text:
This development workflow connects genotype-derived LD scores to bounded SumHer heritability and genetic-correlation fits. It is not included in the current public source archives. The statistical and release limits below remain part of the interface contract.










Responsibility
Native owner
Standalone R interface




Direct BED-to-LD scores
gmat: ldscore_sumher_style()
gbase: gprep(task = "ldscores")


GWAS
glma (existing route)
glma (existing route)


Bounded paired SumHer fit
gcorr: fit_sumher_ldak_style()
gcorr: gcorr(Glist, stat, method = "sumher")


Dense eigensystem
gsolve (existing public API)
Internal dependency



The root gsuite R integration and existing gcorr_sumher() are unchanged. The new fitter’s regression, jackknife and derived estimates run in C++. R validates labels and shapes and packages native output.



Run LD once per reference cohort and annotation definition, save it, and reuse it across phenotype cases. Cache provenance must include the genotype selection, annotation, powers, window and correction settings.
library(gbase)
library(gcorr)
# Set the configured BLAS library to one thread before starting R when using
# multiple OpenMP workers (e.g. MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 or OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1).
Glist <- gprep(bedfiles = c("chr1.bed", "chr2.bed"))
ids <- unlist(Glist$rsids, use.names = FALSE)
annotation <- matrix(1, length(ids), 1,
                     dimnames = list(ids, "Base"))
Glist <- gprep(Glist, task = "ldscores", annotation = annotation,
               window_cm = 1, min_r2 = 0, nthreads = 4)
ld <- Glist$ldscore_models
saveRDS(Glist, "cohort_sumher_reference.rds")

# After GWAS: stat1/stat2 contain rsids, chr, pos, ea, nea, n and
# b/seb (or a signed Z column named stat).
statistics <- lapply(list(trait1 = stat1, trait2 = stat2), function(s)
  checkStat(Glist, stat = s))

# Marker sets and row order may differ after QC. gcorr matches them internally.
fit <- gcorr(Glist, statistics, method = "sumher")
fit$h2
fit$h2_se
fit$rg
fit$rg_se
stopifnot(all(fit$diagnostics$converged))
fit$estimates
For multiple bins, supply their marker-by-bin annotation columns in place of the Base column and preserve their order. Do not combine a Base column with an exhaustive set of bins unless the intended model includes that redundant design. For exact parity using a printed LDAK tagging file, use its printed scores, tagging and contribution footer together; direct full-precision scores and footer values can follow different iterative trajectories.



The default uses the bounded marginal and paired continuous-trait stages, with additive intercepts, estimated pairwise overlap, and no genomic control or regression cutoff. Signed corrected LD scores are allowed. Tagging is floored at one during fitting. Delete blocks are consecutive in supplied marker order; final weights are frozen. Undefined rg and SE values remain undefined, and nonconvergence remains flagged. The default limit permits 101 updates, matching the frozen workflow convention.
The earlier cluster study validated the experimental LD implementation and R fitter. It reported 4318 converged fits out of 4320, with two failed solver stages. Those data are not a full qualification of this new native fitter. Retain both difficult cases when checking the port; do not silently accept their raw estimates or loosen tolerances to manufacture agreement.



These are development source additions. Source commits do not publish R archives or website snapshots. Native CMake lists include the new implementations, so the source-package builder extracts them from their owners. gbase’s generated build flags now include R’s BLAS and Fortran link libraries.
Focused verification and current local toolchain limitations are recorded in the review record (unpublished development review). Before release, use the complete canonical dependency checkouts and qualified prefix, run the focused native CTest targets and R package tests, then run the saved cluster fitter/LD parity cases. Review package versions, ABI requirements and generated source archives before publishing. This proposal leaves existing release version numbers and native qualification manifest constraints unchanged.



gprep(Glist, task = "ldscores") returns the existing descriptor with ldscore_models containing the score array, tagging, expected heritability and resolved settings. Defaults are a 1 Mb physical window, no marker-distance limit, min_r2 = 0, U/D powers, finite-sample correction and Hardy-Weinberg heritability variance. To reproduce the imported cM workflow, set window_cm = 1; cM and nonzero physical/marker windows cannot be combined. All-zero genetic maps do not represent meaningful cM windows.
min_r2 is the preferred name; r2 remains a compatibility alias and supplying both is an error. Existing sparse-LD defaults remain 1 Mb, 1000 markers and 0.01. The historical msize-only sparse call still sets its cutoff to zero. The direct-score cutoff filters architecture scores; tagging and neighbour counts still include all in-window polymorphic pairs.
write_ld = FALSE does not write pairwise LD. Existing sparse resources on the supplied descriptor are preserved. With physical/marker windows, write_ld = TRUE and out_prefix also construct the existing sparse resource in a separate pass. This writer does not support cM windows; such requests are rejected rather than silently substituting a physical window. The former standalone R score entry point is removed; the native gmat API remains available.
The established Glist$ldscores field remains a per-component list of ordinary uncorrected scores. Direct model arrays and metadata are in Glist$ldscore_models. If an existing sparse resource is retained, its ordinary score fields remain unchanged and the new direct model results are separate.
Ordinary compatibility scores retain a unit self-contribution for monomorphic markers, matching the sparse writer. Their architecture-score and tagging contributions remain zero under the direct SumHer formulas.



Use gcorr(..., method = "sumher"). The default fitter selects the stored D model when available, or the sole model in a single-model cache. Thus gcorr(Glist, stat, method = "sumher") needs no additional selector arguments for the ordinary U/D cache. Select score_model = "U" to request the Uniform model. Other multiple-model caches require an explicit choice. The previous estimator and illustrative ordinary score baseline remain available with sumher_fitter = "standard". The default returns h2 per trait and, for multiple traits, rg for every pair. The newly introduced focused paired-fit R export is removed. Existing gcorr_sumher() remains available as a compatibility entry point for the standard fitter.
The stored workflow automatically intersects markers shared by all traits and the score reference, restoring reference order for both checked frames and named Z/N matrices. No manual intersection/reordering step is needed. Checked frames must have unique IDs and matching coordinates/alleles on the retained markers. Keep checkStat() for reference allele harmonization and QC. Diagnostics record input and omitted marker counts per trait. Annotation contribution totals use the entire stored reference, including SNPs with no regression statistics; they are not recalculated on the regression subset. The bounded fitter defaults to min(200, retained markers) consecutive delete blocks, absolute tolerance 1e-4 and maximum_iterations 100 (up to 101 updates). Use num_blocks to override the block count; arbitrary labels, standard-fitter inflation controls and genomic control are not accepted by this route.
It returns gcorr_sumher_ldak_fit, with metric-labelled estimates, standard errors, delete estimates, convergence diagnostics, the selected model and score provenance. This is deliberately distinct from gcorr_sumher_fit; the standard fitter’s category/joint-covariance adapters do not automatically apply to the bounded port.
For imported scores and a supplied contribution footer, omit Glist and pass architecture_ld_scores, tagging, and component_contributions through gcorr(statistics, method = "sumher", sumher_fitter = "ldak", ...). These explicit inputs retain the paired fitter’s validation and default count of 200 blocks; set num_blocks for smaller inputs.



The normal call is fit <- gcorr(Glist, stat, method = "sumher"). Read fit$h2 and fit$h2_se for named trait heritabilities. With multiple traits, fit$rg and fit$rg_se are symmetric trait-labelled matrices. A single-trait fit evaluates only its marginal h2/intercept stage; it does not duplicate the trait or compute an artificial correlation. For three or more traits the workflow fits all unique pairs, deduplicates partner-independent marginal results and retains fit$pairwise. fit$computation records repeated marginal and pair evaluation counts. Pairwise estimates are not a joint likelihood or a positive-semidefinite genetic covariance constraint. Undefined rg/SE and nonconvergence remain explicit. All fits use the same retained marker universe and consecutive block scheme.

title: Direct genotype-to-score and SumHer workflow
text:
Run LD once per reference cohort and annotation definition, save it, and reuse it across phenotype cases. Cache provenance must include the genotype selection, annotation, powers, window and correction settings.
library(gbase)
library(gcorr)
# Set the configured BLAS library to one thread before starting R when using
# multiple OpenMP workers (e.g. MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 or OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1).
Glist <- gprep(bedfiles = c("chr1.bed", "chr2.bed"))
ids <- unlist(Glist$rsids, use.names = FALSE)
annotation <- matrix(1, length(ids), 1,
                     dimnames = list(ids, "Base"))
Glist <- gprep(Glist, task = "ldscores", annotation = annotation,
               window_cm = 1, min_r2 = 0, nthreads = 4)
ld <- Glist$ldscore_models
saveRDS(Glist, "cohort_sumher_reference.rds")

# After GWAS: stat1/stat2 contain rsids, chr, pos, ea, nea, n and
# b/seb (or a signed Z column named stat).
statistics <- lapply(list(trait1 = stat1, trait2 = stat2), function(s)
  checkStat(Glist, stat = s))

# Marker sets and row order may differ after QC. gcorr matches them internally.
fit <- gcorr(Glist, statistics, method = "sumher")
fit$h2
fit$h2_se
fit$rg
fit$rg_se
stopifnot(all(fit$diagnostics$converged))
fit$estimates
For multiple bins, supply their marker-by-bin annotation columns in place of the Base column and preserve their order. Do not combine a Base column with an exhaustive set of bins unless the intended model includes that redundant design. For exact parity using a printed LDAK tagging file, use its printed scores, tagging and contribution footer together; direct full-precision scores and footer values can follow different iterative trajectories.

title: Direct genotype-to-score and SumHer workflow
text:

Undefined rg and SE values remain undefined, and nonconvergence remains flagged. The default limit permits 101 updates, matching the frozen workflow convention.
The earlier cluster study validated the experimental LD implementation and R fitter. It reported 4318 converged fits out of 4320, with two failed solver stages. Those data are not a full qualification of this new native fitter. Retain both difficult cases when checking the port; do not silently accept their raw estimates or loosen tolerances to manufacture agreement.
