Availability depends on requested route and uncertainty; do not infer it from a method name alone


Balanced/record longitudinal
gs_longitudinal_rhe(), gs_longitudinal_reml(), gs_longitudinal_blup()
Explain which estimation procedure ran and which results are valid






Use CHOLMOD with selected inversion as the reference configuration for the new sparse-direct model examples. Selecting CHOLMOD alone is insufficient: coordinate tracing can still do many solves. The three pedigree tutorial models already select linear_solver = "sparse_direct", direct_backend = "cholmod", exact_trace_method = "selected_inverse". The general formula adapter and compiled-control constructor now follow this default; explicit solver choices remain authoritative.
The source currently differs from that policy:

General pedigree formulas default to sparse direct, CHOLMOD and selected inversion. Explicit alternative backends use coordinate tracing unless the caller requests another trace method; unsupported requests are not repaired.
The four specialized pedigree control constructors default to PCG, automatic backend and coordinate tracing.
Compiled gs_fit_control() defaults to CHOLMOD and selected inversion. Its selected-inversion argument is trace_route, not exact_trace_method.
gs_lmm_control() already defaults to CHOLMOD. Its public signature does not expose the native component PCG/stochastic/adaptive controls; those native capabilities are a separate R-exposure gap.
Dense exact and matrix-free covariance routes are different algorithms; a global CHOLMOD substitution is not applicable to them.

Keep explicit solver choices and clear errors when requested CHOLMOD support is unavailable. Specialized low-level control defaults remain separate. The timing difference observed in the tutorial is not evidence that one backend is universally faster for every model and workload.



Use 10,000 animals/individuals as the default demonstration size for scalable routes, with trait and observation counts stated separately. Tiny deterministic oracle tests remain tiny; dense reference routes and bounded uncertainty targets should not automatically be expanded to 10K dimensions.
Keep this coverage table as the inventory, the existing pedigree tutorial as the introductory example, and reuse build/examples/ for replaceable runtime outputs. Do not create a folder or a dated report for each attempted fit. Promote only selected, reviewed figures and concise results to website sources.
Check each recipe in this order: expressibility through exported R functions, correct model/ID mapping, convergence, result extraction, then agreement with an existing equivalent route or appropriate reference. Passing one example does not requalify every covariance/backend combination.

Specialized repeatability uncertainty integration, only if that public convenience route must expose the existing complete-MME machinery rather than using the qualified component recipe.
A genuinely unsupported residual family or prediction contract selected from the catalog, implemented through the existing component and residual abstractions rather than a parallel model engine.

These candidates have no committed implementation schedule. Qualification work should be chosen only when the corresponding public combination is useful.
Scientific recipes and covariance definitions are summarized in model recipes; they do not assign qualification status.



greml::GxeMomentCache implements bounded native moment summaries for V=theta_g K+theta_I D_e K D_e+theta_N D_e^2+theta_e I with supplied e=E alpha. It retains ordinary fixed projection, raw estimates, rank/conditioning and probe MCSE, with a separate phenotype summary. The independent references and matched memory/runtime evidence are recorded in the owner contract (unpublished greml contract). This is a numerical research capability, not a scientifically calibrated variance estimator, learned-score fit, SNP interaction test, prediction workflow, R/YAML interface, production qualification or release. Existing longitudinal/FA failures remain recorded.
The fixed-design Gaussian scientific study (unpublished greml research report) adds conditional moment-recovery and projected-identifiability evidence without changing the native route. Weak relationships, aliases and projection can prevent useful interaction/noise separation. Oracle sampling covariance agrees with replication; exploratory applied plug-in intervals do not establish calibrated uncertainty. General sampling inference and learned-score fitting remain unqualified; the recommendation from that study was targeted uncertainty validation first.
The subsequent native sampling_covariance method provides the complete Gaussian quadratic covariance and its propagation at an explicit working state, with separate numerical trace MCSE. Its sufficient SPD certificate requires nonnegative components and positive residual variance; signed raw states are not repaired or assumed indefinite. Rank aliases and indefinite estimated trace covariances return explicit unavailable results. See the contract (unpublished greml contract) and uncertainty evidence (unpublished greml research report). This bounded implementation does not itself select a working estimator, qualify applied coverage, or authorize learned-score inference or release.
A research comparison of practical uncertainty (unpublished greml research report) retains the same full-data estimates and assesses GENIE-style genomic deletion over frozen 40-window LD panels. All-window jackknife availability does not establish interval calibration: additive and interaction-plus-noise targets undercover, with strong block-structure sensitivity. No general uncertainty procedure, production jackknife API, learned-score qualification or release is established.




The public capability implements the GENIE estimator. Method/software attribution and the existing native API names are retained.
Implemented and numerically compared; partial method support; unreleased. greml::GenieMomentCache implements separate G, per-exposure GxE/NxE and residual components, matched Gaussian-probe moment equations, trace-weighted fractions and full genomic delete-block jackknife. Dense references and unchanged pinned GENIE agree on validated full-rank SPD systems; source/precision conventions and legacy multi-exposure output labels are documented. Exact published testing-tail provenance, annotation/enrichment support, missing-data parity and original QR rank behavior remain incomplete. Contract (unpublished greml contract) and evidence (unpublished greml research report) distinguish these states. No R/YAML frontend, learned score or general performance/scientific qualification is claimed. Prior fixed-score uncertainty and longitudinal/FA/ARG limits remain.



Implemented and numerically/reference-software validated for the documented native route; unreleased. Binary annotation/block covariances and intersection counts support partitioned and unpartitioned G+GxE+NxE moments, overlap-category fractions/enrichments and complete jackknife covariance. Default reference QR admits indefinite and deficient basic solutions with rank/identification metadata; checked-SPD remains an explicit choice, and other methods retain their defaults. Published-result genome-wide two-sided and conditional annotation upper-tail zero-null conventions are reconstructed from original tables, with provenance limits recorded. See the contract (unpublished greml contract) and evidence (unpublished greml research report). This extends the earlier genome-wide entry; it adds no R/YAML, automatic annotation construction, missing-data parity, general scientific/performance qualification or release.




Implemented and mathematically/reference-software validated for the documented native route; unreleased. G, G+GxE and G+GxE+NxE reuse the same annotation kernels, moment/solver choices and complete genomic jackknife. Explicit masks preserve full-sample transforms/probe order; native preparation handles the source phenotype/exposure/covariate conventions and HWE marker completion. This later extension supersedes earlier model-subset and missing-data exclusions for the supplied aligned, full-rank-intercept route. See the owner contract (unpublished greml contract) and correctness evidence (unpublished greml research report). No original wall-clock RNG replay, automatic identity matching/filtering, other frontend, R/YAML, general scientific/performance qualification or release is claimed.



Implemented native application route; unreleased and not generally qualified. gsuite_model_driver gxe binds real BED/keyed-table inputs to the existing GENIE estimator for G, G+G×E and G+G×E+NxE, including supplied binary annotations. It adds explicit alignment/QC, seeded frozen completion, genomic-block inputs, resource guards and full/deletion output. The underlying numerical route and historical qualification limits remain unchanged. See the adapter contract (unpublished greml contract); a real-data scientific or large-scale acceptance result is not claimed by implementation alone.



Implemented and independently numerically validated native research primitive; scientifically unqualified; unreleased. GxeMomentCache::score_objective and fit_score add a complete projected finite-probe objective/analytical gradient and unregularized alternating score fit. Returned coefficients match the final score; rank, stationarity, small-step stagnation and iteration limits remain explicit. This is not complete ENGINE parity: no regularization, cross-fitting, post-learning uncertainty, new R/YAML/file interface or scale qualification. The prior fixed-score/GENIE scientific evidence and limitations remain intact.



Implemented and independently numerically validated native research route; scientifically unqualified; unreleased. fit_score_regularized adds spherical threshold schedules; gxe_variant_split_plan/fit_score_variant_split add disjoint mean-normalized marker halves, swapped evaluation, sign alignment and separate held-out/full estimates. Existing GENIE and disabled-threshold results are preserved. No SE-dependent coefficient gate, learned-score uncertainty, automatic tuning, new frontend or broad empirical/scaling qualification is added.



Implemented and independently numerically validated native research primitives; unreleased and scientifically unqualified. The separate greml inference API supports smooth local geometry, explicit probe-only delta propagation, source conditional-SE gating and paired S2 tests from complete observation-group refits. Literal and component-scale pseudo-values are distinguished; conventional component covariance is limited to equal groups. This does not provide a generally valid analytic SE for regularized data-learned scores or the unverified original component-null test. GENIE and earlier point-estimation/uncertainty qualifications remain intact.



fit_gxe_score_inference implements complete full/deletion refit orchestration for supplied kernels and y/E/C, reusing regularization, variant splits and S2 paired inference. Shared sample/group identity and compact convergence/failure records replace manual deletion-cache plumbing. Fixed genotype transformations, declared preprocessing/baseline and valid observation-group assumptions define the route. It remains scientifically unqualified and unreleased; original selected-component null testing and general analytic learned-score SEs are not claimed. Earlier primitive/GENIE qualifications remain preserved.
The complete native refit workflow passed 11 native and 14 installed full/core checks on 27 October 2026, including independent dense mathematical references. It is implemented and independently numerically validated, scientifically unqualified and unreleased. See the evidence/limits; earlier qualification evidence is retained.



The optional gsuite_model_driver engine route now binds BED/keyed tables to the existing native ENGINE-attributed inference workflow. It uses explicit observation groups, starts and baseline weights; supplied exposure/baseline scales and full-FAM genotype transforms stay fixed on deletion. GENIE input infrastructure and packed operators are reused without changing their methods. This is a bounded native file capability, scientifically unqualified and unreleased; original null-test, calibration and scaling limits remain intact. No new R/YAML or public launcher route is claimed.
The native ENGINE file adapter passed 13 native and 14 installed full/core checks on 27 October 2026, plus installed single/split command replay and licence refusal. Independent dense arithmetic maximum scaled error was 1.18e-13. It is implemented and independently numerically validated for this bounded route, scientifically unqualified and unreleased. See the evidence/limits; earlier qualifications remain preserved.

greml::GxeMomentCache implements bounded native moment summaries for V=theta_g K+theta_I D_e K D_e+theta_N D_e^2+theta_e I with supplied e=E alpha. It retains ordinary fixed projection, raw estimates, rank/conditioning and probe MCSE, with a separate phenotype summary. The independent references and matched memory/runtime evidence are recorded in the owner contract (unpublished greml contract). This is a numerical research capability, not a scientifically calibrated variance estimator, learned-score fit, SNP interaction test, prediction workflow, R/YAML interface, production qualification or release. Existing longitudinal/FA failures remain recorded.
The fixed-design Gaussian scientific study (unpublished greml research report) adds conditional moment-recovery and projected-identifiability evidence without changing the native route. Weak relationships, aliases and projection can prevent useful interaction/noise separation. Oracle sampling covariance agrees with replication; exploratory applied plug-in intervals do not establish calibrated uncertainty. General sampling inference and learned-score fitting remain unqualified; the recommendation from that study was targeted uncertainty validation first.
The subsequent native sampling_covariance method provides the complete Gaussian quadratic covariance and its propagation at an explicit working state, with separate numerical trace MCSE. Its sufficient SPD certificate requires nonnegative components and positive residual variance; signed raw states are not repaired or assumed indefinite. Rank aliases and indefinite estimated trace covariances return explicit unavailable results. See the contract (unpublished greml contract) and uncertainty evidence (unpublished greml research report). This bounded implementation does not itself select a working estimator, qualify applied coverage, or authorize learned-score inference or release.
A research comparison of practical uncertainty (unpublished greml research report) retains the same full-data estimates and assesses GENIE-style genomic deletion over frozen 40-window LD panels. All-window jackknife availability does not establish interval calibration: additive and interaction-plus-noise targets undercover, with strong block-structure sensitivity. No general uncertainty procedure, production jackknife API, learned-score qualification or release is established.

The separate greml inference API supports smooth local geometry, explicit probe-only delta propagation, source conditional-SE gating and paired S2 tests from complete observation-group refits. Literal and component-scale pseudo-values are distinguished; conventional component covariance is limited to equal groups. This does not provide a generally valid analytic SE for regularized data-learned scores or the unverified original component-null test. GENIE and earlier point-estimation/uncertainty qualifications remain intact.



fit_gxe_score_inference implements complete full/deletion refit orchestration for supplied kernels and y/E/C, reusing regularization, variant splits and S2 paired inference. Shared sample/group identity and compact convergence/failure records replace manual deletion-cache plumbing. Fixed genotype transformations, declared preprocessing/baseline and valid observation-group assumptions define the route. It remains scientifically unqualified and unreleased; original selected-component null testing and general analytic learned-score SEs are not claimed. Earlier primitive/GENIE qualifications remain preserved.
The complete native refit workflow passed 11 native and 14 installed full/core checks on 27 October 2026, including independent dense mathematical references. It is implemented and independently numerically validated, scientifically unqualified and unreleased. See the evidence/limits; earlier qualification evidence is retained.



The optional gsuite_model_driver engine route now binds BED/keyed tables to the existing native ENGINE-attributed inference workflow. It uses explicit observation groups, starts and baseline weights; supplied exposure/baseline scales and full-FAM genotype transforms stay fixed on deletion. GENIE input infrastructure and packed operators are reused without changing their methods. This is a bounded native file capability, scientifically unqualified and unreleased; original null-test, calibration and scaling limits remain intact. No new R/YAML or public launcher route is claimed.
The native ENGINE file adapter passed 13 native and 14 installed full/core checks on 27 October 2026, plus installed single/split command replay and licence refusal. Independent dense arithmetic maximum scaled error was 1.18e-13. It is implemented and independently numerically validated for this bounded route, scientifically unqualified and unreleased. See the evidence/limits; earlier qualifications remain preserved.

title: Methods reference
text:
Technical detail and qualification notes supporting the methods overview. Use the overview to choose a starting point; use this page for implementation contracts, route-specific limitations and evidence links.
This catalogue maps development capabilities to their owning repository. Implemented means the capability is implemented in development code and exercised by relevant repository validation; it does not claim production-scale qualification. Experimental identifies a present but deliberately provisional integration surface. Planned identifies work with no current implementation. Availability through R is stated separately. Seven standalone genomic R packages are public source releases. Mixed-model and solver examples use the development integration; greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred, and a root gsuite R release is not currently planned.
The connected genomic example exercises representative routes across six modules using one 10K-individual, 50K-marker simulation. Its qualification record distinguishes execution checks and truth comparisons from untested capabilities.
The standalone command is gsuite run model.yml for both solving and REML. It calls the native gsuite_model_driver executable. The greml and gsolve library names identify their mixed-model and numerical-solver responsibilities; they are not separate user commands. Existing R interfaces are unchanged.

title: Methods reference
text:
Capability overview
Request management is separate from scientific capabilities: the local service collects email-verified reports for maintainer review. Optional preparation takes place in the user’s own assistant; submission calls no models, qualifies no method and authorizes no development. Public hosting remains a separate launch step.
The native conditional ssSNPBLUP PCG route optionally replaces its full non-genotyped pedigree factor with an ancestral factor plus exact pedigree sweeps. This preserves the supplied covariance model and all individual coefficients. Supplied metafounder models additionally retain every correlated latent base in the small factor. Native dense-oracle checks and the ordinary saved 50K comparison are described in the factor-reduction study. The YAML frontend selects this opt-in route with execution.pedigree_factorization: ancestral_sweeps; existing R interfaces remain unchanged. The source bundle includes a complete GenomeDK 1M/16-thread model.
The experimental compact YAML frontend supports supplied-covariance multitrait pedigree, packed ssSNPBLUP and joint polynomial random-regression models with named input/effect mappings. It includes model inspection and labelled coefficient/curve predictions. Wide and long phenotype input preserves residual covariance within explicit measurement IDs, including missing traits and irregular visits. The long-input example (models/multitrait-single-step-long.yml) uses the same supplied-covariance model as the wide five-trait example. Preparation spools source rows and normalized occasions to temporary SQLite storage, and streams record prediction grids through prepared JSONL files. The optional execution.preparation.directory selects existing scratch space. Small storage tests check bounded retained Python row memory, cleanup and prediction-file integrity; pedigree/effect-level indexes and dense supplied matrices remain in memory. This is not industrial parser-memory qualification. Small independent dense-equation comparisons cover the adapters. Genetic channels can use separate incidence IDs within one shared relationship and joint covariance, including direct/maternal models. The complete example (models/direct-maternal-single-step.yml) reports direct and maternal coefficients separately and their mapped record contributions. This is supplied-covariance prediction; it adds no REML or PEV precision work. Selected ordinary packed genetic values additionally support exact PEV, prediction-error standard errors and reliability conditional on supplied covariances, with explicit solve-work caps and dense-inverse checks. Larger target sets can use variance-reduced stochastic PEV or prior-minus-posterior information probing with explicit probe/solve budgets, MCSE and separate prediction/uncertainty acceptance. A local 50K study measures overhead and precision; it does not establish industrial uncertainty throughput or calibration. The matched information-probing comparison uses the same posterior query budget and reports additional prior-product work. Stochastic PEV also supports trait-isolated residual probes at fixed query cost, with MCSE over complete independent groups. This removes cross-trait noise but reduces the independent sample count; its benefit is model-dependent. The fixed-budget 50K comparison records grouped MCSE, exact-target errors, runtime and memory. At 32 posterior solves, trait isolation worsened median MCSE and the eight-target exact error on this fixture; unstructured probing remains the default. Neither plan met the population-wide precision requirement at that budget. REML, broader uncertainty targets and industrial parser-memory qualification remain outside this frontend. The interface additionally supports supplied dense relationship covariance, fixed interactions, composite random-effect groups, Legendre/Chebyshev bases, group-specific trait residual covariance and univariate AR1 or continuous-time exponential residuals on the compiled route. Packed ssSNPBLUP also supports univariate AR1/exponential covariance through exact sparse Markov innovations; actual observed gaps, missing visits and singleton series retain their supplied covariance model. The AR1 (models/single-step-ar1.yml) and exponential (models/single-step-exponential.yml) examples include complete PLINK/YAML workflows. Grouped residual covariance also uses the existing ssSNPBLUP prepared-record path. Independent small dense references check the new compiled routes; this does not qualify their large-data memory use or new combinations of covariance structures. AR1/exponential residuals can also use a supplied trait covariance times a common time correlation. Compiled and packed prediction routes prepare exact conditional innovations over observed traits, preserving marginal covariance with intermittent missing measurements. The multivariate AR1 example (models/multitrait-single-step-ar1.yml) includes PLINK inputs and covariance matrices. Small dense references check wide/long data, irregular gaps and both packed pedigree factors/preconditioners. No dense time-series covariance is prepared; sparse filter design history may grow within incomplete series. Serial REML and industrial multivariate preparation throughput remain outside this qualification. Random-effect channel covariance also accepts supplied factor loadings and positive specific variances, giving K = Lambda Lambda' + diag(psi). Compiled FA1/FA2 models reuse native FA parameterization; packed ssSNPBLUP uses the same validated implied channel covariance. Environment-labelled long input represents genetic covariance across environments, with separate fixed coefficients per declared channel. Small independent dense references check coefficients and equivalent unstructured models, including partial genotyping and both pedigree factors/preconditioners. The multi-environment example (models/multienvironment-factor-analytic.yml) supplies all inputs. This adds prediction with supplied FA parameters; YAML FA estimation, uncertainty and industrial scaling remain unqualified. The simulator and user-data commands share this one YAML schema; numerical controls are specified in its execution block.
Supplied-genomic ssGBLUP is available through compiled PCG, with either a dense effective G covariance or explicit APY core/cross covariance blocks and marginal variances. Native greml retains exact marginal pedigree precision and applies implicit H; APY is explicitly a genomic covariance approximation. Small dense references and equivalent ssSNPBLUP models check predictions, including mixed genotyping and covariance-base settings. YAML also connects raw PLINK data to native streamed APY preparation, with ordered core IDs, explicit covariance scaling/ridge, bounded decoded tiles and file-backed cross products. Independent small dense equations check missing genotypes, ID mapping, APY predictions and the all-core exact boundary. Preparation avoids full G or decoded-panel storage, but retains quadratic core memory and O(noncore*core) disk. Compiled prediction defaults to omitting unused H covariance diagonals; exact precision diagonals/determinants and the preconditioner are unchanged. execution.relationship_metadata: complete restores exact covariance metadata. Industrial APY throughput remains unqualified; packed ssSNPBLUP retains its separate HPC evidence.
The YAML interface also exposes supplied metafounder Gamma with explicit unknown-parent assignments, or explicit independent random genetic group means. They support pedigree, supplied-genomic ssGBLUP/APY and packed ssSNPBLUP models. Metafounder base covariance and additive group-mean contributions remain distinct. Small independent dense equations check coefficients and predictions, including latent levels and individual a + F gamma reporting. Compiled fixed inherited group contrasts, explicit phantom group-parent absorption and combined metafounder/group models are also exposed. Packed Gamma pseudo-EM requires an explicit absolute marker base and returns conditional predictions at the estimated Gamma. The compiled group adapter materializes ancestry proportions; the packed adapter instead applies native F/F’ sweeps to cached original records and prepares exact group diagonals once with operator probes. Packed groups require matching genetic channels and a final group-mean effect, and support full or ancestral Qnn. Supplied metafounders also support ancestral reduction with their complete correlated base block retained; Gamma and the original covariance model are unchanged. The metafounder reduction study records exact references and the matched 50K comparison. Small dense references check both preconditioners and consistent individual reporting. Their industrial memory/runtime qualification remains separate. Existing R interfaces are unchanged.
The packed pedigree-base study records the focused dense/analytic checks and the 50K fixture measurements. Metafounder factors use an exact diagonal congruence for balance; native sparse verification uses compensated residuals and bounded retained-factor correction when needed. Original model residual thresholds and covariance parameters are unchanged. These workstation measurements do not establish 1M/HPC performance.
The optional standalone HPC ssSNPBLUP prediction frontend accepts supplied variance–covariance matrices, with either independent genomic residual covariance or a pedigree A22 blend. The source-only blend adapter has a focused dense-model oracle for both packed PCG routes; its representative five-trait workload has no industrial throughput or memory qualification yet. It performs fixed-covariance prediction and adds no REML or R selector. See the profile settings and limits.
Native greml has a separate opt-in two-component genomic REML route: generic PCG trace/AI identities and analytical profiling of the common variance scale for V = g K + e I. It supports a zero-eligible genetic component and positive residual, with explicit stationarity and numerical/stochastic precision gates. This development C++ interface has no new R selector; fixed absolute variances, general multi-component profiling and large-panel performance qualification remain outside its scope.
Scalar individual BED BayesC/BayesR in standalone gbayes expose opt-in scheduled marker updates, exact scheduler-state continuation, and realized genetic variance decomposition (Vg = VLE + VLD). Scheduling approximates full-sweep sampling; negative LD contributions are valid. Per-chain full-sweep variance and mixture traces preserve burn-in separately from post-burnin means. See the controls and interpretation. Their fit$posterior table includes VG, VLE, VLD and draw-wise heritability, with native uncertainty and convergence summaries.

Binary logistic tests do not adjust for relatedness | | Genomic scoring and posterior prediction | gscore, model-fitting packages | gscore(weights, Glist) applies portable allele-labelled weights and can accumulate overlapping, cross-file marker-set scores from Glist-resolved marker names. clump_threshold(stat, Glist) constructs conventional C+T weights from reported association effects and prepared sparse LD. glma, gbayes and other model owners fit their statistical effects. It consumes ordinary checked summary-statistics data frames and Glist sparse LD and provides LD-aware weighted quadratic tests. prepare_vegas() computes eigenvalue-only spectra in bounded parallel batches and returns a serializable object reusable across traits and sessions; gsea_input() validates the gene-labelled enrichment handoff. ACAT remains native-only. Default tails are approximate except for equal positive eigenvalues; the controlled positive-series evaluator reports accuracy and term-budget failures | | Gene-set, genomic-feature and gene-prioritization analysis | gsea | gsea() provides ORA, preranked GSEA, competitive GLS, bounded MAGMA and optional scalar/multitrait Bayesian pathway regression. Familiar magma() arguments adapt the existing competitive/Bayesian engines. pops() fits chromosome-held-out ridge, BayesC or BayesR regression and returns feature-based gene rankings with compact per-fold posteriors; marginal selection is optional for Bayesian fits. Explicit universe/set preparation, native aggregate/block resampling and optional BH/BY adjustment remain available. Pathway and gene-ranking workflow |
The native MAGMA comparison covers SNP-wise mean gene evidence and competitive pathway analysis with MAGMA 1.10 preprocessing. A small pinned comparison checked 40 genes and two pathways. This is not complete MAGMA equivalence: other gene models, rare-variant preprocessing, missing-data handling and singular-matrix pruning remain outside the route. Its controlled tail evaluator may return unavailable for difficult spectra or tails rather than use a silent fallback. Scalar and joint multitrait Bayesian pathway analysis is exposed through gsea(), reusing gbayes for sampling and parameter learning. PoPS-style gene ranking is exposed separately through gsea::pops(). It repeats marginal feature selection and ridge fitting, or native Bayesian regression with optional training-only selection, after excluding each target chromosome, accepts explicit blockwise gene covariance, and returns ranked predictions plus fold and feature diagnostics. It is a focused PoPS-style model rather than a claim of output equivalence to every upstream PoPS preprocessing and locus-reporting step.
Selected native operations remain outside the R bindings, including gscore pseudo-summary generation. The standalone gbayes::gbayes_single_effect() interface exposes fixed-variance single-effect inference from ordinary summary statistics. Checks cover independent small calculations, pinned ACAT comparison and a connected native example, not broad GWAS calibration. glma::vegas() implements native LD-aware quadratic gene evidence from aligned GWAS Z statistics. prepare_vegas() reuses one validated sparse-LD reader and prepares eigenvalue-only gene spectra in bounded parallel batches. Its ordinary R result can be saved and reused across traits, with explicit tail status during evaluation. It also consumes the full regional BED spectra stored by gprep(task="eigen") without repeating decomposition, for constant positive within-set weights. VEGAS selects checked statistic rows by marker ID; extra rows and another row order are accepted, while all prepared markers and their matching reference alleles remain required. The sparse-LD route retains nonuniform weighting. Existing tail defaults and accuracy limits are unchanged. The gsea package re-exports both interfaces and gsea_input() validates the gene-statistic handoff to gsea() without automatic harmonization or inferred cross-gene dependence. Methods that require gene covariance need it supplied separately. ACAT and other gene-evidence combinations remain native-only. Competitive GLS uses supplied gene-covariance blocks; its Student-t inference is a working approximation for non-Gaussian gene scores. It does not claim full MAGMA or Pascal equivalence. Python interfaces remain deferred. Multivariate sampling covariance can be learned only for the shared-LD route with an explicit response cross-product; arbitrary sampling overlap across different LD references remains outside the interface. See the current qualification limits before interpreting capability as validated use.
The gbayes::gbayes() choices include point_normal, continuous_shrinkage, variational and mixture_variational. These retain method-specific controls/results, rather than inheriting all BayesC/BayesR features. gbase::checkStat() provides the shared ordinary summary-statistics preparation step. See the summary interface guide.

title: Methods reference
text:
Pedigree formula workflows
The pedigree tutorial demonstrates the data-frame interface on 10,000 simulated animals. It reuses existing numerical engines:







Formula model
Scope




Pedigree animal model
One or multiple traits; missing responses omitted trait by trait


Genetic random regression
One response, one pedigree effect and homogeneous residuals


Independent components
Multiple pedigree/identity intercepts, including permanent environment and common groups


Correlated channels
One response with named channels under a shared kernel, such as direct/maternal effects


Structured residuals
Grouped variances, integer-gap AR(1), or continuous-time exponential correlation



Short and explicit forms share normalization. formula and formulas are aliases; starts do not select the engine. REML initializes omitted starts, while supplied values remain authoritative. Fixed solves require complete covariance values. The tutorial gives the route-specific initialization rules.
Distinct descriptors are independent. Correlated channels must be declared explicitly and have known IDs for observed responses. Correlated residual blocks require unique positions within one variance group. Multi-component multitrait/random regression, multi-response residual descriptors, nuggets and unknown-time imputation remain outside this adapter. Covariance boundaries and unsupported combinations are not silently repaired. These examples do not extend workload or platform qualification.

title: Methods reference
text:
Association mapping
Association mapping belongs in native glma and the Glist-based glma() R interface; fine-mapping and colocalisation remain in gmap. The current quantitative-trait methods are exact linear regression, Gaussian/ridge-only infinitesimal LOCO offset testing, and prior-selected LOCO offset testing with automatic structure-dependent scaling or a manual override. The LOCO methods can fit on a selected subset of Glist markers while testing every marker in that Glist; the subset must cover every tested chromosome. Association scans also accept a phenotype matrix with named traits and return one association result per trait. Exact linear scans share genotype reads and dosage decoding. LOCO traits share immutable genotype preparation but each retains its own variance fit, prior selection and calibration. Both LOCO methods use the joint prediction engine. Infinitesimal LOCO fixes one Gaussian/ridge prior and equal standardized-marker variances; prior-selected LOCO compares ridge/elastic priors. Blocked RHE initializes a shared three-point Monte Carlo heritability grid. The global variance pair remains fixed for chromosome-excluded refits. Diagnostics identify this approximate estimator, its grid fallback and fitting phases. The slow per-chromosome variance search and its controls are retired from the standalone interface. Portable matrix products support operation-local OpenMP threads. See the LOCO variance procedure. Exact linear scans can include selected marker genotypes as fixed covariates through condition_on; this is a complete-case conditional test and does not reuse the LOCO null model. Binary traits can use the distinct logistic method for ordinary covariate-adjusted per-marker log-odds Wald tests. Sparse case/control counts, separation and non-convergence have explicit statuses. This baseline does not adjust for relatedness or claim LOCO binary calibration. glma provides linear, logistic, infinitesimal LOCO and prior-selected LOCO functions plus the glma(..., method=) dispatcher. vegas() consumes validated gbase summaries and Glist sparse LD. These methods are separate from gmap_stat() summary-statistic preparation.
Marker sets can also define separate genetic background components for either LOCO method. Named disjoint groups plus an automatic unassigned background are fitted jointly using greml’s multi-component RHE variance profile and the joint engine’s scalar Monte Carlo scale refinement. Prepared storage is required. Component estimates and chromosome exclusions are returned in fit$components and fit$loco_components. See the component model and its approximation limits.

Summary/BED fitting, independent study references, annotations, covariance learning, posterior capture and continuation, genetic-covariance reporting, partitions and selected-individual uncertainty are implemented.
Bayesian workflow



The connected gcorr validation checks genotype-derived LD scores and fits against dense references. A shared unit floor on marginal working means keeps all prescribed draws finite on the fixture. The floor changes variance weights without clamping raw estimates, and activation is reported in native diagnostics. See the weighting contract. The subsequent statistical calibration study completes all fits and passes parameter-recovery screens, but flags undercoverage for 15 primary quantities. Uncertainty qualification remains incomplete. An independent trait-1 QR diagnostic agrees with the native fixed-weight procedure; re-estimating weights during block deletion improves coverage but does not fully resolve it. These capabilities have not been broadly qualified on real GWAS. The coordinated reliability study finds better coverage with known weights and analytical SEs, supporting an uncertainty-procedure limitation in the tested setting. Matched full LD gives stable estimates in the fixture; short windows and mismatched references cause bias. Current normal/jackknife intervals remain experimental; broad confidence-interval qualification is still open.
Detailed equations, layouts, ownership, and limitations remain in each repository’s local catalogue and linked design documents. The actual local dataset campaign is summarized separately in qgdata qualification.

title: Methods reference
text:
Sparse-direct pedigree methods
The three pedigree APIs use the same canonical lower-CSC MME for their supported direct backends. Retained factors supply exact determinants and bounded coordinate traces or CHOLMOD selected-inverse traces. Rejected likelihood-only trials omit trace/AI work; accepted response coefficients finalize BLUP without another response solve. Backend factor-memory limits are preflight bounds, not strict allocator quotas.
Use the model catalog for backend/inference status, multitrait workflow and longitudinal workflow for record contracts, and prediction error for complete-MME PEV, CHOLMOD selected inversion, and bounded PARDISO retained-factor target solves. PARDISO selected inversion remains unsupported. Direct and support thread domains and requested/resolved methods remain distinct diagnostics.

title: Methods reference
text:
Independent LD references
Glist is the single public genotype and LD descriptor. Augment it directly with gmat’s signed, disk-backed sparse LD:
Glist <- gbase::gprep(Glist = Glist, task = "sparseld",
                      out_prefix = "reference_ld", r2 = 0.01,
                      max_distance_bp = 1000000)
saveRDS(Glist, "Glist-EUR.rds")
Glist <- readRDS("Glist-EUR.rds")
gbase::verify_ld(Glist) # once after transfer or download
scores <- gbase::ld_scores(Glist)
Glist$sparseLD retains authoritative marker order, alleles, chromosome, position, reference sample count, file paths, checksums and construction settings. ldfiles, idsLD, and rsidsLD identify the same persisted resource, reference samples, and matrix-ordered markers. RDS saves the descriptor, not the external LD files. validate_Glist() checks this identity and alignment without rescanning the CSR; verify_ld() performs the full native structure, checksum, and recorded-score verification after a transfer or when corruption is suspected. Neither check establishes population suitability. Scores are computed from that same resource:
scores <- gbase::ld_scores(Glist, annotations = annotation,
                           corrected = TRUE)
Annotation rows are aligned by exact marker identity. Corrected scores use the selected reference sample count and retain negative corrected contributions. All scores reflect retained sparse pairs; omitted correlations are not reconstructed. Summary harmonization remains separate.

Regional matrices and reusable eigensystems
Select a region using unique marker IDs already in reference order:
R_region <- gbase::ld_region(Glist, markers = region_markers)
eig <- gbase::ld_eigen(Glist, markers = region_markers)
gmat opens the checked resource once per high-level call and reuses one indexed reader across regions; no full CSR is loaded and only the active dense matrix is materialized. gsolve computes the complete symmetric eigensystem using its existing Eigen backend and verifies reconstruction, residual and orthogonality. The result contains descending values, column vectors with marker row names, and numerical diagnostics. Singular or indefinite matrices are not silently repaired: zero and negative eigenvalues remain available to method-specific checks. Thresholded or windowed sparse LD is not necessarily positive semidefinite.
The eigensystem is computed from the checked regional matrix on demand and can be reused across traits or fits for that region. The full decomposition takes quadratic storage and cubic computation; increasing the dimension limit is an explicit choice. Omitted sparse correlations remain zero, the diagonal is one, and no harmonization, clipping or PSD repair occurs.
For a BED Glist with independent regions saved by gbase::gprep(task="eigen"), gcorr(Glist, stat, method="hess", nthreads=4) reuses its region definitions and reference sample selection and returns estimates plus compact moments in fit$projection. Named Z/N arrays must already be oriented to Glist’s a1 alleles. Stored eigenvalues alone cannot project statistics, so the required vectors are recomputed per region and discarded. Both compact-fit overlap inputs default to zero and can be overridden.
For explicit disk-limited joint HESS, gcorr_prepare_hess() streams BED regions, uses validated physical BED/FAM rows without rebuilding chromosome-wide metadata or name lookups, and releases R matching buffers before decoding. It decomposes the smaller sample- or marker-space Gram and projects all supplied traits together. It discards large matrices/eigenvectors after each region; gcorr_fit_hess() reuses the serializable compact moments in the existing joint correction and conditional uncertainty calculations. This needs no persistent LD files. Spectral controls and trait statistics are fixed at preparation, and overlap inputs can be supplied at fit time. Automatic compact preparation limits the conservative total rank to half the smallest supplied N. Explicit fit-time genomic-control factors and provenance scale unchanged moments without changing N or repeating decomposition. Conditioning and region-specific inference blockers are reported. Compact fits default to uncertainty="hess", using the original software’s full-rank h2/covariance variance systems and genome rg region jackknife. Point estimates retain the documented row-rank equations. The software variance convention has no regional rg SEs or joint sampling covariance; uncertainty="moment" selects the previous signed conditional fourth-moment calculation, and "strict" retains its parameter checks. Prepared-LD interfaces keep their strict default. Invalid jackknife replicates remain missing; out-of-range rg receives only a descriptive SE, without Wald inference. Approximate uncertainty does not establish statistic/reference-scale validity or broad empirical calibration. See the R workflow.
The gcorr R interface also prepares all named regions from one Glist-backed native reader and retains one PreparedRegionalLd per region. HESS, rho-HESS, SUPERGNOVA and LAVA have single-region overloads that reuse a complete checked eigensystem; LDSC and GNOVA already accept prepared gmat score inputs. gsolve can verify imported eigenvalues and vectors against a regional matrix without rerunning the eigensolver. This dense verification is performed once on native import, followed by reuse across fits. The gcorr R interface connects selected methods to these resources, including explicit joint HESS/rho-HESS correction with regional and total uncertainty. It adds no cross-ancestry estimator and also exposes shared LAVA matrices and native conditional inference.
Across these methods, result tables use explicit reference, region, annotation-category and architecture-component labels. Named h2/cov/rg matrices share one layout; method-specific uncertainty, native diagnostics and inconsistent pairwise estimates remain visible. See result conventions.
The interface also exposes SumHer architecture-component and reference-total h2/cov/rg. Multiple traits use the native coordinated marginal and pairwise fits, with joint fixed-weight jackknife covariance when blocks are supplied. Tagging weights are explicit and separate from architecture-weighted scores; no cross-ancestry or full upstream-software parity is implied.
Regional LAVA also accepts explicit binary-trait metadata, reusing Glist allele frequencies for native logistic-Wald reconstruction. Observed and liability h2 remain distinct; binary/mixed pairs use the existing screening and optional bivariate simulation inference. LAVA shares each regional fit across traits and exposes partial correlations, multiple regression, explained variance and supported conditional/omnibus inference.
Native regional execution now supports multiple named references and regions. Each request explicitly assigns a reference to every trait; all traits in that request must agree. Independent requests may use different references. Results retain analysis, region and reference labels, along with method diagnostics or a per-request failure. Execution is sequential and writes no result files. Joint HESS and rho-HESS can reuse prepared regions within one selected reference while retaining their existing disjoint-region and joint uncertainty assumptions. Reference labels are caller-declared identities, not an ancestry validation step.
For continuous-trait regional LAVA correlations, gcorr_lava() accepts an explicit inference list. The native bivariate procedure supplies screened p-values, 95% simulation intervals and Monte Carlo diagnostics while retaining raw point estimates. See the regional inference contract. This adds no new numerical algorithm or statistical calibration claim.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native colocalisation
gmap provides approximate-Bayes-factor colocalisation for one region and two continuous traits, assuming at most one causal variant per trait and non-overlapping samples. It returns H0-H4 probabilities and explicit prior-sensitivity summaries. The implementation has independent numerical checks and pinned coloc comparisons; these establish numerical agreement, not broad statistical calibration. The gmap::gmap_coloc() route accepts two aligned regional beta/SE tables, explicit phenotype SDs and priors without an LD object. It returns regional probabilities and conditional-H4 marker support, distinct from component-pair colocalisation. See the worked example. GWAS association is implemented separately in glma; Bayesian fine-mapping and posterior-set interpretation are described below.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native Bayesian inference
The gbayes::gbayes() R workflow exposes single-trait and joint multivariate regression from a prepared individual-level BED Glist or from checked summaries and Glist sparse LD. The BED route uses matched pre-adjusted phenotype columns and native packed-genotype preparation; its joint route can learn residual covariance from observed trait cross-products. BayesC/BayesR support fixed parameters or optional effect-covariance and mixture-weight learning, exact chain seeds, chain-level threading and native posterior summaries. Multiple traits require explicit independent sampling or the common-N shared-LD covariance model. Variable sample sizes are an explicit approximation and, for multivariate fits, require independent sampling and study-size metadata. Shared-LD multivariate sampling covariance can be learned when the response cross-product and likelihood dimension are supplied. Scalar BayesC/BayesR expose fixed, exact in-sample and reference-LD adjusted residual policies. Exact learning uses an explicit response sum of squares, likelihood dimension, scaled inverse-chi-square prior and complete same-sample LD. The reference-LD route uses standardized summary normalization and records its base residual variance, genetic variance and adjusted working variance separately. Latent base-effect covariance is labelled separately from realised genetic covariance. The annotation argument exposes logistic inclusion, continuation-probit pattern/component probabilities and log-linear variance models, with fixed or learned coefficients and native diagnostics. The same interface now binds grouped latent covariance priors and optional native posterior genetic covariance, partition activity/covariance and selected-individual score uncertainty. Heritability normalization requires explicit phenotype variances. Group summaries retain cross-group LD; score uncertainty excludes residual noise. Named study-specific references additionally expose native independent-provider preparation with differing LD, sample sizes and marker subsets. Multiple studies may inform shared effects of one trait within a model of at least two traits. Study identity, trait identity and reference provenance remain distinct. This is not an overlap correction or an automatic ancestry-specific effect model.
gbayes provides single-trait BayesC and BayesR with fixed parameters or explicit learning of residual variance, slab variance and mixture weights. Prepared scores and cross-products can use dense storage, gmat LD operations with explicit marker scaling, or prepared factors with reduced residuals. Factorized execution avoids a dense cross-product matrix. Truncated inputs use explicitly projected scores; residual learning then requires retained-space normalization (dimension and response sum of squares). Results include posterior means, empirical posterior variances, marginal inclusion probabilities and compact per-chain summaries. BayesR also returns marker component probabilities; both methods summarize learned parameters. Residual-variance learning requires compatible phenotype sums of squares and an explicit Gaussian likelihood dimension, not just LD and scores. The gmap() R binding exposes BayesC/BayesR separately across named traits and regions, including optional variance and mixture-weight learning. MCMC learning requires explicit inverse-chi-square or Dirichlet hyperpriors. Residual learning also requires complete in-sample LD, phenotype sum of squares and likelihood dimension; these are never inferred from the reference panel.
The scalar reference-LD recipe has five-repetition qualification for matched continuous-trait BayesC and BayesR analyses, including heritability, effect and score recovery and four-chain diagnostics. Independent scalar calculations, dense/gmat agreement and matched sblr checks support its native implementation. See the qualification record for the exact LD construction, priors and chain lengths. Supplied cross-products must define a valid positive-semidefinite operator; structural checks do not repair or certify arbitrary thresholded LD. A separate five-repetition design qualifies disjoint-block residual learning, the BayesS MAF exponent, shared-LD latent effect and sampling-covariance learning, and strong-LD relocation under their stated contracts. Scalar and multivariate saved states also reproduce uninterrupted chains exactly. Broader annotation models and arbitrary overlap structures remain outside that evidence.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native regional Bayesian analysis
The Bayesian-enabled gmap::gmap library fits or summarizes one-region BayesC/BayesR models through installed gbayes. It preserves marker alignment, region coordinates, trait/effect units and the complete native posterior. Results include marker rankings and the posterior expected active-marker count, calculated as the sum of marginal PIPs. Existing gbayes priors and learning controls pass through.
These posterior summaries describe marker support. Separate set helpers below interpret marginal PIPs or component assignments. These summaries do not themselves perform colocalisation or estimate regional heritability. The separate gmap_coloc_components() interface consumes multi-effect evidence. Inputs are already aligned. The gmap() R binding returns regional posterior estimates, native set controls and chain diagnostics for named regions and traits, with regional preparation shared across traits. One regional eigensystem supports an ordered retained-positive-mass schedule; the first threshold accepted for every trait is selected and every attempt remains visible. The colocalisation target acquires no Bayesian dependency. Focused checks cover posterior reuse, metadata/ranking semantics and installed interfaces.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native single-effect inference
gbayes now provides a deterministic single-effect normal model for one prepared marker set. It reuses the normal conditional calculation and accepts the existing dense, LD-backed and factorized inputs. Outputs include marker assignment probabilities, conditional and averaged effect moments, and model evidence against no effect. Residual and effect-prior variances are fixed; marker prior weights can be specified explicitly.
The model assumes exactly one active marker, so assignments sum to one even when evidence is weak. They are not unconditional association probabilities. This is a reusable building block; the separate multi-effect entry point below adds iteration and convergence handling. gmap now consumes assignments for credible sets; multi-signal colocalisation remains separate. The standalone gbayes::gbayes_single_effect() R interface accepts an ordinary data frame with unique rsids and either b/seb or score/information, plus fixed positive residual/effect variances and optional marker prior weights. It returns per-marker assignment probabilities and moments. It does not expose every native input or parameter-learning option. Focused independent numerical integration and installed-interface checks cover the native calculation.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native multi-effect inference
gbayes also provides single-trait sum-of-single-effects fitting through sequential IBSS updates. It reuses the existing single-effect calculation and dense, LD or factorized operators. Outputs include component assignments, combined effect means, variational variances/PIPs, and an objective trace with explicit convergence or sweep-limit status.
The objective is an evidence lower bound relative to the null likelihood, not an exact model Bayes factor. The approximation factorizes across components; convergence does not guarantee a global optimum or calibrated uncertainty. The maximum component count is supplied, and components may select the same marker. The default fixed-variance route leaves every component active. Optional EM learning estimates a variance for each component and compares it with zero; inactive components contribute no effects or PIPs. Optional residual-variance learning uses expected residual sums of squares with compatible normalization. Inner learning limits and outer convergence are reported explicitly. gmap supplies credible sets only for active components while retaining inactive indices and all component variances. The gmap() R binding exposes this route separately across regions and traits, with optional residual- and effect-variance learning. Residual learning requires complete in-sample LD and explicit phenotype normalization. Small analytic/evidence and operator checks cover the native calculation; full susieR equivalence is not claimed.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native posterior sets
The optional gmap Bayesian component supports two explicitly labelled routes. Marginal-PIP sets reuse sblr’s LD-neighborhood and approximate multi-signal selection, including incomplete-set handling and alternative lead/removal rules. Their mass is an expected active-marker count, not a probability that at least one causal variant lies in the set. This route consumes BayesC/BayesR PIPs.
Component-based credible sets consume single-/multi-effect assignment rows. They retain each component, report achieved probability coverage and flag exact duplicate memberships. Shared diagnostics include lead-based and full pairwise LD summaries. Low purity is flagged without trimming away coverage. Sparse LD omissions are explicitly recorded; purity is evaluated on the supplied matrix.
These helpers validate probability domains and exact fit/LD marker order, preserve available convergence/likelihood status, and do not refit or align data. Learned zero-variance components are recorded without sets; the raw assignment route still treats every row as a component. Weak fixed-variance components can produce diffuse sets; a complete credible set does not establish a signal. The R binding exposes these controls through control$sets, with explicit set meanings and component eligibility diagnostics.
gmap_sets() converts the nested native result to set-level and marker-level tables without changing those meanings. gmap_bfdr() operates only on fitted marker PIPs: at a supplied threshold it reports the selected count, the expected false-discovery count sum(1 - PIP) and their ratio. A requested BFDR target selects the largest PIP-threshold group below that bound. It does not require LD, retained posterior draws or another model fit, and it is not a frequentist FDR guarantee.
Prior-variance learning is empirical Bayes, not posterior uncertainty over model size or a test proving signal existence. The EM search is local; inactive components are reconsidered from a positive starting variance each sweep. The reusable learned single-effect entry is available independently. Existing fixed-variance entry points retain their previous numerical behavior.

title: Methods reference
text:
Regional Bayesian R workflow
For an individual-level BayesC/BayesR fit, gmap::gmap_bed(fit, Glist, regions) reuses the saved global posterior. The Glist must carry in-sample sparse LD prepared from exactly the fitted people and markers. Sample order, physical BED offsets, alleles and frequencies are checked. Within-region LD must be complete by default. Native gmap groups the fitted marginal PIPs; the result is neither a regional refit nor a component credible set. This route also accepts a joint-trait BED fit and retains trait labels. See the BED-to-gmap workflow.
gmap::gmap() accepts an aligned Glist and exact sufficient-statistic columns marker, allele1, allele2, score (\(X^T y\)) and marker_ss (\(\operatorname{diag}(X^T X)\)). It fits each named region/trait separately using BayesC, BayesR or multi-effect inference. It does not convert GWAS z scores or beta/SE automatically. The supplied LD and marker scales define the working cross-products; a reference approximation does not become exact cohort LD.
fit <- gmap::gmap(list(height = stat_height, weight = stat_weight), Glist,
            regions = list(locus1 = markers_locus1, locus2 = markers_locus2),
            method = "multi_effect",
            prior = list(residual_variance = 1, effect_variance = .02),
            control = list(effects = 4, estimate_effect_variance = TRUE,
              eigen = list(retained_positive_mass = 1)))
summary(fit)
plot(fit, region = "locus1", trait = "height", quantity = "pip")
Prior values above are illustrative and must match the supplied data scale. Controls and seeds are shared across fits; use separate calls for different priors or independent random streams. Each verified region is decomposed once across traits. The default retained-mass schedule is c(.995, .99, .95). diagnostic_summary records the selected requested/achieved mass, rank and projection change, while eigen_attempts records each attempted threshold. Set control$eigen$retained_positive_mass=1 for the exact full-rank route. Residual-variance learning is restricted to that full-rank route. Component colocalisation also requires a converged full-rank multi-effect fit; use the same explicit setting when the fit will be passed to gmap_coloc_components(). control$sets exposes method-specific native set controls. BayesC/BayesR retain pooled and per-chain PIPs, with native between-chain spread summaries; these are not convergence certificates or Monte Carlo standard errors. Scalar summary BayesC/BayesR in gmap() and gbayes() also expose optional control$ld_swap relocation moves on their dense/sparse and eigen likelihoods. The native gbayes sampler owns neighbour selection and Metropolis-Hastings acceptance. Probability defaults to zero; fit$ld_swap reports proposal counts, not convergence. The existing timing studies used swaps disabled.
For traits analysed in independent samples, the saved fits can be compared:
shared <- gmap::gmap_coloc_components(
  fit, fit, Glist, trait1 = "height", trait2 = "weight", regions = "locus1",
  control = list(complete_region_coverage = TRUE,
                 non_overlapping_samples = TRUE))
summary(shared)
plot(shared)
The two assertions require complete regional coverage and independent trait samples; they must describe the actual analysis. This route requires converged full-likelihood multi-effect fits, uniform marker priors and the same complete LD reference. It consumes stored component evidence without fitting or eigen computation. LD files must remain available for checked purity calculations. H0–H4 probabilities belong to individual component pairs, not the entire region. Inactive, low-purity, incomplete and duplicate components remain labelled; no eligible pairs is not evidence for H0. Summaries and plots of completed results work from saved R objects without accessing LD files.
OLS beta/SE/n preparation is available through gmap_stat(); see below and the worked simulation tutorial. No cross-reference or overlapping-sample colocalisation is exposed.

title: Methods reference
text:
Linear-regression GWAS input for mapping
gmap::gmap_stat() performs a separate OLS summary conversion in the R layer: for sample phenotype variance \(s_y^2\), it reconstructs \(d_j=(n-1)s_y^2/[(n-2)SE_j^2+\hat\beta_j^2]\) and \(X_j^\mathsf{T}y=d_j\hat\beta_j\). The common-sample, intercept-only, continuous-outcome contract is explicit. LD supplies the off-diagonal cross-products; external LD is approximate. Numerical fitting and sets remain native. See the worked example.

title: Methods reference
text:
MR through the R interface
gcorr exposes GSMR, GSMR2, IVW, Egger and weighted-median components through gcorr_prepare_mr() and method-specific fitters. Preparation consumes two aligned gbase effect/SE summaries and an explicit signed-LD matrix; it does not accept an LDlist, align alleles or infer ancestry/sample overlap. The serializable result records every selection and LD decision. Focused fitters and gcorr(prepared, method=...) return HEIDI, estimate-unit and method-specific diagnostics. See the MR workflow.

title: Methods reference
section: Covariance models through the R interface
text:
Covariance models through the R interface
gcorr_covariance() retains labelled continuous genetic covariance and full joint sampling covariance. Focused SEM and GGM functions expose recursive SEM, descriptive partial-correlation networks and fixed-graph GGM. Parameter tables, trait units and estimation metadata remain explicit. Fitted SEM paths and free GGM edges support native joint Wald tests. Coordinated multivariate GNOVA annotation categories and SumHer architecture components can reuse the same models, with cross-group contrasts based on the retained joint jackknife covariance. See the covariance-model workflow.

title: Methods reference
text:
Native matrix-free execution experiments
The generic greml PCG route now supports same-state adaptive trace-prefix extension. Native-only opt-in controls add bounded raw inverse-probe warm starts, coarse component-action reuse, solution-subspace recycling and independent-basis residual trace estimation. The latter two require experimental evaluation; determinant precision and the packed coefficient path remain separate. See native contracts. No new R controls or general scaling qualification are implied.
Standalone gbayes::gbayes(data=..., Glist=..., method="bayesc") and BayesR accept automatic phenotype-scaled BED priors with parameter learning and retained diagnostics. Scalar BED responses are centred on their original units; see the defaults and controls for initialization, explicit-prior compatibility and convergence limits.
Fixed-covariance compiled prediction also omits unused global REML first/second covariance-derivative matrices and RHS arrays. It retains the same numerical MME, residual precision caches and preconditioner; full estimation keeps its existing derivative assembly. This removes quadratic-in-parameter-count storage from prediction without imposing a memory ceiling. The refreshed native capability is prediction_value_only_assembly.

title: Methods reference
text:
BLR from exact cross-products
The current standalone gbayes cross-product contract is blr() for one response and mblr() for joint responses, with exact labelled XX/Xy/yy and the shared bayesfit. Scalar defaults calibrate vb=h2yy/(trace(XX)mixture mass) and ve=(1-h2)*yy/d on supplied feature units, where d defaults to n-1 for declared centered statistics. This replaces the earlier scalar qgg-style wrapper design. See the current cross-product workflow. The existing gsea re-export follows the installed gbayes signature; gsea’s separate native set/PoPS samplers retain their existing contracts. The frozen qgg comparison below records the earlier convention rather than the new defaults.
Development interfaces: this section describes gbayes 0.1.6 and gsea 0.1.2 with matching native libraries. The public gbayes/gsea 0.1.1 archives do not include the BLR entry points or set-summary helper below. See release and development status.
Use gsea::set_cross_products() for binary sets under independent observations, then gsea::blr() for one model fit from the returned XX, Xy, yy and n. Feature preparation, gene-association statistics, prediction and chromosome-held-out validation are separate operations. Centering and scaling are recorded with the summaries; fitted coefficients retain those prepared coordinates. The dense p-by-p Gram matrix remains necessary for this interface.
BLR uses exact in-sample residual learning, no reference-LD adjustment, and qgg’s intended scalar BLR variance-prior conventions. The qgg R blr() examined on 19 October 2026 passes vb then vg to a native entry point expecting vg then vb; this affects the effective initial slab variance. gbayes does not reproduce that mismatch. The independent comparison supplies equal explicit vg/vb to qgg and checks its variance trace. RNG order and retained output still differ.
timing$sampling_seconds measures the native fit call, including its checks and posterior accumulation. Native/R input preparation and subsequent posterior summaries are reported separately. A single-chain timing is not convergence evidence. The new entry point does not expose full coefficient draws or chain continuation; existing genomic interfaces retain their own capabilities.
Bayesian set workflows automatically use native direct cross-products for scalar independent-gene models with an intercept only. Bayesian set-based PoPS keeps memberships through training and prediction when screening is absent; other model structures retain general projection. Model-specific n-1 pathway normalization, priors and original-unit pathway coefficients are preserved. Their timing records mark upstream gene-statistic computation as unmeasured (NA, caller supplied), distinguish preparation from native BLR, and label PoPS fold sums separately from a single fit. See the gene-set guide for route limits.
Assistant instruction sources, ChatGPT launch generation and optional plugin packaging are owned by gchat. The website consumes a pinned public export; see website maintenance. Request submission, authentication and email approval remain in the existing gsuite request service unchanged.

title: Longitudinal sparse-pedigree REML and BLUP
text:
Longitudinal sparse-pedigree REML and BLUP
gs_longitudinal_pedigree_records() stores only observed scalar longitudinal records. Each row supplies an animal, phenotype, reporting time, fixed-design row, caller-supplied random-regression basis row, and residual-group label. Missing occasions are absent rows. Records may be irregular, repeated, arbitrarily ordered, and uneven across animals; pedigree-only animals remain in the fitted domain. Character residual groups use deterministic lexical order and integer groups use deterministic numeric order, so record permutation does not change covariance-parameter positions.
ped <- gs_pedigree_data(
  individual = c("dam", "sire", "offspring", "relative"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "sire", "sire"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "dam", "dam")
)
animal <- c("dam", "dam", "sire", "offspring", "offspring")
time <- c(0, 1.4, 0.2, 0.7, 2.1)
y <- c(1.1, 1.8, 0.9, 1.4, 2.2)

records <- gs_longitudinal_pedigree_records(
  ped, animal, y, time,
  basis = cbind(intercept = 1, time = time),
  fixed = cbind(intercept = 1, time = time),
  residual_group = ifelse(time < 1, "early", "late")
)
start <- gs_longitudinal_pedigree_start(records)
control <- gs_longitudinal_pedigree_reml_control(
  linear_solver = "sparse_direct", direct_backend = "pardiso",
  requested_threads = 8,
  exact_trace_method = "coordinate",
  maximum_direct_coefficient_dimension = 5000,
  max_exact_trace_systems = 5000
)
fit <- gs_longitudinal_pedigree_fit(
  records, start, covariance = "optimized", control = control,
  prediction = list(
    animal = c("offspring", "relative"), time = c(1.5, 1.5),
    basis = cbind(1, c(1.5, 1.5)),
    fixed = cbind(1, c(1.5, 1.5))
  )
)
The deterministic non-RHE start fits the supplied fixed design, calculates \(s_r^2=\frac{\mathrm{RSS}}{N-\operatorname{rank}(X)}\) and mean basis magnitude \(m_b=\frac{1}{N}\sum_j\lVert b_j\rVert^2\), then sets \(Q_0=\frac{s_r^2}{2m_b}I\) and each residual-group variance to \(s_r^2/2\). User-supplied SPD Q and positive residual starts override it.
Both solvers use one canonical animal-major sparse MME. linear_solver = "pcg" is portable and is the large fixed-covariance BLUP route. "sparse_direct" is an optional moderate-problem route with one reused PARDISO or CHOLMOD symbolic analysis, exact retained-factor likelihood, and bounded complete coordinate traces. Automatic selection prefers PARDISO; CHOLMOD and support work are serial. Explicit direct selection never falls back: an unavailable backend returns not_supported and the gsolve message. PCG factors the bounded fixed-effect preconditioner block and one basis-rank block per pedigree animal, and verifies the true MME residual.
Coordinate traces remain the default. Explicit CHOLMOD supernodal selected inversion replaces only the exact coordinate trace systems. Deterministic positive-definite planning compiles derivative support once, then reuses one trace plan, derivative mapping, and selected-inverse workspace across covariance states. The result reports calls, selected and filled-factor entries, workspace/request/output and projected peak bytes, systems avoided, and serial selected-inverse support threads. AI derivative-response systems, exact determinant work, optimizer acceptance, and retained BLUP finalization are unchanged. CHOLMOD orchestration and support remain serial, while selected-inverse dense kernels use an independently requested oneMKL thread count. PARDISO selected inversion, including automatic when it resolves to PARDISO, is explicitly not_supported without fallback after symbolic capability resolution and before numerical factorization. PCG remains a separate fixed-covariance route with zero direct work.
The result reports starting/final covariance, fixed effects, animal-by-basis latent coefficients, observed genetic trajectories, fitted values, residuals, Py, optional prediction trajectories, covariance/optimizer diagnostics, and complete factorization/trace/AI work. Successful optimization reuses the accepted response coefficients for one BLUP finalization and performs no additional response solve. The shared typed serializer translates these diagnostics without numerical work. In the direct diagnostics, sparse_direct$requested is a logical direct-route flag, whereas requested_backend and resolved_backend are backend strings.
Resource preflight bounds coefficient dimension, coordinate systems, RHS batch width, workspace, and factor memory. Construction and PCG diagnostics expose the single record pass, zero optimizer record revisits, stored sparse-statistic values/nonzeros, fixed and animal preconditioner blocks, RHS width, and true residual. CHOLMOD selected-inverse trace and retained-factor prediction-error paths are available through this API. Exact PEV/reliability requires retained selected-inverse state.
PARDISO selected inversion, MUMPS, covariance boundaries, RHE, serial residual correlation, multiple relationship components, genomic models, marker effects, and ssGBLUP are not supported by this interface. The prediction-error contract supports bounded PARDISO selected_solve coefficient and trajectory uncertainty from retained factors. This does not add PARDISO selected inversion or PCG exact PEV.

title: gmat integration
text:
The R workflow has one owner at each layer:
gbase Glist → gbase sparse-LD preparation → gmat disk resource → task packages
gbase::gprep() owns genotype preparation and augments a Glist with sparse-LD identity, marker and sample selections, paths, settings, and provenance. gbits owns BED decoding. gmat owns panel mappings, sparse-LD computation, the disk format, validation, and readers. Task packages accept the Glist and use installed public gmat interfaces from C++.
