title: gmat integration
text:
Serializable bridge objects
Root gsuite retains only the BED resource and panel objects needed by its own internal genotype integration:

gsuite_bed_resource retains canonical BED/BIM/FAM paths, physical counts, and literal ordered BIM/FAM metadata.
gsuite_bed_panel retains component resources, exact selections, selected metadata, and zero-based native source mappings.

These list-style S3 objects have no external pointers. Sparse-LD preparation and access are not duplicated in root gsuite.

title: gmat integration
text:
Identity and ordering
Component order is list order. Components must have identical ordered (family_id, individual_id) pairs before selection. Sample identities and per-component marker IDs are resolved exactly, and requested order is preserved. Global marker order concatenates component selections. Duplicate or missing identities are errors. Nothing silently sorts chromosomes, positions, markers, samples, or alleles.
The gbase::gprep(task = "sparseld") contract, numerical conventions, and Glist fields are specified in sparse-LD preparation.

title: gmat integration
text:
Limitations
The integration does not harmonize alleles, flip dosage, convert genome builds, or parse summary statistics. All five files in a persistent gmat sparse-LD resource must remain available together.
See the gmat method catalogue for the complete native contracts.

title: Marker-QC contract
text:
gbase::gfilter() is the summary-only marker-selection operation. It accepts the strict serializable c("gs_genotypes", "Glist") descriptor produced by gbase::gprep(task = "prepare") and returns a plain marker-ID vector. It does not mutate the descriptor, read packed BED genotype bytes, write BED or CSR files, decode a genotype matrix, or construct sparse LD. gmat and gbits remain unchanged owners of metadata/LD and packed-genotype operations respectively.
Marker identity is canonical chromosome/file/BIM order. Every required chromosome-wise field is checked for the same shape, and IDs must be complete and globally unique. The existing preparation validator also reopens the BIM/FAM/BED descriptors and verifies source mappings. Genotype counts must be nonnegative integers whose sum equals the exact summary population recorded by sample_source_indices_0based and provenance$summary_samples. MAF must agree with n0, n1, and n2. Thus a study-sample preparation uses that selected population rather than the complete FAM count.



Each enabled rule creates a full-length exclusion mask; the final mask is their union. NULL disables a numeric rule and FALSE disables a logical rule.

MAF excludes \(\mathrm{maf}_j\leq\texttt{maf}\); equality is excluded.
Missingness is \(\frac{n_{\mathrm{miss}}}{n_0+n_1+n_2+n_{\mathrm{miss}}}\) and excludes values strictly greater than missing; equality is retained.
HWE excludes exact-test p-values strictly less than hwe; equality is retained.
INFO excludes values strictly less than info; equality is retained.
Ambiguity excludes the exact allele pairs A/T, T/A, C/G, and G/C.
The indel/non-SNP rule retains only exact uppercase single-base A, C, G, or T for both alleles. It therefore rejects multi-base, symbolic, and lowercase encodings without silently normalizing alleles.
MHC excludes a closed interval, including both endpoints, on stored chromosome labels 6 and chr6: GRCh37 [28,477,797, 33,448,397], or GRCh38 [28,510,120, 33,480,577]. The assembly must be explicitly GRCh37 or GRCh38, supplied as an argument or in Glist$assembly; it is never guessed.

All numeric thresholds are finite scalars in [0,1]. Logical controls are nonmissing scalars. A marker-aligned INFO field is required only when INFO filtering is enabled. It may be a named numeric vector or list, but its names must be a duplicate-free exact set of prepared marker IDs. Values are reordered by identity into canonical order before the mask is calculated.



For each biallelic marker, gbase conditions on the observed sample count and minor-allele copy count and enumerates every feasible heterozygote count with the same allele total. The two-sided p-value is the sum of conditional genotype probabilities no greater than the observed genotype probability. Probabilities within relative tolerance 1e-12 are treated as ties. This is the conventional probability-ordering exact test. Monomorphic markers receive p-value 1. All-missing or structurally invalid counts are descriptor errors; any otherwise nonfinite HWE result is conservatively excluded when HWE filtering is enabled.
qgg 1.1.6 instead uses a one-degree-of-freedom Pearson chi-square calculation. Familiar argument names excludeMAF, excludeMISS, excludeHWE, excludeINFO, excludeCGAT, excludeINDEL and excludeMHC alias the gbase thresholds and flags. Supply either spelling, rather than both. excludeDUPS is accepted; preparation already enforces unique marker identities. The tested version’s gfilter() also has disabled-mask hazards, relies on incomplete positional/name alignment, and subsets its combined mask incorrectly during INFO filtering. gsuite deliberately uses the exact test, complete identity validation, independent full-length masks, and an explicit default HWE threshold of 1e-12. It also freezes the documented inclusive MAF boundary.



Glist <- gbase::gprep(
  study = "Reference",
  bedfiles = bedfiles,
  task = "prepare",
  nthreads = 4
)

rsids <- gbase::gfilter(
  Glist,
  maf = 0.01,
  missing = 0.05,
  hwe = 1e-12,
  ambiguous = TRUE,
  indels = TRUE
)

Glist <- gbase::gprep(
  Glist = Glist,
  task = "sparseld",
  rsids = rsids,
  out_prefix = "reference_ld",
  nthreads = 4
)
Preparation computes reusable summaries once. The same unchanged descriptor can be filtered under several policies, and sparse LD is subsequently built only for the selected markers.

title: gbase
text:
gbase
gprep(task = "ldscores") computes U/D and bin-specific LD scores directly from a prepared Glist, using native gmat and R’s configured BLAS. See the workflow and limits.
gbase contains small, task-neutral R data contracts shared by the gsuite ecosystem. It performs no statistical fitting. Its genotype preparation contract uses the installed public gmat, gbits, and gsolve interfaces, with a qualified native prefix checked during compilation and native versions and ABIs checked again when the package loads. gsolve supplies dense products and regional eigensystems or eigenvalues; the portable binary disables CHOLMOD, MKL and PARDISO while retaining OpenMP support.
Summary statistics use the established qgg workflow: checkStat() maps and aligns an ordinary data frame to Glist, applies explicit QC, and returns an ordinary data frame with familiar short column names:
library(gbase)

stat <- checkStat(Glist = Glist, stat = raw_stat)
The result has no special summary-statistics class, constructor or accessor. Each task function validates the columns it uses, and statistical work belongs to the task package.
PLINK genotype resources are prepared once and remain serializable:
Glist <- gprep(bedfiles = c("chr1.bed", "chr2.bed"))
Glist <- gprep(
  Glist = Glist,
  task = "sparseld",
  out_prefix = "reference",
  max_distance_bp = 1000000,
  max_distance_variants = 1000,
  r2 = 0.01
)
The second call returns the same Glist contract augmented with its sparse-LD descriptor; it does not introduce a separate genotype or LD owner.
validate_Glist() checks BED/BIM/FAM identity one file component at a time, retaining only marker IDs for the global uniqueness check. It does not keep every chromosome’s full BIM metadata in memory together.
The same Glist is the input to task-neutral marker and LD utilities:
markers <- gfilter(Glist)
scores <- ld_scores(Glist)
region <- ld_region(Glist, markers = markers[1:100])
spectrum <- ld_eigen(Glist, markers = markers[1:100])

blocks <- data.frame(block_id = "chr1", first_marker = markers[1],
  last_marker = markers[length(markers)])
Glist <- define_ld_blocks(Glist, blocks)
Sparse-LD construction and metadata stay on the Glist returned by gprep(task = "sparseld").
Chromosomes can be extracted as marker sets from the existing metadata:
sets <- getChromosomeSets(Glist)
This gives one named, disjoint set per chromosome, preserving reference marker order. Grouping uses chromosome labels, including when one BED file contains several chromosomes. The helper reads no genotype or LD files.
Full regional LD eigenvalues can also be prepared directly from BED without first making sparse LD:
regionSets <- list(region1 = Glist$rsids[[1]][1:100])
Glist <- gprep(Glist, task = "eigen", sets = regionSets, nthreads = 4)
values <- Glist$eigen$values$region1
saveRDS(Glist, "Glist-with-regional-eigenvalues.rds")
Each region is a named marker set from one chromosome. Membership is retained in reference order, and the prepared sample IDs are stored with the spectra. Missing genotypes are mean-imputed; constant markers are rejected by ID. Only eigenvalues are computed, with no clipping or truncation. When markers outnumber samples, the smaller sample-space Gram matrix is used and the full marker spectrum is recovered by padding its null eigenvalues with zeros. Regions are processed sequentially; nthreads controls local BED decoding. The existing gsolve Eigen backend performs dense products and decomposition without a mandatory OpenBLAS dependency. Sparse-LD cutoffs and windows do not apply. glma::prepare_vegas(Glist) reuses these stored spectra for VEGAS without repeating LD computation or decomposition. It returns a serializable prepared object with the required marker and allele order for subsequent traits. Constant positive weights within each gene are supported; nonuniform weights continue to use the sparse-LD route. Statistical evaluation remains owned by glma.
mapSets(sets, Glist) resolves named marker memberships to prepared marker IDs or indices. Unknown members are dropped; empty sets remain visible. getLD(Glist, rsids=region) computes full regional BED correlation in requested marker order using the selected people, installed gmat decoding and R’s configured BLAS. Missing genotypes are mean-imputed and constant markers are rejected. It writes no files and applies no sparse-LD windows or cutoffs. The returned matrix records sample count and decoding/product timings. Statistical priors, sampler controls and posterior sets remain with task packages.

title: Software access and distribution policy
text: The scientific documentation and selected R packages are publicly available. The gsuite standalone mixed-model application is offered only to users with a valid licence. Implementation, interface availability, release status and access conditions are separate facts.

title: Software access and distribution policy
text:
Public resources
The advanced notes, bibliography, capability descriptions, qualification limits, YAML specification and small examples remain public. Approved benchmark methods, results and reproducibility information are also public. Reading a model or installation guide does not require a standalone licence.
The public R source repository supplies gbase, gbayes, gcorr, glma, gmap, gscore and gsea under their existing package licences. Public archives and development source can have different capabilities; consult the release-status guide. The companion projects gsim and gact retain their own distribution terms.
The bounded native sources deliberately included in these public packages remain part of those releases. This policy does not withdraw their existing licences or reclassify public numerical building blocks as restricted code.

title: Software access and distribution policy
text:
Licensed standalone application
A standalone licence covers the authorised use described in its agreement. Delivery includes the matched standalone executable, native runtime, installation bundle and included operational tools for the agreed platform and release. Updates, support, permitted sites and duration are specified in that agreement. A shared institutional installation must remain within its authorised scope.
Academic, evaluation and commercial arrangements may have different terms. A licence requirement does not itself imply a particular fee. Pricing, eligibility and a licence-request contact are not announced here. There is no public self-service standalone download or licence portal.
The intended HPC arrangement uses signed offline entitlements and avoids per-node activation or mandatory online checks. Enforcement-enabled builds check admission to new computations; admitted jobs can finish after expiry. Existing result files and inspection remain accessible. The installation guide describes the current implementation and release configuration.

title: Software access and distribution policy
text:
Interfaces and development availability
The standalone command is distinct from the seven public R packages. Development mixed-model R interfaces and native libraries are not an additional public release of the standalone product. Future mixed-model R packaging and its access conditions require a separate release decision. Existing public package rights remain unchanged.
Use the implementation overview to find available methods, then the linked interface and release guides to establish access. A method being implemented does not mean that every interface, combination or development version is a public download.

title: Software access and distribution policy
text:
Internal resources
Production signing private keys, licence issuance records, customer information, confidential datasets, unreleased builds and nonpublic implementation sources stay outside the public website and package repository. Public verification keys are distinct from signing private keys. Customer entitlements are delivered privately and do not appear in published examples, logs or benchmark evidence.
The public website uses an explicit allowlist. It publishes approved documents, examples, evidence and the verified seven-package source repository. Standalone archives, native executables and libraries, entitlement files and internal release records are excluded. Controlled standalone delivery is separate from website publication.

title: Software access and distribution policy
text:
Release conditions and existing licences
This is the product distribution policy, not a replacement software licence. Each component retains its applicable copyright and licence terms. Existing public releases retain their existing terms. In particular, controlling who receives an archive does not itself remove rights supplied by an open-source licence; see the GNU licensing FAQ.
A standalone release requires review of its exact executable, frontend, linked/bundled libraries, runtimes and source obligations. The GPL declaration of the experimental root R package neither clears that separate distribution nor determines every separately built component. Restricted redistribution terms must be compatible with the actual delivered combination.
Production delivery also requires approved terms, a configured production trust set, an enforcement-enabled build, target-system qualification, checksums and a controlled delivery route. Existing development and validation bundles are not automatically production licensed releases. Contact details and automated delivery remain pending; documentation publication does not activate them.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Technical detail and qualification notes supporting the architecture overview. Use the overview to choose a starting point; use this page for implementation contracts, route-specific limitations and evidence links.
gsuite is organised by user task. Shared data preparation lives in gbase; analysis methods live in independently installable R packages; numerical and statistical computation remains in the corresponding native libraries. The root gsuite development integration currently provides mixed-model and solver R interfaces. The ecosystem documentation is maintained here independently of that integration. A root R package release is not currently planned; greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred, with separate or combined packaging undecided.
The standalone command is gsuite run model.yml for both solving and REML. It calls the native gsuite_model_driver executable. The greml and gsolve library names identify their mixed-model and numerical-solver responsibilities; they are not separate user commands. Existing R interfaces are unchanged.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Native capabilities and R availability
The request system is separate website infrastructure, owned by gsuite developer tools. Its Python/SQLite service stores email-verified submissions, private follow-up and maintainer decisions. Users may prepare a request in their own AI conversation or submit directly; the service calls no models and launches no agents. The static gtools portal contains a support entry and a copyable prompt; hosting is configured separately. The service has no repository write credentials or implementation authority and adds no R/native dependency.
Native greml’s conditional marker operator has an opt-in ancestral pedigree factor with exact sweeps for the remaining individuals. Greml owns the inheritance reduction and coefficient maps; installed gsolve owns the smaller sparse factor. Its reuse preconditioner shares the complete solve. The YAML frontend exposes execution.pedigree_factorization: ancestral_sweeps and checks native capability support; existing R interfaces remain unchanged. See the factor-reduction study.
The optional standalone HPC prediction frontend accepts CSV pedigree and phenotypes, PLINK genotypes and YAML covariance matrices. Its source-only pedigree-blend adapter composes public greml pedigree providers with the native conditional ssSNPBLUP PCG operator; numerical computation remains in greml, gsolve and genotype owners. The standalone model/task driver lives in greml apps/model_driver/; its input preparation, compiled-model tasks, packed-model tasks and augmented prediction routes are separate translation units. Tasks select supplied-value solving or REML, with optional uncertainty where supported by the model route. The driver consumes installed public interfaces; gsolve retains numerical solver ownership. Optional YAML truth evaluation is owned by the standalone frontend, outside the native model inputs. model_evaluation.py validates labelled targets and freezes cohorts from observed records; prediction_metrics.py is shared by the runner and the developer CSV comparison command. The worker evaluates only after an accepted native fit and collects targets, metrics and failure diagnostics with separate numerical/evaluation acceptance. Truth never enters record assembly, covariance estimation or prediction equations. See the greml/apps/model_driver/ organization. This standalone interface does not add R controls. See the representative workload and qualification.
The experimental compact YAML interface binds generic input columns, named effects, polynomial bases and natural covariance matrices. Its Python layer validates and expands declarations and labels results. Ordinary pedigree and joint random-regression solves use greml’s public compiled-MME facade; ssSNPBLUP uses the existing packed PCG route. Numerical model evaluation remains native. This standalone interface exposes supplied-covariance solving and deterministic sparse-direct REML for unstructured or factor-analytic genetic covariance and scalar/separable serial residual parameters; R interfaces remain unchanged. Whole blocks or named optimizer coordinates can be held fixed, with native free-score convergence and likelihood acceptance. Wide phenotype rows and long ID/trait/value rows lower to the same residual occasions. The frontend groups long rows by explicit record ID, validates shared mapped covariates and orders observed scalars by declared trait order. Native sparse incidence, covariance submatrices and solvers are unchanged; source tables and normalized observation rows are streamed through temporary SQLite storage, while pedigree/effect-level indexes remain in memory. Explicit correlated channels can bind different individual-ID columns while sharing one relationship and joint channel covariance. Python lowers these bindings, including weighted multiple-individual contributions per channel, to existing sparse record references; the packed native adapter uses all-record prediction preparation and retains its bounded record cache. Owner-filtered marker-weight training remains a separate strict contract. Selected-channel outputs distinguish individual genetic coefficients from record contributions evaluated at each channel’s mapped individual. Selected ordinary packed genetic uncertainty lowers explicit individual/trait requests to native target solves. greml reuses the fitted conditional PCG operator/preconditioner and its full or ancestral factor, and composes existing marker/H prior covariance actions. Python validates requests and labels results; it does not invert mixed-model equations. Every target retains transformed and original-equation checks. Stochastic requests compose gsolve’s existing variance-reduced diagonal estimator with that PCG action, using explicit sketch/probe/solve budgets and independent prior/posterior streams. Requests can select either posterior-PEV or information-covariance probing. The latter subtracts the same posterior action from the reported prior, then reconstructs PEV. Genotyped-only targets use G directly with batched trait products, avoiding extra pedigree solves; mixed targets use the existing H action. Diagnostics separate posterior query time from additional information-prior actions. Predictions and uncertainty have separate acceptance fields: finite imprecise candidates remain labelled unqualified, while numerical failures publish no uncertainty estimates. Regression, group and metafounder uncertainty remain outside this YAML adapter. Uncertainty CSV validation and relabelling stream rows directly to output, avoiding additional whole-population Python row/label copies. Stochastic PEV can isolate requested traits in residual probes. Greml maps reporting coordinates to colors and reuses the fitted PCG action; gsolve owns the generic masked estimator. All masked queries count toward the solve cap, while MCSE uses independent complete trait groups. The sketch and statistical model are unchanged. YAML exposes this opt-in choice as probing: trait. The compiled adapter also accepts labelled external relationship covariances, fixed interactions, composite identity-effect groups, Legendre/Chebyshev bases, grouped trait residual covariances and scalar/separable multivariate AR1/exponential residuals. It lowers to installed public greml relationships and residual components; Python does not fit the model or implement a new numerical solver. Dense relationship preparation and long serial blocks have separate scalability limits. Native compact format 7 is checked before result creation. Typed random-effect covariance declarations can supply FA loadings and specific variances. The frontend validates shape/order and materializes the small implied channel covariance for input inspection. Compiled prediction uses greml’s public FA random-group/natural-state APIs. Packed preparation validates the native FA layout and the implied covariance/used genetic precision, then reuses its existing channel matrix and PCG solver. Environment labels can select channels through existing long-format response bindings. No population incidence or new solver is introduced; FA does not reduce the number of genetic coefficients. Native identification and derivative work retain their scaling limits. FA estimation and uncertainty remain outside this YAML prediction integration. Univariate packed serial residuals instead lower group/position metadata and natural variance/correlation or rate to greml’s exact Markov-innovation record adapter. It transforms complete sparse design rows and responses once, with actual observed gaps and O(records) metadata, retaining scalar prepared blocks and the existing all-record prediction/cache path. It does not construct dense series matrices, alter the genetic model or add a PEV precision method. Multivariate separable serial covariance uses greml’s q-state conditional innovations preparation, including intermittent missing traits. Public gsolve eigensystems whiten the small observed-trait covariance; response and complete sparse incidence are transformed together and cached with identity residual precision. Compiled prediction consumes the same native cache. Metadata scales with observations and traits; sparse filter design history can grow with distinct coefficient columns in an incomplete series. This introduces no dense population/time covariance or fixed application RAM ceiling. Serial covariance estimation and industrial throughput qualification remain separate. Supplied-genomic ssGBLUP composes public greml genomic covariance/APY constructors with SingleStepPrecisionOperator and compiled PCG. The adapter passes explicit backend/thread and unlimited diagonal-workspace allowances, and retains the native exact marginal pedigree treatment. APY accepts supplied blocks or raw PLINK genotypes with ordered core IDs. The latter reuses native tiled BED preparation, a retained core factor and paired file-backed covariance/precision actions. Implicit H accepts those operators without constructing genomic precision CSC. Python computes means one marker at a time; genomic preparation RAM is O(core^2) plus bounded tiles and linear metadata, while the cross block occupies O(noncore*core) disk. No application RAM ceiling is imposed. Compiled ssGBLUP prediction omits unused H covariance metadata by default, preserving exact precision diagonals, determinants and PCG preconditioning. Complete metadata is an explicit setup option; native constructors retain complete metadata by default. Industrial APY preparation, precision-diagonal and prediction scaling remain unqualified. Compiled YAML models can supply metafounder Gamma and unknown-parent assignments through public native Pedigree. Explicit random genetic-group means reuse PedigreeGroupProportions; the example adapter materializes F once and expands compiled incidence, then reports individual F-gamma contributions. These are distinct models with independent dense-reference checks. The packed adapter composes GeneticGroupDataOperator with cached original records and an independent repeated channel covariance; inheritance and reporting remain implicit pedigree sweeps. It prepares exact group diagonals once with operator probes, without an n-by-g matrix or expanded record incidence. Supplied metafounders use full Qnn or an exact ancestral factor retaining all latent bases and their supplied correlated precision block. All models use the original precision actions; metafounder factors additionally apply an exact diagonal congruence with consistent solve maps for numerical balance. Group models also support ordinary ancestral sweeps. In metafounder models, only ordinary non-ancestral individuals enter the peripheral sweeps; all latent coefficients remain available. Combined base/group models are rejected. Compiled group incidence setup still has O(n times groups) storage. No new numerical solver, R control or fixed RAM ceiling is introduced. This schema is the sole standalone model interface; simulator output uses the same input/effect/covariance declarations and execution settings. The frontend streams CSV/TSV rows into a disposable SQLite snapshot, including long-input occasion grouping, residual bindings and record prediction grids. Prepared prediction targets are checksum-protected JSONL files read one row at a time during reporting. CLI preparation closes and removes its own temporary snapshot; optional execution.preparation.directory selects existing scratch storage. Pedigree and effect-level indexes, PLINK metadata and supplied dense matrices remain in memory. This reduces retained Python row storage without changing native equations or imposing a fixed application RAM ceiling.
Generic matrix-free reuse is owned by greml: adaptive trace-prefix extension and opt-in bounded warm/cache controls, with experimental solution recycling and residual trace estimation. gsolve owns the corresponding RHS-relative independent-PCG, supplied-product coarse correction and orthogonal projection primitives. These native options add no R control names; packed routes retain their existing caches.

Capability
Immediate boundary
Standalone R package

No; used through gbase and root gsuite

glma
Linear, logistic and LOCO association plus LD-aware marker-set evidence
Association evidence belongs here; enrichment belongs to gsea
Yes: glma


gbayes
Bayesian regression, fixed-variance single-effect summary inference, parameter learning and posterior calculations
Does not own fine-mapping interpretation or score application
Yes: gbayes


gscore
Scoring-specific transformations and efficient score application
Model fitting remains with association or Bayesian model owners
Yes: gscore


gmap
Regional fine-mapping, posterior-set interpretation and colocalisation
Reuses gbayes for Bayesian fitting
Yes: gmap


gcorr
LD-score and regional correlation methods, covariance models and MR
The gcorr(Glist, stat, method=...) workflow supplies common setup for ordinary LDSC, GNOVA and an illustrative SumHer baseline; HESS reuses stored eigen-region definitions and reference samples, projects reference-oriented Z/N arrays region by region, defaults to no sample overlap and returns compact moments. The ldsc() workflow accepts direct named Z/N arrays or checked single- or multi-trait statistics and Glist-owned LD, with stratified or grouped set models. LDSC, partitioned LDSC, GNOVA and SumHer retain marker identity in R and use numeric native arrays with integer jackknife blocks and compact results. Set names are resolved once to integer rows; disjoint grouped scores retain one membership and one value per marker through native fitting; compact multi-trait BED projections use physical marker/sample indices without chromosome-wide metadata copies for joint HESS without persistent LD/eigenvectors. The R adapter selects an automatic rank budget, records explicit genomic-control scaling and reports inference blockers. Native gcorr owns joint correction, the original HESS software variance systems and genome correlation jackknife, and the signed moment/strict conditional alternatives; compact R fits default to software uncertainty. Colocalisation belongs to gmap
Yes: gcorr


gsea
Gene-set enrichment, genomic-feature regression and chromosome-held-out gene ranking
Reuses glma marker-set evidence and optional gbayes pathway models
Yes: gsea



gbase is the standalone shared R package for task-neutral genotype, summary statistics and LD preparation. Its pure R getChromosomeSets() helper extracts disjoint chromosome marker sets from Glist metadata without opening genotype or LD files. gsim is the standalone R package for simulation. The root gsuite package contains the mixed-model and solver integration and the suite-level version and documentation interfaces.
The capability overview lists the analyses available through each package. The package-boundary guide records the dependency rules.
Scalar individual-level Bayesian scheduling and realized genetic-variance decomposition remain owned by native gbayes. The standalone R adapter exposes the existing controls, variance traces and scheduler continuation state; gact owns the worked simulation/prediction example. See the Bayesian guide. The scalar BED adapter summarizes VG, VLE, VLD and draw-wise heritability in fit$posterior using native posterior-summary routines and original chain draws.
Summary preparation accepts ordinary data frames, marker-by-trait matrices and gact Z/N lists. checkStat(..., ldcheck=TRUE, impute=TRUE) harmonizes alleles, checks reference QC and LD consistency, masks rejected scores, then imputes supported missing Z-scores. impute() runs prediction alone. Gbase owns the R contract and thin native orchestration: gbits counts packed genotypes, gmat reads complete regional standardized dosage, and gsolve supplies dense products, Cholesky factors and verified eigensystems. The adapter retains bounded local LD and compact score diagnostics; it saves no genotype matrices or LD files. Ancestry references are disjoint integer sample selections on the same Glist. Explicit covariance mixtures cover independent standardized meta-analysis scores with constant coefficients; they do not recover unknown study LD.
Both standalone LOCO methods use glma’s joint full-panel controller and gbayes’s batched prediction engine. infinitesimal_loco fixes one Gaussian/ridge prior with equal variance on empirically standardized markers; prior_selected_loco compares ridge/elastic priors. Blocked RHE and a shared Monte Carlo grid estimate global variances, which remain fixed for chromosome refits. glma owns the residual-offset scan and structure calibration, gbayes owns prediction fitting and Gram reuse, and gsolve owns matrix products. The standalone bridge no longer calls the slow chromosome-specific variance-ratio searches. See the variance procedure.
Named disjoint marker sets define separate genetic components in either standalone LOCO method. glma validates the partition, adds the unassigned background group and composes greml’s existing multi-component RHE estimator with the joint engine. RHE supplies a variance profile; the scalar Monte Carlo grid refines its total. Global component normalizations and parameters remain fixed during chromosome exclusions. No native gbayes or gbase interface change is required, and calls without sets retain their existing behavior.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Shared genomic resources
Glist is the serializable contract connecting data preparation with analysis. gbase::gprep() validates a PLINK panel and can attach sparse LD computed by gmat from gbits-backed genotypes. The same Glist can then be passed to analysis packages without copying the genotype or LD data into R.
gprep(task = "eigen", sets = regionSets) also prepares full regional LD eigenvalues directly from BED. gmat supplies centred unit-norm columns through gbits, gsolve supplies dense products and eigenvalues-only decomposition, and gbase attaches the named spectra and sample identities to Glist$eigen. The smaller sample-space Gram matrix is used when markers outnumber samples. This route is independent of sparse-LD cutoffs and does not fit a gene test. Analysis packages still require an explicit consumer interface for this resource.
flowchart LR
    bed["PLINK BED / BIM / FAM"] --> gprep["gbase::gprep()"]
    gprep --> glist["Glist"]
    glist --> glma[glma]
    glist --> gbayes[gbayes]
    glist --> gscore[gscore]
    glist --> gmap[gmap]
    glist --> gcorr[gcorr]
    glist --> gsea[gsea]
The Glist fields ldfiles, idsLD and rsidsLD identify the stored LD resource, its reference samples and its marker order. validate_Glist() checks the lightweight descriptor used by ordinary calls. verify_ld() performs the full sparse-LD integrity scan when a resource crosses a trust boundary.
Native consumers open one gmat LD reader per high-level call and reuse it across regions, traits, chains or marker sets. Regional matrices, independent blocks and eigensystems remain tied to the same Glist identity. This avoids repeated payload checks and unnecessary dense copies.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Analysis flow
Each R package validates task-specific inputs, calls its native implementation and returns labelled R results. Shared preparation does not blur statistical ownership:

glma fits association models and produces marker- or set-level evidence;
gbayes fits Bayesian regression models and produces posterior quantities;
gscore applies prepared weights, including Glist-resolved marker-set scores, while model fitting remains with the model owner;
gmap performs regional fine-mapping, posterior-set and Bayesian-FDR interpretation, and colocalisation;
gcorr fits summary-statistic correlation, covariance and MR models; and
gsea performs enrichment or PoPS-style gene ranking after gene or feature evidence has been prepared.

A connected association-to-enrichment workflow therefore follows:
flowchart LR
    stats["Checked association statistics"] --> vegas["glma::vegas()"]
    ld["Glist sparse LD or regional BED spectra"] --> vegas
    vegas --> genes["Gene-level evidence"]
    genes --> enrichment["gsea::gsea()"]
The VEGAS step processes the supplied marker sets directly. One sparse-LD reader prepares eigenvalue spectra in bounded parallel batches; the resulting ordinary R object can be reused across traits and sessions without reopening LD or repeating decompositions. Cross-gene covariance, when required by a downstream enrichment model, is a separate explicit input. Alternatively, glma reuses the full within-region spectra stored by gbase::gprep(task="eigen"); constant weights require no new decomposition. Nonuniform weights continue to use the sparse-LD route. gbase owns preparation and identity validation; glma owns the statistic and tail evaluation. VEGAS selects checked summary rows by marker ID and verifies their alleles; aligned database statistics need no reference reconstruction or manual sorting.
Method-specific controls, outputs and qualification limits belong in the method catalogue and the linked workflow guides, rather than on this architecture page.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Mixed models and numerical methods
The root gsuite package exposes the mixed-model integration. R formulas or explicit covariance components are prepared for greml, which owns model semantics, estimation, prediction and uncertainty. greml delegates general factorization and solving to gsolve. gbits supplies packed genotype operations, and gmat owns reusable genotype-panel and matrix resources.
Native greml also provides opt-in generic PCG identities and a separate common-scale profiled REML entry point for V = g K + e I. These remain native C++ controls; the existing R dispatch and optimizer defaults are unchanged. The changed native layouts require matching full ABI47 and core/adapter SOVERSION3 consumers. Focused numerical verification does not establish large-panel throughput or population calibration.
flowchart LR
    input["Formula or covariance components"] --> gsuite["gsuite R interface"]
    gsuite --> greml["greml: model and inference"]
    greml --> gsolve["gsolve: numerical methods"]
    gbits["gbits: packed genotypes"] --> gsuite
    gmat["gmat: genomic resources"] --> gsuite
    greml --> result["Labelled fit, prediction and diagnostics"]
The mixed-model guide explains this boundary, and the model catalogue records the supported model and backend combinations.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Dependency rules

Task packages may depend on gbase; gbase does not depend on a task package.
Task packages do not import the root gsuite package.
A task package may use another task package only for an explicit scientific workflow, such as the gsea re-export of glma::vegas().
Packed genotype decoding and algebra belong to gbits; panel identity, matrices and LD resources belong to gmat.
General numerical methods belong to gsolve; mixed-model semantics belong to greml; each other statistical method belongs to its task library.
New dependencies must follow this direction and must not introduce cycles.

gsim is separate from the analysis dependency graph. It creates ordinary R data that can be passed into examples and analysis packages.
Regional dense MCMC follows the same ownership boundaries: gbase maps marker sets and exposes full BED LD through installed gmat decoding and R’s BLAS; native gmap validates and binds the region, then reuses native gbayes sampling. Familiar argument adapters remain in the gmap and gbayes R packages. Native gmap owns qgg-compatible marginal-PIP grouping; it does not require qgg at runtime. gact imports gbase for shared marker-set mapping and explicitly installs the standalone analysis packages through install_gsuite(). Familiar QC, LD, MCMC and scoring arguments remain R adapters over their existing native owners. Bayesian PoPS splits chromosome folds and assembles predictions in the gsea R package; native gsea/gbayes owns nuisance projection, cross-products and sampling. Fold results retain posterior diagnostics without repeated training matrices. Standalone gbayes binds verified Glist LD blocks to native factorized BayesC/BayesR for mcmc-eigen, independently of the annotated SBayesRC model. Native gbayes owns retained joint-effect genetic variance and chain diagnostics; the R task packages arrange these into familiar post and conv tables. When the genetic reference is the fitted operator, accumulation reuses the cached residual quadratic. Both task R interfaces pass optional scalar-summary LD-swap controls to the existing native gbayes sampler; no sampler is duplicated in the R layer or native gmap. Native gbayes prepares the LD-neighbour graph once per fit and shares it across chains. Sparse-LD operators scan existing stored correlations; factorized operators derive neighbours from their fitted cross-products. The R packages expose pooled and per-chain proposal counts. Probability defaults to zero, preserving the existing sampler and timing evidence.
Standalone gbayes::gbayes(data=..., Glist=..., method="bayesc") and BayesR accept automatic phenotype-scaled BED priors with parameter learning and retained diagnostics. Scalar BED responses are centred on their original units; see the defaults and controls for initialization, explicit-prior compatibility and convergence limits.
Fixed-covariance compiled prediction selects value-only numerical assembly: base MME values, RHS and residual precision caches are unchanged, while global first/second covariance-derivative matrices and RHS arrays are absent. The full derivative assembly remains the default for estimation. This avoids O(parameter_count^2 * coefficient_pattern_nonzeros) storage that prediction previously allocated without using it; block-Jacobi inputs are unchanged.
The extended YAML adapters preserve native ownership. Fixed inherited group contrasts and independent group means compose public pedigree proportion operators with compiled incidence; combined metafounder/group models retain a separate ordinary inheritance base and metafounder covariance base. Explicit phantom group-parent codes are absorbed into missing-parent assignments, not biological parent nodes. Packed Gamma pseudo-EM runs through the existing native estimator on an explicitly declared absolute marker base; the verified prepared estimate rebuilds the prediction pedigree. No Gamma uncertainty is implied. PEV precision development has resumed with bounded independent-pilot allocation.
Sparse external natural covariance is streamed from an ID-labelled lower triangle. Greml retains its gsolve sparse factor as an inverse-action operator, with exact precision diagonal metadata; no dense inverse is formed. Supplied nonseparable trait-by-visit residual covariance lowers to the existing native patterned residual family. Within-unit grids remain dense and intended for moderate sizes. Format-8 transport is checked before fitting. Packed fixed and combined group models prepare ordinary inheritance proportions once, including reference-coded fixed contrasts as record columns. Their O(ordinary individuals × groups) proportion arrays are explicit preparation resources. No repeated pedigree factorization or dense genomic matrix is added. Independent-pilot PEV allocation chooses a fixed final sample count inside the posterior solve cap; pilot values are discarded. Industrial qualification remains separate.
Packed ssSNPBLUP REML now lowers to a native greml EM session with refreshed record precision/RHS and preconditioners, sharing the exact pedigree factor and packed genotype provider across covariance states. Natural genetic/residual starts, whole-block fixing, exact or bounded stochastic traces, score MCSE and dual equation-residual gates are explicit. Optional start-to-final restricted likelihood uses bounded exact references or paired matrix-free SLQ with separate MCSE/depth-sensitivity status. Default fitting does no global determinant work. The YAML frontend separates strict shared validation, analysis/thread controls, model lowering, native execution and labelled estimation reports into modules; the generic gsuite run model.yml coordinator reuses those same modules for every supported route/task. Preparation and fitting run in a private temporary worker, with native/CSV results and failed-run diagnostics collected to the YAML output directory. Process-tree RSS sampling is separate from native peak RSS; execution and collection timings do not change numerical qualification. validate and describe inspect model inputs without native fitting. Existing R interfaces and the YAML schema remain unchanged. The optional GenomeDK binary producer collects that already built native closure and relocates copied library paths. Its installer uses a fresh minimal Conda runtime and admits the artifact only after exact references and backend agreement; it changes deployment, not model compilation or numerical ownership. Native sources/R/build tools are excluded from the recipient payload. This private binary workflow requires actual Linux qualification and retains the existing redistribution limits. The standalone user guide owns installation and execution instructions; the GenomeDK validation record reports the accepted binary installation and its evidence limits. There are no legacy syntax aliases. See packed REML for the initial model scope and qualification limits.

title: Architecture reference
text:
Direct regression summaries
This describes development gbayes 0.1.6 and gsea 0.1.2 with matching native libraries. The public gbayes/gsea 0.1.1 archives do not expose these summary entry points or direct preparation routes. See release and development status.
gsea::set_cross_products(sets, y, universe) prepares independent-observation binary-feature summaries directly from memberships. Native gsea accumulates co-occurring set pairs through inverted membership lists, then centers/scales the dense Gram matrix. Genes outside every set remain in the explicit universe. gsea::blr(XX, Xy, yy, n) re-exports the general gbayes R adapter and reuses the installed native BayesC/BayesR sampler. The R adapter validates inputs and returns the existing posterior summaries and diagnostics; no new sampling engine is introduced. This route does not replace Bayesian pathway preparation with gene covariance or additional covariates.
The native Bayesian pathway adapter now also accepts PreparedSets directly for independent genes and an intercept only. It retains pathway-specific n-1 normalization and delegates inference to gbayes. General projected designs remain necessary for covariance, additional covariates and joint traits. The R workflow selects this preparation automatically where eligible, records preparation separately from native fitting, and keeps supplied gene statistics outside both clocks. Set-based PoPS can retain memberships through prediction.
Assistant instruction sources, ChatGPT launch generation and optional plugin packaging are owned by gchat. The website consumes a pinned public export; see website maintenance. Request submission, authentication and email approval remain in the existing gsuite request service unchanged.

title: From conversation to a reproducible analysis
text:
You bring the scientific question and study knowledge. An assistant can help inspect data, run R code, examine diagnostics and prepare a report using gsuite.
Help me use gsuite Report a bug or suggest a feature
Both entry points open the gsuite assistant with the same complete instructions ready; press Send once, then describe your task when the assistant responds. Analysis help and request preparation stay in the same conversation, reusing known details. Copy-and-paste instructions also work in another assistant. Conversations remain in your own account and are not automatically sent to gtools. Only explicit form submission creates a request; an analysis conversation or prepared summary does not submit anything.
This illustrative conversation uses the single-trait pedigree example; it is not a completed analysis. To run it, the assistant needs access to your files, R and the existing development integration. That interface is not provided by the seven public source packages; greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred. Website rendering does not execute the code.

title: From conversation to a reproducible analysis
section: 1. Start with the question and data
text:
1. Start with the question and data
You might ask:

I have body-weight records, sex, cohort and herd, plus a pedigree. Help me estimate additive genetic variation and predict animal effects. First inspect the data and explain any issues that affect the analysis.

The assistant checks the column meanings and measurement units with you, then inspects missing values, duplicated records, factor levels and phenotype distributions. It checks that observation IDs match the pedigree, parent IDs are represented consistently, and pedigree relationships are valid. Repeated measurements require particular attention: several records per animal may need a different model from one observation per animal.
For a reproducible demonstration, use the Prepare ordinary data frames section and the data preparation at the start of Single trait in the pedigree tutorial. That supplies pedigree and data, including BW, sex, cohort, herd and id. For your study, use your own data frames instead.
str(data)
summary(data)
colSums(is.na(data))
anyDuplicated(pedigree$id)
setdiff(data$id, pedigree$id)
table(table(data$id))
These are initial checks, not a complete data-validation procedure. The assistant records issues and proposed changes in a data-check summary. Decisions such as excluding records or recoding missing parents belong in the analysis script, with an explanation you can review.

title: From conversation to a reproducible analysis
section: 2. Translate the question into a model
text:
2. Translate the question into a model
You might ask:

Treat sex, cohort and herd as fixed effects. Use the pedigree for additive genetic animal effects. Explain the assumptions and show me the model code.

For the tutorial’s single-trait model:
\[
y = X\beta + Za + e,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(a)=\sigma_a^2 A,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(e)=\sigma_e^2 I.
\]
Here \(A\) is the pedigree relationship matrix. The model assumes independent animal and residual effects and a common residual variance. Whether herd should be fixed, and whether additional environmental effects are needed, depends on the study design and your scientific question.
The qgtools-style separation of effects, relationships and covariance components makes each decision explicit:



Model decision
gsuite specification




Fixed effects and animal grouping
Formula


Observations and explanatory variables
data


Relationships between animals
Pedigree kernel


Genetic and residual variance components
gvc() descriptors


Estimate covariance parameters
task = "reml"



library(gsuite)

PED <- gs_pedigree(pedigree, id = "id", sire = "sire", dam = "dam")
vcs <- list(
  animal = gvc(variable = "id", traits = "BW", kernel = PED),
  residual = gvc(variable = "residual", traits = "BW")
)
Starting variances are omitted here: gsuite uses its existing deterministic initializers. The pedigree tutorial also shows the short form, which expresses the same model with fewer arguments. The assistant checks the supported model combinations before suggesting an extension; a general specification does not imply that every model is implemented.

title: From conversation to a reproducible analysis
text:
3. Run and examine the fit
You might ask:

Run this model, retain the script and fit, and check convergence before interpreting the estimates. Explain any failures rather than silently changing the model.

fit <- gfit(
  formula = BW ~ sex + cohort + herd + (1 | id),
  data = data,
  vc = vcs,
  task = "reml"
)

summary(fit)
fit_diagnostics <- diagnostics(fit)
fit_diagnostics$status
fit_diagnostics$converged
fit_diagnostics$initialization
stopifnot(isTRUE(fit_diagnostics$status$ok),
  isTRUE(fit_diagnostics$converged))
coef(fit)
head(gs_ranef(fit)$animal)
This data-frame route defaults to CHOLMOD selected inversion and requires a build with CHOLMOD support. The check above stops the example before prediction plots and reporting if status or convergence is unsuccessful.
After checking status and convergence, examine estimates and residual patterns for unusual values or possible confounding.
plot(fitted(fit), residuals(fit),
     xlab = "Fitted value", ylab = "Residual")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
Record failures and unavailable diagnostics alongside the results.

title: From conversation to a reproducible analysis
section: 4. Turn the analysis into a report
text:
4. Turn the analysis into a report
You might ask:

Create a Quarto report with the data checks, model and assumptions, convergence diagnostics, variance estimates, animal predictions and residual plots. Explain what the results support and what remains uncertain.

The report uses the actual saved results. It identifies the data used, exclusions, software versions and analysis settings, and links conclusions to tables and figures. It separates predicted animal effects from observed phenotypes and avoids presenting a failed fit as a completed analysis.
The working directory can remain small:







File
Purpose




analysis.R
Data preparation, checks and model fitting


results.rds
Extracted estimates, predictions and diagnostics for reporting


report.qmd
Methods, results, figures and interpretation


session-info.txt
R and package versions



Save the reporting values rather than relying on an in-memory fit to survive between R sessions:
results <- list(
  summary = summary(fit),
  diagnostics = diagnostics(fit),
  fixed_effects = coef(fit),
  animal_effects = gs_ranef(fit)$animal,
  record_mapping = fit$record_mapping,
  fitted = fitted(fit),
  residuals = residuals(fit)
)
saveRDS(results, "results.rds")
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "session-info.txt")
The conversation helps develop the analysis. The scripts, extracted results and report preserve the work so you or a colleague can inspect and reproduce it without reconstructing the conversation.

title: From conversation to a reproducible analysis
text:
Continue with more complex models
The same collaboration applies to multitrait and longitudinal analyses: discuss the question, inspect the record structure, specify effects and covariances, run a supported model and assess the results. gsuite remains an R package with explicit interfaces; no conversational service is required inside the package.

gsuite source packages
Install the public gsuite R packages from the source repository:
options(repos = c(
  gsuite = "https://psoerensen.github.io/gtools/gsuite/repository",
  CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
))

install.packages(c(
  "gbase", "gbayes", "gcorr", "glma",
  "gmap", "gscore", "gsea"
))
These are source packages. Windows users need the Rtools version matching R; macOS users need Xcode Command Line Tools; Linux and HPC users need the C++17 toolchain configured for their R installation.

Direct source downloads
Release/development distinction: the public repository currently supplies gbayes 0.1.1 and gsea 0.1.1. Development documentation for gbayes 0.1.6 and gsea 0.1.2 includes newer BLR, set-summary and MAGMA functionality that these downloads do not provide. See the release-status table and check your installed package version and help.
Using install.packages() with the repository URL above is recommended because R resolves package dependencies automatically. The source archives can also be downloaded directly for offline transfer or installation on HPC systems.

title: Downloads
text:
Licensed standalone mixed models
The standalone gsuite application is offered only to licensed users. Its documentation, YAML specification and small examples remain public; standalone archives are delivered separately from the public package repository. See the distribution policy.
The command runs mixed models from one YAML file. Start with the quick start, binary installation instructions or complete ssSNPBLUP example. The installer creates a minimal Conda runtime without compiling. Binary archives are supplied by the maintainer; they are not public downloads here. See the GenomeDK validation record for tested installations.
The native greml and gsolve libraries own mixed-model inference and numerical solving. Their R packaging is deferred; separate or combined packages remain undecided. A root gsuite R package release is not currently planned.
The pedigree tutorials and other root-integration examples require an existing development installation. The seven source packages above do not provide that interface. Those examples describe the current development integration, not a promised future R package API.

title: Software validation
text: These focused simulation checks ask whether selected gsuite implementations behave as expected with known truth or independent numerical calculations. The statistical methods were established in the original literature; these checks do not establish them anew or cover every supported setting. Tutorials teach workflows, while Benchmarks compare performance.

title: Software validation
text:
Shared genomic simulation
The shared simulation design (gsim) fixes ten seeds, 10,000 individuals, 50,000 markers and known generating effects. Each page shows how to use one library and what was checked on the same datasets:

glma: association scans
gcorr: heritability and genetic correlation
gbayes: Bayesian regression
gscore: held-out prediction
gmap: regional mapping and colocalisation
gsea: genes and pathways

The worked analysis connects the six modules in one workflow. Results are descriptive for the specified simulation; the library pages state the relevant limits.

title: Software validation
text:
Other evidence

Standalone GenomeDK validation: accepted model/spatial REML checks, backend comparisons and the separate historical binary-installer evidence.
Earlier connected genomic checks: prior focused checks, including a separate reference-LD parameter-learning qualification.
gcorr method comparison: six summary-statistic methods on a separate two-trait simulation, with figures, replicated errors and availability.
Current scope and qualification limits: package-level and model-level checks that remain incomplete.

Evidence from different simulation designs is identified separately and is not pooled.

title: Tutorials
text:
Choose a complete analysis to learn how gsuite is used. Detailed options and data-preparation steps are collected under Guides; results used to assess the software are under Software validation.
For the standalone package tutorials, install the required packages from the source-package repository. Pedigree and root-integration examples require an existing development installation; greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred.
For the statistical background, read the mixed-model theory notes. They are independent of a software installation and cover both established methods and current research.

title: gtools
text:
gtools brings together gsuite, gsim, gact and gteach. Explore analysis tools and teaching materials through methods, examples and documentation.
gsuite is the ecosystem and documentation umbrella. Seven standalone genomic R packages are available from its source repository. gsim and gact are public packages with their own websites and repositories. gteach provides R- and Quarto-based teaching materials through its own website. R packaging for the native greml and gsolve libraries is deferred; separate or combined packaging remains undecided. A root gsuite R package release is not currently planned.

title: gsuite
text: gsuite is an ecosystem for statistical genetics, bringing together standalone R packages, reusable computational libraries and analysis documentation. The public packages cover genomic workflows. The standalone mixed-model application is offered only to licensed users; development R interfaces and public package releases have separate availability.

title: gsuite
text:
What can gsuite do?

Fit pedigree mixed models: specify effects and covariance components, estimate variance parameters and obtain predictions.
Work with genotype data: prepare resources, filter markers and construct sparse linkage-disequilibrium matrices.
Analyse GWAS summaries: estimate heritability and genetic correlation, fit covariance models, and perform Mendelian randomisation.
Fit Bayesian models: analyse traits or independent populations jointly, learn parameters and annotation effects, and summarize genetic variation.
Map and predict: run association scans, fine-map regions, assess colocalisation and reuse estimated effects for prediction.

Start with the capability overview for current R access and limits. The mixed-model catalog records specific LMM combinations and their evidence.

Mixed models for genetic evaluation

Genomic methods

Heritability and genetic correlation: prepare summary statistics and LD, choose score or regional methods, and interpret the returned estimates.

Gene sets and pathways: construct gene evidence and select an enrichment or Bayesian pathway method.

title: Benchmarks
Benchmarks
Architecture
text:
gsuite brings together R packages, native computational libraries and analysis guides for statistical genetics. You usually work through a task-specific R package or the standalone mixed-model command; the native libraries do the computation underneath.
Public documentation and the seven public R packages are distinct from the licensed standalone product. Development mixed-model R adapters do not imply a public mixed-model package release. The distribution policy defines these access boundaries separately from numerical capability.
The authoritative gbayes R design specifies the target six fitters and shared resource, result and execution contracts, with no backward-compatibility requirement. The initial bayes/mbayes packed BayesC/BayesR adapters reuse the existing native samplers and share a labelled bayesfit result, resolved execution plan and scientific access. The R/native bridge supplies prepared response cross-products and likelihood dimension to joint residual learning. The sbayes/msbayes summary adapters share that result contract and reuse the existing checked scalar/joint summary samplers. Sbayes supports sparse or block-eigen LD; msbayes supports sparse shared or independent study-specific references with an explicit sampling declaration. Summary prediction is unavailable without identified training coding. Blr/mblr consume exact labelled common-design cross-products through the same samplers/result contract; their R/native bridge constructs shared immutable cross-products and private chain state. PSD/rank/scatter validation and explicit saved prediction transforms preserve supplied feature units. Mbayes bayesFA/bayesFR now use the common contract and existing factor samplers. FA constructs one additive relationship internally through public gmat/gbits interfaces, preserving selections/frequencies, excluding/reporting monomorphic markers and normalizing mean diagonal to one. There is no supplied K or Glist$K. FR retains per-draw total-effect reconstruction, distinct activity summaries and saved sample-SD coding. Chains are serial and diagnostics are scoped to retained invariants; paused mixing limits remain.
All six public fitters finish through one R result boundary. It validates the versioned structural fields, ordered effect axes, final states and logical-chain identities after route-specific formatting. Missing availability entries receive truthful stored-value status and explicit unsupported reasons; factor prediction status preserves its training-only FA and saved-coding FR limits. Provenance records R/package versions alongside native metadata. This boundary changes no sampler, prior, numeric result or qualified prediction/continuation capability.
Individual C/R continuation restores existing native full checkpoints through the common bayes/mbayes fit contract. R validates same-build/data/resource identity and preserves global thinning with at most one checkpoint advance; no sampler transition is duplicated. Resumed summaries cover the added segment. Full resource hashing and mandatory checkpoint/segment allocations are checked. The summary C/R adapters also restore existing native checkpoints, binding harmonized scores/N, trait/provider maps, sampling policies and full prepared LD bytes; eigen fits additionally bind verified blocks and eigen settings. Their global thinning and segment-summary semantics match individual C/R. Cross-product C/R adapters restore the same full native states through existing Rcpp control slots. R binds exact checked XX/Xy/yy, n, feature/trait labels, prediction coding and likelihood dimension, preserving supplied units, global thinning and added-segment summaries. The declared gbase dependency is initialized before runtime fingerprinting. No native numerical or bridge changes are added. Specialized-summary, annotation and factor continuation remain outside these contracts.
Individual C/R posterior capture reuses native covariance, partition and selected score accumulators. R checks explicit reference/target identities and memory, prepares target copies with saved fitting coding, repairs known scalar coordinate labels, and maps native moments/traces into bayesfit. Observational capture consumes no RNG or extra sampler transitions, including resumed segments. Full effect draws and the remaining method/interface capture gates are unchanged.
Cross-product C/R capture shares the checked fitting XX operator with native covariance/partition accumulators through a thin Rcpp adapter. The explicit reference=“training” request reports B’ XX B / likelihoodDimension in supplied feature coordinates; projected designs retain their projected interpretation. No LD or allele semantics are inferred. Public access reuses the common quantity formatter with explicit component/variance-ratio meanings, feature/reference identity, budgets and ordinary-prediction availability. Native numerical library sources and sampler transitions are unchanged.
Summary C/R capture shares that formatter and uses the existing native accumulators on sparse/scalar-eigen and joint sparse likelihoods. Covariance reporting requires an explicit aligned sparse-LD reference over all fitted markers, including study unions, independently of fitting LD/eigen policies. Partition activity needs no reference; covariance and explicit-denominator h2 retain their native meanings. Per-call capture excludes discarded continuation advances and preserves states/RNG. Summary coding/intercept identification and prediction gates remain in place; no native computation is added.
Scalar bayes/sbayes now expose bayesRC through the existing native annotation sampler. The R resolver separates pi-derived coefficient starts from proper Gaussian priors and maps updatePi to annotation learning without a global Dirichlet update. Sbayes requires verified block-eigen LD and records its separate block residual policy. Native summaries keep prior probabilities, posterior allocations and per-chain coefficient traces distinct in bayesfit. No new sampler, joint RC model or full sblr parity is implied.
Sbayes also exposes existing point-normal and continuous-shrinkage MCMC through a serial native orchestration bridge sharing one immutable LD preparation. Point-normal preserves all-postburn conditional means and requires thinning one; shrinkage uses verified blocks and the common completed-multiple retention map. Method-specific scale/learning contracts and available paths remain distinct. Missing variances, PIPs, traces and RNG checkpoints are not manufactured.
Sbayes variational/mixture_variational routes use the same common fit contract over existing native fixed-prior mean-field solvers. A budgeted R/native boundary checks LD and replicated mixture-state allocations before fitting. Whole-panel coordinate convergence, ordered-window approximation and relative objective endpoints retain separate meanings. Fixed priors are not posterior parameter estimates; sampled chains, responsibilities and absolute ELBOs are unavailable.
The common bayes/mbayes/blr/mblr adapters accept method="bayesCM" and algorithm="vbayes", resolving fixed covariance dictionaries and optional native residual EB. Variational results use the shared schema with explicit optimization/availability diagnostics and no MCMC chains. Joint packed missing outcomes use the published native route; complete scalar packed CM uses bounded exact Gram preparation. The design records current source, normalization and prediction limits. The existing development Bayesian R facade accepts method="bayesCM" and algorithm="vbayes" (also the default for this method). The R adapter resolves phenotype-table/Glist or explicit matrix inputs to existing complete, missing or RSS mr.mash numerical APIs. Default covariance patterns/scales and argument aliases are R interface policy; inference remains in gbayes. Historical routes are unchanged. Bayesian YAML is not required for this R workflow.
The same facade maps method="bayesFA" and method="bayesFR", with algorithm="mcmc" as the default, to the existing mega_lmm and mega_bayesc native routes. It normalizes phenotype tables, keeps the bayesFA relationship kernel explicit, and maps familiar sampling controls to retained draws and chain seeds. Native priors, separate-chain outputs and scientific limits are unchanged. No additional numerical implementation or YAML schema is introduced.
For an analysis, start with Methods or the tutorials. For implementation contracts and detailed limits, use the Architecture reference.

title: Architecture
text:
Native capabilities and R availability
Native gbayes also has prepared-design Gaussian temporal block selection, discrete first-event risk-set and absolute-risk primitives, and Pólya–Gamma coordinate inference for sparse binary Gaussian mixtures and fixed-scale Bridge priors. Temporal residual-scaled and independent slabs are separate profiles. These native interfaces have focused small-model checks; they do not yet add an R healthcare workflow, full published-method reproduction, learned Bridge scales or a fitted competing-risk posterior. Existing dense references and sparse Gaussian-prior logistic operators remain separate supported native routes.
The direct SumHer workflow keeps LD-score calculation in gmat with the gbase R adapter, and paired fitting in gcorr with the standalone gcorr R adapter. R checks labels and shapes; regression and jackknife execute in native code. The default SumHer dispatcher uses stored D scores; the previous estimator remains available explicitly.
Native gbayes owns a separate bounded MegaLMM factor MCMC backend with one relationship kernel, loading shrinkage, variance-proportion grids and supplied outcome masks. It reuses gsolve and existing Gaussian/BayesC primitives without calling greml’s REML optimizer or changing mr.mash. Covariance and prediction summaries handle factor sign ambiguity. A separate native MegaBayesC marker chain learns marker-to-factor and direct effects, sparse loadings and their inclusion/slab/order scales. It uses installed gsolve operations, preserves separate activity summaries and saves training genotype coding for prediction. The standalone gbayes R package owns its R adapters and Bayesian YAML runner (gbayes.model/v1); the standalone mixed-model YAML schema is unchanged. Both factor routes are bounded to 256 samples, 128 traits and 16 factors; the marker route also limits markers to 4096. The packed marker route is resident, not a streaming implementation. New-kernel MegaLMM prediction and arbitrary fixed-covariate fitting remain unavailable, and full-model MegaBayesC mixing remains unresolved. Large-scale qualification remains separate.
Native gbayes also owns supplied-dictionary mr.mash-rss and complete-data individual mr.mash variational regression. It shares genotype/LD operators and gsolve conditioning with the ecosystem, while retaining a separate inference backend from multivariate BayesC/BayesR. This development route supports PSD covariance mixtures, learned weights and a bounded native prediction adapter. Dense and existing packed BED individual adapters share the inference engine. Exact common-sample C,S,H or individual residuals permit optional full/diagonal residual-covariance empirical Bayes; reference-LD summaries retain fixed covariance. Complete outcomes and consistent training centering are required. An additive missing-outcome adapter shares the engine and implements published conditional imputation/intercept updates, with covariance and entropy corrections. Its augmented variational bound is separate from the observed-data likelihood diagnostic. Joint fixed-covariate, relatedness and latent-factor learning are not included. Its R/YAML adapter lives in the task package and adds no task-neutral gbase computation. Calibration, external-LD robustness and large-scale performance remain unqualified.
Packed individual mr.mash and MegaBayesC adapters reuse the existing immutable BED provider and Glist physical indices. MegaBayesC fetches one decoded marker column at a time and retains its sample-SD/centered-raw coding. mr.mash BED keeps HWE coding. Both estimate imputation frequencies on selected training samples; packed prediction reuses training coding and validates marker metadata.
