Seven standalone genomic R packages are public source releases. The root gsuite R integration is development software; a root R package release is not planned, and greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred. The standalone command is gsuite run model.yml; binary availability is described on Downloads. Public and development versions can differ: check the release-status table.

title: Architecture
text:
Shared genomic resources
Glist carries checked genotype-panel identities and references to prepared resources, including LD where available. Analysis packages reuse that shared preparation rather than inventing their own genotype formats. Marker order, alleles, reference samples and covariance assumptions still need explicit checks. See the resource contracts.

title: Architecture
text:
Analysis flow

Genotypes or summary statistics.
Checked shared preparation.
Task-specific analysis.
Labelled results and diagnostics.

For example, glma::vegas() prepares gene evidence and gsea::gsea() analyses sets of genes. Required cross-gene covariance is a separate input, not something inferred by passing results between packages. See the connected pathway guide.

title: Architecture
text:
Mixed models and numerical methods
greml owns the statistical model, estimation and prediction. gsolve owns general numerical operations such as factorization and iterative solving. Available models, interfaces and uncertainty estimates depend on the chosen route; use the model catalog and its qualification notes.
The standalone frontend parses YAML and indexes observation/factor levels. Its development Linux runner detects the permitted CPU topology and selects native core binding within that mask, while preserving inherited NUMA policy unless interleaving is explicitly selected. Placement decisions are recorded separately from numerical qualification; see execution diagnostics. The greml contract exposes stochastic marginal-pedigree diagonal estimation for preconditioning; the model precision and its exact-diagonal interface remain exact. YAML lowering records explicit probing controls and requires a supporting native driver. Exact setup remains the default. Its LMT frontend separates directive translation from data conversion. A shared input contract binds optional conversion manifests without rereading large data; scientific numeric encoding is recorded and required for manifest reuse, avoiding unbounded decimal mantissas in real-valued exports; unsupported genomic ridge semantics block XML generation. Neither command executes LMT or claims numerical equivalence. See LMT preparation. Sample-mean centered pedigree-moment adjustment maps to LMT’s adjustg2a; the small comparison helper records native gsuite checks separately from live LMT adjustment verification.
Its DMU import/export frontend translates a documented ASCII linear-model subset between that YAML contract and DMU files, with source hashes, ID mappings and explicit exclusions. It introduces no numerical route or DMU runtime dependency. Wide fixed-design rank certification assembles sparse cross-products in the native driver and factors them through the public gsolve interface; it does not add a Python sparse-matrix dependency. Wide packed preconditioning likewise assembles fixed-effect precision from native records, uses a sparse inverse and bounds only the global aggregate correction. gsolve owns the reusable additive subspace action. Statistical equations and full coefficient dimensions remain owned by greml.

title: Architecture
text:
Dependency rules
Standalone job admission is separate from numerical libraries: development builds disable enforcement by default. An enforcement-enabled build requires annual entitlement for new jobs while admitted jobs finish. There is no runtime bypass. This is not a cleared commercial release; see standalone installation.
Task packages share task-neutral contracts through gbase; they do not depend on the root gsuite R package. Native libraries are reused through installed public interfaces. Statistical ownership stays with the analysis package. Developer details are in package boundaries and the dependency reference.

title: Architecture
text:
Direct regression summaries
The newer BLR and direct set-summary interfaces are development features in gbayes 0.1.6 and gsea 0.1.2, absent from the public 0.1.1 archives. See the release status and technical description.
Implementation does not imply broad statistical or performance qualification. Keep the current qualification limits and method-specific evidence alongside any capability claim.
Standalone observation precision, spatial residuals, selected prediction contrasts and additional-effect REML reuse greml’s model/session contracts. Genomic and parent-product matrix kernels belong to gmat; gsuite’s YAML layer binds inputs and labels results. These additions leave the existing R interface contracts separate. See model capabilities and limits.
Native gbayes development also exposes a fixed-prior continuous Gaussian vector conditional over supplied score/information matrices, reusing gsolve dense SPD solves. This conditional is reused by the bounded native fitting reference below. Ancestry storage, an R interface, model qualification and release remain separate.

Supplied-design Gaussian BOA reference
Native gbayes now provides bounded fixed-covariance Gaussian BOA regression with explicit dense ancestry-specific designs, exact joint posterior moments, same-response marker conditionals and genetic prediction. The caller supplies centred designs and a pre-adjusted response; fixed effects are not jointly fitted. Diagonal and full SPD ancestry priors are supported. This is a native numerical reference (at most 256 effects), with no R interface, packed ancestry operator, ancestry inference, covariance learning, scalable or routine BOA prediction claim. See the component gbayes/docs/boa-gaussian.md contract and development evidence. Implementation and focused numerical validation do not establish population-level scientific calibration, broader qualification or release status.


Ancestry-aware phased genotype operations
Native gbits now provides D, C, D-C*p, forward/transpose products and marker-wise information/residual updates over existing packed H1/H2 and known ancestry labels. Native gmat binds these operations to sample/marker/allele identities, declared phase alignment and training centring frequencies. Inputs use byte ancestry labels; resident labels are now bit-packed; no dense ancestry-expanded matrix or genomic relationship matrix is used by these operations. Missing genotypes, unknown/probabilistic ancestry and unphased dosage are unsupported; no automatic inference, harmonisation or imputation is performed.
Focused explicit genotype arithmetic checks and small gbayes integration examples are distinct from large-scale or scientific qualification. The existing dense BOA fitter remains bounded to 256 effects. Genotype operations alone do not establish a packed fitter, label persistence/streaming, R/YAML interfaces or biobank-scale qualification; the Gibbs route below has separate evidence. See component gbits/docs/design/ancestry_operations.md, gmat/docs/ancestry-panel.md and gbayes/docs/boa-gaussian.md for contracts, resource bounds and method-specific evidence. No release is implied.


Packed fixed-covariance Gaussian BOA sampling
Native gbayes now supplies a systematic marker-block Gaussian Gibbs route over existing gbits/gmat ancestry operations. It maintains one phenotype residual, reuses exact fixed-prior Gaussian conditionals, caches small within-marker covariances, accumulates marginal moments/selected covariance pairs, and supports selected sampling diagnostics, in-memory continuation and ancestry-specific genetic predictions with unchanged training centring. It does not allocate a dense ancestry-expanded design or complete joint marker-effect covariance.
The response is explicitly pre-adjusted and identity-aligned; fixed effects and variances are not learned. Execution remains serial; the initial byte-label storage assessment is superseded by bounded resident bit-packing measurements described below. Small dense-posterior comparisons with Monte Carlo uncertainty and existing regression checks are separate from routine large-panel, mixing/population and scientific qualification. There is no R/YAML interface or release claim. See component gbayes/docs/boa-packed-gibbs.md and its development evidence for contracts, resource bounds and limits. The bounded dense BOA reference remains unchanged.


Gaussian BOA robustness and resident label memory
Controlled native examples now cover ancestry-column aliasing, strong LD, ancestry imbalance and a rare counted allele at frequency .004. Direct conditional and residual checks remain numerically accurate, but LD marker contrasts remain poorly mixed after the tested continuation. Good selected prediction diagnostics do not qualify individual effect covariance estimates or covariance learning. Unsuccessful and inconclusive sampling outcomes are retained in component evidence.
Native gbits now bit-packs resident deterministic labels behind unchanged byte constructor inputs and gmat identity contracts. Bounded measurements show 8x label payload reduction for K=2 and 4x for K=3, with increased CPU cost and unchanged byte-import peak limitations. No new file format, statistical prior, covariance learning, streaming interface or routine biobank-scale qualification is added. See gbayes/docs/boa-robustness.md and gbits/docs/design/ancestry-storage-evidence.md for conditions, measurements, regressions and limits. Earlier validation/release boundaries remain distinct.


Bounded joint-marker Gaussian BOA updates
Native gbayes adds an opt-in fixed marker partition for exact joint Gaussian updates of coupled ancestry effects, using the existing conditional factorization, shared residual, packed marker decoding, summaries, diagnostics and prediction contracts. No more than 64 effects per block or 256 decoded sample rows are used in temporary design calculations. The original sampler and public structure layouts remain available with their established numerical and RNG update branch.
The fixed posterior, input identities and training centring are unchanged. The caller chooses blocks; correlations crossing block boundaries can still limit exploration. Conditional accuracy, Monte Carlo precision, measured resource cost and scientific qualification are recorded separately in gbayes/docs/boa-blocked-gibbs.md. This adds no covariance learning, automatic LD grouping, R/YAML interface, routine large-panel qualification or release claim.
In controlled duplicated-marker examples, keeping that pair together restores the weak contrast variance and substantially increases its effective sample count; splitting the pair remains unsuccessful. Independent Gaussian references and same-build continuation checks support the bounded update. This does not qualify unknown or long-range LD structures, larger partitions or covariance learning. Original unsuccessful evidence remains preserved.


LD-informed Gaussian BOA scheduling
Native gbayes adds fixed bounded partitions derived from an identity-checked gmat sparse LD resource, with optional BOA design scoring for explicitly supplied candidate pairs. Ancestry-specific likelihood-column correlation can differ from ordinary genotype LD. The builder reports strong supplied edges that cross the chosen groups and those left without a scheduled joint visit.
An opt-in route performs fixed cross-boundary Gaussian conditionals at recorded global sweep intervals, reusing the existing posterior and shared-residual calculation. Blocks retain the 64-effect ceiling and bounded sample decoding. The existing manual and single-marker interfaces remain unchanged. Missing graph edges, limited bridge budgets, collective LD and unverified large panels remain explicit limitations. This adds no covariance learning, adaptive priors, R/YAML layer or release qualification. Component contracts and method-specific evidence are in gbayes/docs/boa-ld-partitions.md.
Controlled fixed-covariance examples show improved exploration when a missing minor-ancestry dependence is represented and jointly visited. Collective LD directions still defeat the tested pairwise graphs and limited bridge budgets. Independent Gaussian references and exact continuation support the numerical transition; general partition robustness and covariance learning remain unqualified.


Matrix-free Gaussian BOA inference
Native gbayes now offers an opt-in prior-whitened precision operator over the existing packed ancestry products, deterministic posterior-mean solves and global Gaussian draws using randomized right-hand sides and gsolve PCG. The fixed-covariance, pre-adjusted-response model, sample/marker identities and training centering are unchanged. No genome-wide dense design, cross-product, precision or posterior covariance is formed.
Finite iterative solves produce numerically approximate draws. Independent bounded Gaussian references, tolerance/conditioning checks, selected posterior diagnostics and computational observations remain distinct from scientific or large-panel qualification. Existing single-marker, blocked and boundary routes remain available with their earlier mixing limitations. See component gbayes/docs/boa-packed-global.md for native contracts and evidence. This adds no covariance learning, ancestry inference, R/YAML integration or release claim.
Focused Gaussian reference and posterior comparisons support the selected known-phase LD, ancestry-imbalance and mosaic examples. Extreme-conditioning checks retain rejected covariance solves and inaccurate loose-tolerance draws. A bounded resource observation confirms small operator storage but substantial repeated genotype traversal cost; it does not establish routine large-panel use.


Block preconditioning for global Gaussian BOA inference
Native gbayes provides an opt-in bounded block preconditioner for the same complete prior-whitened Gaussian precision. Supplied disjoint marker blocks reuse installed gsolve factors; cross-block terms remain in every full operator application. The diagonal default, Gibbs routes and training-centering contracts remain available. No automatic block construction or posterior approximation beyond the existing finite solve tolerance is added.
Independent bounded references support means, covariance products, identical-normal draws, prediction, residual reconstruction and tagged continuation. Selected LD/ancestry cases and one 4,096-sample, 2,048-marker resource observation show benefits including setup costs; a poor extended-LD partition instead increased solve time. These observations establish neither universal speedup nor routine large-panel qualification. See component gbayes/docs/boa-block-preconditioning.md for the construction, evidence and costs. Earlier conditioning and partition failures remain applicable; global covariance learning and release remain unqualified.


Hierarchical Gaussian BOA covariance learning
Native gbayes provides an opt-in blocked Gaussian route with a shared inverse-Wishart SNP-effect covariance and fixed residual variance. It reuses packed known-ancestry designs, exact Gaussian conditionals, shared-response residual updates and existing diagnostics. Covariance-dependent factors are rebuilt each sweep; tagged continuation includes the covariance and RNG state. The initial interface supports one to four ancestries and supplied disjoint blocks of at most 64 effects. It has no R/YAML or global-learning interface.
Independent conditional checks and bounded two-ancestry collapsed-posterior references support the implemented route. Prior sensitivity, unobserved ancestry and identical design columns remain identifiability limits. A deliberately poor LD partition failed mixing criteria. The published heavy-tailed prior is supported, with covariance MCSE marked unverified when moment existence is unestablished. Empirical variances and low R-hat do not establish identifiability. See component gbayes/docs/boa-covariance-learning.md for evidence and costs. This bounded capability does not establish routine large-panel qualification, empirical population validation or release; earlier failures remain recorded.


Scientific evidence for Gaussian BOA
A bounded controlled population study compares pooled SNP-BLUP, separate purebred predictions, breed-proportion prediction and native fixed/learned Gaussian BOA. Known ancestry and common supplied centering are retained in future-generation purebred, F2 and backcross targets. Benefits depend on effect heterogeneity and reference composition; pooled prediction is competitive when breed effects are nearly shared. Oracle supplied covariance is distinguished from learned covariance throughout.
The study supports selected synthetic prediction and prior-predictive covariance calibration, while retaining poor boundary/low-variance recovery, prior sensitivity and numerous fits with inadequate Monte Carlo precision. Low R-hat and accurate prediction do not establish covariance identification. Matched-target fixed Gaussian comparisons support bounded blocked, overlapping and global routes; poor LD partitions still fail precision criteria. See component gbayes/docs/boa-scientific-study.md for the frozen design, complete results, costs and qualification decisions. These results establish neither published software parity nor routine large-panel or empirical-population qualification. Production algorithms, native interfaces and public release status are unchanged.


Supplied-tree covariance ownership
The optional installed gmat::arg target owns immutable supplied-tree resources, explicit diploid sample-node identities, branch-area covariance actions, fixed training centering and selected training/target products. It uses installed tskit C behind a private implementation and implements gsolve’s public operator contract. Existing greml covariance sums, REML/RHE and Gaussian prediction retain their statistical ownership. Core gmat::gmat consumers acquire no tskit dependency. This is bounded native numerical research support; genealogy inference, R/YAML integration, population prediction calibration and biobank qualification are absent. See gmat/docs/arg-covariance.md for the initial contract and independent evidence.


Fixed-score environmental moment cache ownership
greml owns GxeMomentCache and its phenotype-specific GxeResponseSummary. They compose installed gsolve operators and checked moment solving; packed callers reuse installed gbits covariance adapters and gmat panel ordering. The generic cache adds no genotype dependency to greml and no R/YAML frontend. Its factorized environmental sketches preserve ordinary fixed-effect projection and avoid an environmental-pair cache. See the owner contract (unpublished greml contract) for resource identity, mathematics and bounded evidence. The separate native sampling_covariance method composes these same operators and installed gsolve probes/checked solves to propagate Gaussian sampling covariance at an explicit SPD-certified working state. Numerical trace MCSE, working-state availability and interval calibration are distinct; there is no additional genomic storage or R/YAML interface. Learned scores, association, production-scale qualification and release remain separate.



Randomized G×E variance-component estimation: ownership
greml owns this capability, which implements the GENIE estimator and retains GENIE attribution. The existing native API GenieMomentCache is unchanged: supplied exposure-specific GxE/NxE kernels, GENIE finite Gaussian-probe moments, heritability fractions and genomic block-jackknife arithmetic. It composes existing installed gsolve operators/checked solves and gbits/gmat packed panel contracts without changing GxeMomentCache or adding a genotype dependency to the generic library. The owner contract (unpublished greml contract) and reference comparison (unpublished greml research report) define the full-rank SPD support domain and differences from original QR/output conventions. Annotation and exact published testing-tail parity remain incomplete. No R/YAML frontend, learned environmental score, new inference engine or release is added.



Annotation and numerical compatibility
greml’s native GenieMomentCache now accepts binary annotation/block operators and intersection counts, using existing gbits products and gmat identity contracts. gsolve owns the additive full-pivot Householder QR solve; greml selects it through the GENIE default reference QR option, retaining checked-SPD as an explicit choice. Statistical ownership includes overlap/deletion normalization and distinct published-result testing conventions. Contract (unpublished greml contract) and algorithmic comparison (unpublished greml research report) retain literal pinned-source quirks and provenance limits. No new storage framework, R/YAML frontend, learned-score engine or public release.



Selected covariance models and missing-data preparation
greml extends the existing GENIE cache with G/G+GxE/full-model selection and explicit original-row masks. Native tabular/one-marker helpers preserve the reference normalization and imputation mapping; gbits still owns decoding and packed products, gmat identities and annotations, and gsolve numerical solves. No new storage or inference engine, R/YAML frontend or dependency was introduced. See the contract (unpublished greml contract) and mathematical/software evidence (unpublished greml research report).


Randomized G×E native file adapter
greml’s existing gsuite_model_driver gxe application route owns keyed BED/phenotype/environment/covariate/annotation orchestration and reports; GenieMomentCache retains the equations and QR default. gmat supplies panel and annotation identities, gbits supplies marker decoding and direct packed covariance products, and gsolve retains projection/factorization/QR ownership. No native library ABI, R/YAML frontend or inference engine is added. The adapter contract (unpublished greml contract) defines alignment, frozen completion, blocks, budgets and output states. Existing routes remain unchanged.

title: Architecture
text:
Supervised environmental-score learning ownership
greml owns the new GxeMomentCache::score_objective and fit_score native research members. They reuse its immutable factorized cache, response binding, projection and installed gsolve rank-checked moment solver. Existing gbits/gmat operators supply genotypes and identity; learning adds no operator calls or new dependencies. GENIE and other native routes are unchanged. Regularization, variant splitting, learned-score inference and new R/YAML/file adapters remain outside this bounded capability; operator preparation is not claimed to be a single physical genotype pass.

title: Architecture
text:
Regularized score and variant-split ownership
greml owns the source-defined spherical threshold map and split orchestration over its existing GxeMomentCache and gsolve moment solver. Existing gbits/gmat selection, transformation and covariance operators supply disjoint normalized marker subsets. Held-out averages and full-marker refits are separate outputs; full moments combine cached actions before cross-products, requiring no third genotype cache or new kernel calls during fitting. GENIE is unchanged. No new numerical engine, storage format, R/YAML adapter or post-learning inference is introduced, and marker splits do not certify statistical independence.

title: Architecture
text:
Environmental-score uncertainty ownership
greml owns the new labelled inference primitives over existing G×E fits, including source-style numerical delta propagation and paired refit records/ observation-group comparisons. gsolve owns Student-t complement probabilities, reusing its private Boost.Math dependency. Existing gmat/gbits contracts still own panels/operators; deletion data and baseline/preprocessing definitions are caller-supplied. GENIE and its jackknife/testing behavior remain unchanged. No new inference engine, storage scheme, R/YAML wrapper or broad qualification is introduced, and probe variation is not silently added to phenotype SEs.

title: Architecture
text:
Native environmental-score workflow ownership
greml owns fit_gxe_score_inference: complete observation-group score/baseline refits and paired S2 summaries over supplied ordered y/E/C and native kernel operators. It uses installed gsolve contracts, fixed-transformation row restriction and existing single/variant-split learners; caches are streamed and compact failures retained. This adds no root R interface or numerical dependency. GENIE and the previous score/covariance algorithms are preserved.

title: Architecture
text:
ENGINE file adapter ownership
greml’s optional model driver owns the engine BED/keyed-table adapter. It reuses the unchanged GENIE input/QC/completion functions, installed gmat panel identities and gbits direct covariance operators, then calls the existing native environmental-score inference workflow. Observation grouping and explicit supplied starts/baseline/scales belong to this application route; no native solver or estimator changes are introduced. GENIE’s gxe command, root R interfaces and separate public launcher dispatch remain unchanged.

title: Architecture
text:
Individual-level RHE in gcorr
The standalone gcorr R package owns rhe() input alignment, Glist orchestration, method-specific summaries and results. greml owns ordinary RHE and GENIE estimation; gsolve owns moment solves and gbits owns packed products. Estimation does not invoke prediction or REML. Source distribution links ordinary RHE from the existing bounded gbase archive and compiles only canonical greml GENIE source in gcorr. The gbase greml closure is explicit and does not follow the expanding full native core. No root gsuite import is required.
Direct LD scores use gbase::gprep(task = "ldscores"). Ordinary values retain the existing lowercase Glist$ldscores per-component layout; architecture arrays and resolved settings are stored separately in Glist$ldscore_models.
SumHer fitting uses gcorr(..., method = "sumher"). The default marginal/pairwise route uses stored D scores when available, retains full-reference contribution totals and returns a distinct SumHer fit class. It returns h2 per trait and rg for all trait pairs. Select sumher_fitter = "standard" for the previous estimator; its compatibility entry point remains unchanged.
The standalone DMU and restricted four-trait LMT adapters share staged data manifests. Directive translation and data conversion are independent operations; the legacy combined DMU commands reuse the same parser and writer. Reverse LMT conversion requires explicit marker/allele metadata rather than inferring it from text dosages.
MiX99 I/2022 CLIM and ASReml-SA 4.2 preparation reuse the shared classification writer and interoperability manifests through classical_interop.py. Directive parsing/rendering is separate from binary64 table conversion; the admitted single-trait identity profiles exclude pedigree/genomic computation and never launch third-party software.

title: R package boundaries
text:
The R layer is divided by user task instead of placing every interface in one large gsuite package. The root gsuite package remains the ecosystem identity, website and development integration surface. A root R release is not currently planned; greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred, with separate or combined packaging undecided. Independently distributed task capabilities are R/native pairs: an R package owns the user contract and its corresponding native library owns the implementation. Each task package can be installed and used without the root package.


The dependency direction is:
gbase <- gcorr, glma, gbayes, gscore, gmap, gsea

task packages do not import gsuite
task packages depend on each other only for an explicit scientific workflow
gbase must not depend on a task package. Its public source distribution builds task-neutral gbits/gmat and bounded gsolve-core/greml-core source into a reusable static archive. A task package must not depend on the root gsuite package. This prevents dependency cycles and lets users install one task without installing the complete suite.



This is the canonical map of R/native distribution units. Method details belong in the capability overview; native transitive dependencies belong in the build manifests.








R distribution surface
Native owner shipped or linked for that surface
Status and boundary




gsuite
Root bridge over gsolve, greml, gbits, gmat and gbits::gsolve_adapter
Mixed-model, solver and integration interfaces.


gbase
Task-neutral gbits/gmat plus bounded gsolve-core and greml-core source
Shared Glist, summary-statistics, LD-resource and public source-build contracts. This is the deliberate exception to the one-task/one-native-owner pattern.


gcorr
libgcorr plus selected greml RHE/GENIE interfaces
Genetic correlation, individual-level moment estimation, covariance models and MR.


glma
libglma
Association scans and the native implementation of vegas().


gbayes
libgbayes
Bayesian inference and posterior prediction.


gscore
libgscore and libgscore_summary
Score application and C+T; model fitting remains with model owners.


gmap
unified libgmap with Bayesian support
Fine-mapping and colocalisation.


gsea
libgsea and libgsea_bayes
Enrichment; re-exports glma::vegas() for the connected workflow.


gsuite native dependencies
gbits, gmat, gsolve, greml and gbits::gsolve_adapter
Native infrastructure used by the public root integration interfaces.



gsim is the simulation package and exchanges ordinary data with the analysis packages.



Code belongs in gbase only when it is stable, task-neutral and needed by more than one task package. The package contains or will own:

allele-labelled summary-statistics data frames, marker-by-trait matrices and gact Z/N lists;
checkStat() mapping, harmonization and explicit QC of reported statistics against a Glist reference;
opt-in DENTIST-style LD consistency checks and quality-filtered Z-score imputation against ancestry-matched complete regional BED correlation;
validation of marker identity, positions, alleles and supplied numerical columns;
explicit allele-oriented variant keys;
gbase::gprep() preparation and sparse-LD publication plus the serializable Glist contract shared by individual-level task packages;
gbase::define_ld_blocks() one-time verification and serialization of an exhaustive independent-block partition tied to the sparse-LD identity;
summary-based marker filtering and Glist-owned LD scores, regional matrices, complete verified regional eigensystems, and reusable eigenvalues-only full regional BED spectra through gprep(task = "eigen", sets = ...).

checkStat() follows the established qgg workflow and preserves ordinary input formats. Its data-frame columns are rsids, chr, pos, ea, nea, with the available analysis columns among eaf, b, seb, stat, p, n and info. Downstream functions validate the subset they require. Gbase does not require a public summary-statistics class, constructor, accessor or print method.
The following do not belong in gbase:

automatic strand inference or downstream LD-model fitting;
genotype, LD or matrix storage;
statistical fitting, priors or sampler controls;
scoring, correlation or association algorithms;
orchestration across tasks.

title: Source-package repository
text:
The public distribution unit consists of exactly seven R source packages: gbase, gbayes, gcorr, glma, gmap, gscore, and gsea. The root gsuite package, gshare, and the complete gsolve and greml libraries are not part of this repository. The standalone mixed-model application is offered only to licensed users through separate delivery. Public package licences and release archives remain unchanged; see the distribution policy.
Users install from the conventional R repository:
options(repos = c(
  gsuite = "https://psoerensen.github.io/gtools/gsuite/repository",
  CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
))

install.packages("gbase")
install.packages(c("gbayes", "gcorr", "glma", "gmap", "gscore", "gsea"))
The repository retains the first 0.1.0 archives and publishes the current package versions in PACKAGES: gbase 0.1.3, gcorr 0.1.9, glma 0.1.2 and the remaining four packages 0.1.1. The publisher verifies the archive names, latest index and SHA-256 checksums before including these seven packages in the public snapshot.


As of 22 October 2026, the downloadable gbayes and gsea packages remain 0.1.1. The development sources in this repository are gbayes 0.1.6 and gsea 0.1.2. Publishing documentation does not rebuild or release these source archives.








Capability
Current public download
Development source

Absent in gbayes 0.1.1

The native gsea changes supporting these development features are not a public release. Existing source archives are unchanged. Use packageVersion() and installed help to establish which interface is available; the ordinary public installation command above does not install these development versions.



For a gact installation, configure these repositories before running devtools::install_github("psoerensen/gact"). gact imports gbase and provides the explicit gact::install_gsuite() helper for the full analysis installation. Loading gact never installs packages or downloads its database.



gbase builds the task-neutral gbits and gmat implementation together with bounded gsolve-core and greml-core source sets. It installs their public headers and one position-independent static archive for the task packages. The cores exclude sparse direct factorization, selected inversion, CHOLMOD, oneMKL, PARDISO, and the pedigree, longitudinal, and full mixed-model surfaces.
gbayes contains its R/Rcpp layer and Bayesian native implementation. In addition to its package DLL, it installs the public headers and a second static archive needed by glma, gmap, gscore, and gsea. Those packages therefore compile only their own native implementation instead of recompiling the large Bayesian source set. gcorr needs only the gbase archive.
Every task package links the installed archives declared by its R package dependencies, so no preinstalled gsuite SDK is needed. Native files in release packages are generated from the canonical sibling repositories. They are not maintained as copied source inside this repository.
The ordinary source-build requirements are:

Linux or HPC: R’s configured C++17 compiler;
Windows: the Rtools version matching R;
macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools or another compiler configured for R;
R packages Rcpp and RcppEigen; gcorr, glma and gsea also declare BH for their Boost.Math headers.

OpenMP is used when the R toolchain supplies it and otherwise the same source build remains available without OpenMP.


Development sources read OpenMP flags directly from R’s Makeconf, including the empty setting for a serial build. Both the source-package generator and Linux binary-bundle builder avoid querying the internal flag through R CMD config. The generator preserves package-owned LinkingTo dependencies, including BH. Native gbayes uses an explicit std::uint64_t multiplier in its Gram-cache byte calculation, avoiding the Linux integer-type mismatch. The glma bridge constructs its 34 LOCO diagnostics in smaller steps so that Rcpp 1.0.12 can compile it without changing the returned fields.
These are development repairs, not replacement releases. Existing public archives and frozen qualification records remain unchanged. Run the focused generator regression checks from the gsuite root with:
Rscript --vanilla tools/validation/test_source_package_build.R
To include compilation of the complete glma bridge against an archived Rcpp header tree, set SOURCE_BUILD_TEST_RCPP_INCLUDE to its inst/include folder, SOURCE_BUILD_TEST_CXX to the C++ compiler, and SOURCE_BUILD_TEST_NATIVE_INCLUDE to the installed native public-header folder. The focused check used the official Rcpp 1.0.12 archive with SHA-256 0c7359cc43beee02761aa3df2baccede1182d29d28c9cd49964b609305062bd0; the test does not install or upgrade Rcpp.
The existing native test_variational_prediction target checks the Gram-cache caps, and the glma LOCO test checks diagnostic names and order. Compilation against pinned Rcpp headers is separate from a complete Linux/conda package installation check; that platform acceptance is required before release.




From the gsuite checkout, with the canonical native repositories beside it:
Rscript --vanilla tools/build/build_source_repository.R
The command stages generated package sources, extracts source lists from the owners’ CMake declarations, builds and checks packages in dependency order, installs them into an isolated library, and writes the seven archives plus PACKAGES, PACKAGES.gz, PACKAGES.rds, and SHA256SUMS under repository/src/contrib. Release assembly requires the R package openssl to calculate SHA-256 checksums; end users do not need it unless another dependency requires it.
Use --stage-only to inspect generated source, --build-only to assemble the archives without compiling them, and --skip-check for an installation smoke build. --from=<package> resumes an interrupted ordered run. Those modes are partial validation. --only=<package> builds and checks one package using already installed compatible prerequisites in the isolated library; it leaves other release archives unchanged.
Approved contents under repository/ are tracked as release artifacts. All staging, check, object, and installation outputs remain generated and ignored. The build command itself never deploys, pushes, or changes GitHub Pages.



Before each publication, review package versions, source-check results on release platforms, licence notices, archive contents and checksums, absence of private source, and the website wording. Running the documented website publisher copies the approved release into site/gsuite/repository in the public gtools checkout. Pushing that reviewed snapshot activates the gtools GitHub Pages deployment workflow.
For local development qualification without changing public archives or their index, use --local-only, optionally --library=ABSOLUTE_PATH and --only=gbase or --only=gcorr. The latter must follow installation of its matching gbase dependency. Generated package staging replaces only the selected package. The gcorr development source adds canonical greml GENIE source while retaining the explicitly bounded gbase native closure.
The individual-level RHE development interface requires gbase 0.1.4 and gcorr 0.1.10. These development versions bind the source-built numerical contracts; they do not change the existing downloadable releases or public index.



The generated custom installer preserves R’s unfiltered object symbol tables as libs/<arch>/symbols.rds. Static archive producers also install their native object tables beside the archive (libgsuite_core.a.symbols.rds in gbase and libgbayes_core.a.symbols.rds in gbayes). Consumers include every table from their linked project archives, with owner-qualified names, so compiled-code checks cover archive code as well as the package’s own objects.
Ordinary source installations generate the tables through R’s own object-symbol reader when the normal check-generated file is absent and nm is available. Missing or incomplete evidence leaves the conservative DLL-level check in place; a partial table is never installed. No symbols are removed or whitelisted, no termination calls are intercepted, and compiled-code checking remains enabled. tools/validation/check_compiled_symbol_metadata.R checks complete metadata, positive detection of a direct termination reference, and the missing-dependency fallback. This build evidence does not change numerical or statistical code.

title: Formula and variance-component compiled-MME REML
text:
For the new data-frame shorthand, optional starts, fixed solves and genetic random regression, begin with Pedigree analysis. Both formula and formulas now use the same general adapter. This page documents the specialized compiled-MME route, explicitly requested with a gs_fit_control() object, complete explicit covariance starts, and task = "reml" (or greml() with those same controls). Its result layout remains specialized and does not support the gsolve(fit) handoff. Supplying starts alone does not select it. General fits accept named controls for the selected pedigree or component fitter. Compiled controls now default to CHOLMOD selected inversion.
The data-frame gs_pedigree() constructor described here is distinct from gs_model_pedigree(), the ordered-parent constructor used by the persistent-model API. The two signatures are not interchangeable and do not dispatch implicitly.
greml() is the estimation entry point; gfit() remains available with task = "reml". Model incidence comes from formulas, pedigree relationships come from gs_pedigree(), and explicit positive-interior covariance starts come from named gvc() components. The interface lowers one immutable model to greml’s public compiled-MME plan, creates one numerical session, optimizes, and finalizes BLUPs from the retained accepted response state.
PED <- gs_pedigree(pedigree, id = "id", sire = "sire", dam = "dam")

fit <- gfit(
  BW ~ sex + batch + (1 | id),
  records,
  list(
    animal = gvc("id", "BW", PED, start = 1),
    residual = gvc("residual", "BW", start = 1)
  ),
  control = gs_fit_control(direct_backend = "cholmod")
)
For multiple traits, formulas is a named list and each component start is an SPD matrix in the declared trait order. Each trait has a separate fixed-effect block. Scalar records are ordered by formula-list order and original data-row order. An NA response is absent; observed traits from the same data row form one complete or incomplete patterned residual unit. Missing fixed covariates, nonfinite observed responses, and missing pedigree identifiers are errors.


From the repository root, with gsuite installed, run:
source("tools/examples/run_single_trait_pedigree_example.R")
The complete example starts with two ordinary data frames: data has one observation per row (id, BW, factor sex, continuous covariate x); pedigree has one animal per row (id, sire, dam). It reuses the small deterministic BW formula-test illustration, not a random draw from the fitted pedigree model. Its artificial sex labels vary across records of an animal; real data should use consistent animal sex. These toy values illustrate the API, not biological inference or variance recovery.
The formula BW ~ sex + x + (1 | id) supplies fixed effects and animal incidence. A separate gs_pedigree() relationship and named animal and residual components supply covariance structure and positive starting variances. Under this model, animal covariance is the pedigree relationship times the animal variance; residuals are independent with a common variance. Repeated observations share the animal effect, with no additional permanent environment effect. Starts are not fixed variances.
IDs, not row positions, align the tables. Pedigree rows may be reordered; unknown parents use NA, while known parents must be listed. Observation IDs absent from the pedigree are errors. Animal a8 has no observations but remains in the pedigree and receives a conditional animal prediction from relatives.
summary(fit) displays covariance estimates and convergence, coef(fit) returns fixed effects, and the public fit$random_effects$animal table contains IDs and animal BLUPs (not full predicted body weights). fit$converged and fit$convergence_reason expose the stopping result. Prediction tables follow pedigree order, so compare them by ID. Prediction for new data and prediction uncertainty are not supported on this formula route.
For development verification only, select the existing isolated installation before sourcing the same example:
.libPaths(c(file.path("build", "r-library"), .libPaths()))
source("tools/examples/run_single_trait_pedigree_example.R")



The only random grammar is exactly (1 | variable). A scalar formula has one or two distinct terms, with at most one pedigree component and one independent identity component. Multitrait formulas retain one shared pedigree term. Random slopes, more than two terms, duplicate terms, ||, nesting, crossing, functions, interactions, and expressions on the grouping side are rejected. After removing the random terms, base R model.frame() and model.matrix() build the fixed design and preserve coefficient names, contrasts, factor levels, and the formula environment.
Random incidence is never materialized as an R matrix. Each observed scalar record supplies a pedigree entity ID, trait/member ID, residual unit and coordinate, and a unit random-intercept weight directly to the compiled-MME specification. This first version may materialize a dense R fixed-effect model.matrix() and therefore targets moderate in-memory data frames.



Scalar fits accept one identity component, one pedigree component, or one of each, plus one homogeneous residual component. Formula order determines the random coefficient blocks and covariance-parameter order. Pedigree levels use external pedigree order, including unphenotyped animals. Identity levels use the sorted observed character or integer domain. Every record contributes a unit weight directly to each present component, including the data-induced pedigree/identity cross block; no R incidence matrix is built.
For example, repeatability and a common-environment model use the same bounded composition rule:
ID <- gs_identity()
repeatability <- gfit(

title: Formula and variance-component compiled-MME REML
text:
From the repository root, with gsuite installed, run:
source("tools/examples/run_single_trait_pedigree_example.R")
The complete example starts with two ordinary data frames: data has one observation per row (id, BW, factor sex, continuous covariate x); pedigree has one animal per row (id, sire, dam). It reuses the small deterministic BW formula-test illustration, not a random draw from the fitted pedigree model. Its artificial sex labels vary across records of an animal; real data should use consistent animal sex. These toy values illustrate the API, not biological inference or variance recovery.
The formula BW ~ sex + x + (1 | id) supplies fixed effects and animal incidence. A separate gs_pedigree() relationship and named animal and residual components supply covariance structure and positive starting variances. Under this model, animal covariance is the pedigree relationship times the animal variance; residuals are independent with a common variance. Repeated observations share the animal effect, with no additional permanent environment effect. Starts are not fixed variances.
IDs, not row positions, align the tables. Pedigree rows may be reordered; unknown parents use NA, while known parents must be listed. Observation IDs absent from the pedigree are errors. Animal a8 has no observations but remains in the pedigree and receives a conditional animal prediction from relatives.
summary(fit) displays covariance estimates and convergence, coef(fit) returns fixed effects, and the public fit$random_effects$animal table contains IDs and animal BLUPs (not full predicted body weights). fit$converged and fit$convergence_reason expose the stopping result. Prediction tables follow pedigree order, so compare them by ID. Prediction for new data and prediction uncertainty are not supported on this formula route.
For development verification only, select the existing isolated installation before sourcing the same example:
.libPaths(c(file.path("build", "r-library"), .libPaths()))
source("tools/examples/run_single_trait_pedigree_example.R")

title: Formula and variance-component compiled-MME REML
text:
The only random grammar is exactly (1 | variable). A scalar formula has one or two distinct terms, with at most one pedigree component and one independent identity component. Multitrait formulas retain one shared pedigree term. Random slopes, more than two terms, duplicate terms, ||, nesting, crossing, functions, interactions, and expressions on the grouping side are rejected. After removing the random terms, base R model.frame() and model.matrix() build the fixed design and preserve coefficient names, contrasts, factor levels, and the formula environment.
Random incidence is never materialized as an R matrix. Each observed scalar record supplies a pedigree entity ID, trait/member ID, residual unit and coordinate, and a unit random-intercept weight directly to the compiled-MME specification. This first version may materialize a dense R fixed-effect model.matrix() and therefore targets moderate in-memory data frames.

title: gs_genotypes preparation contract
text:
gbase::gprep() implements the bounded "prepare", "sparseld", and "eigen" tasks. For preparation, gbase owns argument validation, orchestration, and the returned R descriptor; gmat owns strict BIM/FAM parsing and exact ordered multi-file identity; gbits owns BED header, size, offset, packed-code, and threaded count logic. The existing SNP-major PLINK BED files remain the sole persistent genotype representation. qgg is a read-only behavioural and scientific reference and is not a runtime dependency.
Sparse-LD orchestration is specified separately in sparse-LD preparation. gbase::gprep() does not add separate LD-score tasks: gbase::ld_scores(), ld_region(), and ld_eigen() consume the augmented Glist directly. Genetic-map import, GRMs, association, scoring, and other qgg tasks are not implemented by gbase::gprep(). Marker filtering is provided separately by gbase::gfilter(). Unknown preparation tasks fail explicitly.



Every BED/BIM/FAM vector is nonempty and has identical length. Omitted companions are derived by replacing only a final case-insensitive .bed suffix. Every path is normalized and must name an existing regular file. gbits requires the exact header 6c 1b 01 and exact size \(3+M\lceil N/4\rceil\); individual-major, truncated, and trailing-byte inputs fail.
The first FAM supplies ids and the complete physical sample order. Individual IDs are nonempty and globally unique. gmat requires every component to have the same exact ordered (family_id, individual_id) sequence; no set-only check or positional permutation is used. With ids = NULL, all samples contribute and study_ids is NULL. A supplied vector is nonempty, unique, nonmissing, fully resolved, retained in caller order, and used only as the summary sample set; ids remains complete.
Every BIM row has six fields, a nonempty chromosome and marker ID, finite nonnegative map position, positive physical position, and distinct nonempty alleles. Source marker IDs are globally unique across every supplied BIM, including unselected rows. BIM order is canonical. A supplied rsids vector is validated completely, then filtered in file/BIM order; caller order is intentionally not retained because the public descriptor remains a file-partitioned physical view. source_marker_indices_0based records every original BIM/BED index, including noncontiguous selections. BED is never rewritten.



a1 is BIM field 5 and a2 BIM field 6. Counts and frequencies always refer to copies of a1:



PLINK code
Copies of a1
Count




00

n2

n1

For \(N_{\mathrm{obs}}=n_0+n_1+n_2\), the returned values are \(\mathrm{af}=\frac{2n_2+n_1}{2N_{\mathrm{obs}}}\), \(\mathrm{af}_1=\mathrm{af}\), \(\mathrm{af}_2=1-\mathrm{af}\), \(\mathrm{maf}=\min(\mathrm{af},1-\mathrm{af})\), \(\mathrm{hom}=(n_0+n_2)/N_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\mathrm{het}=n_1/N_{\mathrm{obs}}\). All-missing selected markers fail with their marker ID. Empirical frequencies are not clipped: monomorphic values are exactly zero or one. This deliberately differs from the tested qgg 1.1.6 reference, whose summaryBED() clips frequencies to [0.00001, 0.99999] and substitutes 0.5 for all-missing markers.



The result is a plain list with class c("gs_genotypes", "Glist"). It carries study, normalized bedfiles/bimfiles/famfiles, complete ids, optional study_ids, n, nchr, m, chromosome/file-wise rsids, mchr, chr, pos, map, a1, a2, cpra, af, af1, af2, maf, nmiss, hom, het, n0, n1, n2, assembly = NULL, physical sample/marker mappings, format and ordering labels, and provenance. It contains neither dense genotypes nor a mandatory external pointer and therefore survives an exact saveRDS()/readRDS() round trip.
gsim has a native bounded BED reader for Glist-backed simulation. It resolves selected sample and marker IDs against FAM/BIM files, checks allele orientation, and reads selected BED blocks. A custom deterministic getG_fun remains an explicit alternative. Check the installed gsim version before use.



Use gbase::getChromosomeSets() to extract chromosomes directly from Glist metadata, without reading BED or LD:
sets <- getChromosomeSets(Glist)
Each chromosome supplies one named, disjoint set covering its markers. Chromosomes retain their first-occurrence order and members retain reference/BIM order. Grouping uses chromosome labels rather than BED file boundaries, so it also works with a single file containing all chromosomes. Pass these sets to glma(..., sets=sets) for chromosome variance components.



Keep gaps when extracting database statistics, then prepare all trait columns against the eligible markers in Glist:
stat <- gact::getMarkerStat(GAlist, studyID=c("GWAS1", "GWAS2"), rm.na=FALSE)
stat <- checkStat(Glist, stat, ldcheck=TRUE, impute=TRUE, nthreads=4)
attr(stat, "ldcheck")$original
attr(stat, "imputation")$r2
The same call accepts a summary data frame or a numeric marker-by-trait matrix with marker row names. For a data frame, Z is taken from stat/z, derived from b/seb, or selected with columns=. Alleles are harmonized once; matrix/list alleles can be supplied in the marker_alleles attribute. Without allele metadata, scores must already use Glist’s a1 coding. Ordinary data-frame checkStat() calls retain the established behavior when both options are off. Use impute(Glist, stat) for prediction alone on already aligned input.
Accepted observed Z-scores are preserved. LD-rejected observations are retained in the diagnostic table, masked, and then eligible for imputation. Reference QC exclusions stay excluded; predictions below r2=0.6 remain missing. Diagnostics are attributes on the ordinary input format. Known sample sizes are retained; missing sizes and effect/SE/P fields for new or repaired scores are not inferred. Analyses using imputed scores must account for prediction uncertainty and supply any required sample-size or effect information.
For several ancestries, label samples on the existing descriptor:
Glist <- setReferenceGroups(Glist, list(EUR=eur_ids, EAS=eas_ids))
stat <- checkStat(Glist, stat, ldcheck=TRUE, impute=TRUE)
Groups are disjoint subsets of the prepared samples and are stored as one-based integer indices. Gact carries study ancestry in attr(stat, "ancestry"); an explicit ancestry=c(GWAS1="EUR", GWAS2="EAS") overrides it. Several reference groups require one ancestry choice per trait. A preselected, unlabeled single reference remains supported for one common ancestry.
An explicit ancestry_weights=c(EUR=0.8, EAS=0.2) uses Rmix = 0.8 R_EUR + 0.2 R_EAS; a group-by-trait matrix allows different weights per column. Weights are squared standardized coefficients for independent meta-analysis Z-scores, constant across markers. They are not inferred from the scores and are not a general model of individual admixture or changing study composition/overlap. Allele-frequency differences are checked for pure ancestry columns; covariance weights do not identify a pooled meta-analysis frequency. Reference MAF, missingness and HWE are checked within each contributing ancestry, without pooling populations for HWE.
Imputation uses ridge-conditioned complete regional BED correlation, with lambda=0.1, 1 Mb cores and 250 kb buffers. The default max_markers=2048 bounds local decoded genotypes and dense matrices; dense cores split and their buffers shorten. Matching ancestry and missingness masks reuse factors across traits. No imputed prediction becomes a predictor, no genome-wide LD matrix is built, and no LD or eigenvector files are saved. Stored sparse-LD thresholds are not used. Reference sample selections and allele coding must match the intended downstream LD model.
LD checking uses deterministic repeated held-out partitions, a truncated eigensystem and a default threshold of 5e-8. Near-perfect LD clusters stay in one partition so their members cannot predict each other. This is a DENTIST-style adaptation with bounded windows and clustered partitions; it is not a reproduction of the original program. All checking finishes before imputation, using a second bounded reference pass where predictions are needed. P values and reference prediction quality are approximate. The original DENTIST study recommends at least 5,000 reference individuals. Small deterministic tests verify the computation; genome-scale speed and mismatch calibration have not been established for this new route.
The formulas follow ImpG-Summary and the consistency checks follow DENTIST.



regionSets <- list(region1 = Glist$rsids[[1]][1:100])
Glist <- gprep(Glist, task = "eigen", sets = regionSets, nthreads = 4)
Glist$eigen$values$region1
saveRDS(Glist, "Glist-with-spectra.rds")
sets is a nonempty uniquely named list of marker-ID vectors. All markers must exist in Glist, duplicates are rejected, and each set must belong to one chromosome. Sets may overlap and need not be contiguous. Marker membership is stored in reference/BIM order. The samples default to study_ids when present, otherwise all ids; an explicit ids argument selects and records another reference sample set. At least two samples are required.
gmat reads unit-norm centred regional dosage columns through gbits. Missing calls are imputed to the observed marker mean; constant or all-missing markers fail with their ID. gsolve computes dense products and eigenvalues only. The spectrum is that of full within-set correlation, without sparse-LD thresholds or distance windows. No eigenvectors, clipping, statistical test, or persistent LD files are produced.
For N selected samples and M markers, the smaller Gram matrix is used. When M exceeds N, the sample-space spectrum is padded with M-N exact zeros and sorted to retain the full M-value spectrum. Floating-point null eigenvalues can differ from a full marker-space decomposition at rounding level. The default eigen_control$maximum_dimension = 2048 applies to min(N, M), not M. One region is processed at a time with O(NM + min(N,M)^2) scratch storage; only O(M) values and region identities remain on Glist. nthreads controls gbits decoding, while the current portable gsolve product and Eigen spectrum backends are serial and do not require OpenBLAS. No global thread setting is changed.
Glist$eigen records named sets, descending values, native diagnostics, selected sample IDs and offsets, controls, and provenance. It survives ordinary RDS persistence. validate_Glist() checks its identities and spectrum shape; it does not recompute the eigenvalues. If a downstream analysis removes markers or changes the reference samples, prepare matching spectra again. glma::prepare_vegas(Glist) reuses the stored spectra; sets may select named regions but must preserve their full membership. Its prepared$markers holds the union of requested markers in reference order. glma::vegas() selects checked statistic rows by marker ID, so the data may contain additional markers or another row order. All required markers and their reference alleles must be present; no QC or allele harmonization is repeated during fitting. Constant positive weights within each set are supported. For nonuniform weights, use glma’s existing sparse-LD preparation on a Glist without the unweighted eigen resource. Save the prepared object to evaluate subsequent traits without reopening the original BED files. gsea re-exports both functions.



gbits scans packed marker records directly. Selected original offsets are checked with 64-bit arithmetic. Threaded execution assigns deterministic static marker partitions and never calls R from workers. Temporary native storage is \(O(T\lceil N/4\rceil)\) packed bytes for T workers plus \(O(M)\) counts and selection mappings; preparation does not build an \(O(NM)\) decoded matrix. The separate regional eigen task uses the bounded regional scratch described above.

title: Numerical and mixed-model routes
text:
This guide explains route choice and scaling. The model catalog owns capability status, the primitive registry owns reusable mechanism mappings, and architecture owns package dependencies. A native primitive does not establish a qualified public R route.


These examples use the existing root development integration. They are not provided by the seven public source packages. Future greml/gsolve R packaging is deferred, and its interface and separate or combined distribution are not yet decided.
greml() estimates variance components; gsolve() holds them fixed and returns fixed effects and random-effect predictions. Both use the same formula/data/pedigree and explicit gvc() specifications as gfit().
fit <- greml(formula = BW ~ sex + (1 | id),
             data = data, pedigree = pedigree)
summary(fit)
fit$variance_components

# The same model/data specification, now with fixed covariance values.
solved <- gsolve(formula = BW ~ sex + (1 | id), data = data,
                 pedigree = pedigree, vc = c(id = 1, residual = 1))

# Optional shortcut: reuse the prepared model and its fitted covariance values.
resolved <- gsolve(fit)
resolved_pcg <- gsolve(fit, control = list(linear_solver = "pcg"))
Starting values are optional for greml(). Direct gsolve() calls require all covariance values. For gsolve(fit), the default is to use the fitted values, requiring successful status and REML convergence. A complete named vc list/vector can override them; names identify components, and matrix coordinates retain the fitted trait/basis order. Such an override solves the stated fixed model and does not turn a failed REML fit into a successful one.
The handoff reuses prepared records, sparse design and ID mappings. It supports saving/reloading the fit with saveRDS() / readRDS(). Numerical factors are rebuilt for the new solve. Fits therefore retain their analysis data; consider this when sharing saved objects. Supplying a new control replaces the route-specific controls; omitting it inherits the fit’s controls.
Single-trait, multitrait and longitudinal pedigree formulas support the existing PCG and sparse-direct routes. CHOLMOD is the default direct backend. The explicit single-response component route, including correlated channels and grouped/AR(1)/exponential residuals, uses its existing direct solvers. Backend availability depends on the installed build. General gs_model workflows and low-level numerical gsuite_solve() retain their own APIs.
gfit(task = "reml") and gfit(task = "solve") remain available. The compiled route selected by gs_fit_control() is REML-only: greml() can use it, but its fit cannot be handed to gsolve(). This interface change adds no new numerical algorithms or qualification claims. The pedigree tutorial shows the three main data-frame workflows. REML fits already include predictions, so a second solve is optional.



gsolve owns checked column-major matrix views, leading dimensions, caller-owned workspaces, square and rectangular operators, dense/sparse SPD factors, PCG, preconditioners, deterministic probes, SLQ, and numerical diagnostics. Its operator contracts declare symmetry, definiteness, concurrency, and available diagonals. Rectangular operators provide forward/transpose application and bounded column materialization.
greml owns covariance models, fixed-effect projection, likelihood, score, standard average information (AI), optimization, prediction, and uncertainty. gsuite validates explicit R inputs and translates installed public results. Packed genotype operations belong to gbits; resource identity and LD belong to gmat. The optional gbits adapter supplies numerical operators without a reverse dependency from gsolve or greml to genotype libraries.



For single-trait covariance components, \(V = \sum_c \theta_c K_c\) and
\[
P=V^{-1}-V^{-1}F(F^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}F)^{-1}F^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}.
\]








Route
Computation and storage
Practical boundary




Exact dense
Factors observation covariance V; quadratic storage
Small reference models; prepared genomic BED terms are rejected


Matrix-free covariance
PCG applies inverses/projections; common Hutchinson probes estimate traces and SLQ estimates log determinants
Operator and bounded \(O(nk)\) Krylov/probe storage; solver and stochastic precision must both be adequate


Sparse MME
Assembles coefficient-space statistics and uses a retained sparse factor or a qualified coefficient operator
Fill and resource limits matter; backend, trace, inference, and uncertainty support depend on the specific API


Hybrid covariance
Uses structured sparse terms as a state-matched preconditioner for separately declared matrix-free terms
Components enter once; a pedigree plus genomic sum is not automatic single-step GBLUP


Iterative large-p projection
Nested PCG avoids retaining \(V^{-1}F\) and the full fixed-normal matrix; fixed determinant uses SLQ
Selected contrasts may be available while full fixed-effect covariance is unavailable



The low-level gs_model() sparse/hybrid interface is distinct from the specialized pedigree and component-MME interfaces. Its limitations do not apply to all sparse-direct APIs. CHOLMOD selected inversion and PARDISO selected_solve target uncertainty are documented in prediction error. PARDISO selected inversion is unsupported.
Unbalanced multivariate covariance uses the observed principal submatrix of a trait-by-unit covariance: scatter, base-operator application, trait mixing, and gather. Random regression uses supplied basis columns. Neither operation requires a dense production incidence or Kronecker matrix. Selected prediction uncertainty computes only requested target blocks.



Prepared packed BED storage trades preparation work and memory for repeated applications; genomic production routes form no dense GRM. Sparse MME cost depends on coefficient dimension and fill. Matrix-free memory is dominated by operators and bounded Krylov/probe buffers. Nested fixed-effect solves add their own tolerance and determinant-precision requirements.
Independent multiple-RHS PCG solves columns independently. Explicit true block PCG shares a block Krylov recurrence and reports rank compression, deflation, restarts, and each original RHS’s true residual. Its orchestration owns one outer thread. A two-level preconditioner uses a caller-supplied, copied, rank-compressed coarse basis tied to one covariance state; it does not discover a basis automatically. Outer RHS/probe parallelism and operator-local OpenMP must not be nested. Requested and resolved execution are reported separately.
Route selection is API-specific. Low-level model routes are explicit; pedigree direct controls may resolve automatic to an available backend according to their documented policy. An explicit unsupported request does not silently change the statistical route.



The persistent R interface specifies handles, lifetime, ordering, controls, and low-level examples. The formula interface is a separate bounded lowering API. The package qualification limits remain; that page also records the focused constructor naming repair.
Model qualification, qgdata evidence, and the DMU workflow retain scoped numerical evidence and negative outcomes. They do not establish general biobank readiness or universal performance. Build and packaging commands belong in development and binary distribution.

title: Methods
text:
Capability overview
Access: documentation and the seven published R packages are public; the standalone mixed-model application is offered only to licensed users. Development interfaces and public release versions remain distinct. See the distribution policy before treating an implemented capability as an available public download.
The experimental direct SumHer workflow adds gbase::gprep(task = "ldscores") and gcorr::gcorr(Glist, stat, method = "sumher") for single- and multiple-trait analyses. Direct scores are accumulated without saving pairwise LD to disk. SumHer returns h2 per trait and rg for every pair; the previous estimator remains available explicitly.
